title: eulerize incorrectly uses weight='weight' for shortest paths, fails on negative weights
description: fnx.eulerize uses shortest_path_length(G, u, v, weight='weight') and shortest_path(G, u, v, weight='weight') internally. The eulerize algorithm only needs the BFS (hop-count) shortest path between odd-degree nodes — edge weights are irrelevant. nx uses shortest_path(G, source=m, target=n) with no weight kwarg (unweighted BFS). On graphs with negative-weight edges fnx's calls hit Dijkstra's negative-weight rejection and raise ValueError('Contradictory paths found: negative weights?'); nx works fine because BFS doesn't care about weights. Fix: drop weight='weight' from both shortest_path_length and shortest_path calls in eulerize (match nx's behaviour and parity contract).
close_reason: Dropped weight='weight' from shortest_path / shortest_path_length in eulerize; now uses BFS matching nx. 4-shape parity probe matches; 367 tests pass.

title: test: Laplacian spectral invariants (L=D-A, zero-multiplicity=components, eigsum=2E)
description: Spectral graph theory cross-checks: L=D-A, row sums 0, trace=2|E|, smallest eigenvalue 0, multiplicity-of-0 = number_connected_components, eigsum=2|E|, connected iff lambda2>0, K_n closed-form spectrum (0 once + n^(n-1)). Cross-checks laplacian/adjacency matrices, spectrum, component count. ~84 cases.
close_reason: Predicted class CONFIRMED, with one qualification I want on the record. I picked this bead expecting the permutation-invariant-assertion defect from br-r37-c1-imp6j. Half of that prediction was wrong-headed: a SPECTRUM is permutation-invariant by nature, so the eigenvalue tests cannot see a row-order regression and should not be blamed for it. But the STRUCTURAL test is blind for an avoidable reason - it builds D from A (D = diag(A.sum(axis=1))), so a consistently permuted (L, A) pair still satisfies L = D - A. MUTANT, measured: emitting BOTH laplacian_matrix and adjacency_matrix in sorted-label order instead of g.nodes() order passes every pre-existing assertion in this file - L=D-A, zero row sums, trace=2|E| - and leaves the spectrum bit-identical, since permutation preserves eigenvalues. The new assertion catches it. With labels ['c','a','b'] the L diagonal follows node order [1,1,2] and not sorted order [1,2,1]; the assertion is written against both, so it discriminates rather than passing by luck. ONE-SIDED IFF, measured: the docstring claims 'connected iff lambda_2 > 0' but only the forward direction was asserted, on the 22 connected draws of 40 - the 18 disconnected draws fell through with no spectral check at all. The reverse (disconnected => lambda_2 == 0) holds 18/18 and is now asserted in the else branch, so every draw is now checked rather than 22 of 40. Added: the row-to-node correspondence pinned against the DEGREES (not against A), including the off-diagonal being -1 exactly where an edge exists; nodelist permutation with the diagonal following the new order and the trace and row sums preserved; and the weighted case the docstring never mentions - laplacian_matrix reads the weight attribute by DEFAULT, so trace(L) is 2*sum(weights) (14, not 2|E|=4) while the row sums stay zero, that invariant being structural rather than weight-dependent; weight=None restores the identity. Evidence: file 81 -> 84 passed, no skips (3 new fixed witnesses; the existing sweeps gained assertions and the disconnected branch rather than cases); 222 passed across the Laplacian family (laplacian_spectral_moments, laplacian_spectrum_native, normalized_laplacian_isolated_node_parity, laplacian_spectrum_eigsolver_conformance_guard). title: perf(views): migrate Graph/DiGraph outer G.adj to a native-backed AdjacencyView so __len__ is a C slot — measured ceiling 1.85x vs nx (from 0.806x)
description:
Profile-first step of br-r37-c1-bmrbc is DONE by OliveDesert 2026-08-08. This bead is the implementation, now fully specified and unblocked. ELF 675707ac, balanced-square substrate, dual A/A nulls per ratio (all 0.9989-1.0006), load 7.8 of 64, 500 len() calls per timed unit.

THE CEILING IS MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED — no prototype was needed, because the ceiling already ships. G.nodes and G.edges expose __len__ as a wrapper_descriptor (a C slot) while G.adj's is a plain Python function, on the SAME graph returning the SAME count:

  len(G.adj)  nx vs fnx                      0.8062x CI [0.8050, 0.8067]   nx 69.1 ns / fnx 85.6 ns
  CEILING: nx len(G.adj) vs fnx len(G.nodes) 1.8500x CI [1.8481, 1.8523]   nx 69.1 ns / fnx 37.3 ns
  fnx len(G.adj) vs fnx len(G.nodes)         2.3062x CI [2.3044, 2.3080]   Python frame tax 48.5 ns
  CONTROL: nx len(G.adj) vs nx len(G.nodes)  1.0004x CI [0.9998, 1.0017]

The control is what makes the ceiling legitimate: nx's own two views land within 0.04% of each other, both Python-framed, so len(G.nodes) is the same workload as len(G.adj) on nx's side, and fnx's already-native len(G.nodes) is a fair proxy for what a native adjacency __len__ would cost.

PRIZE: 0.806x -> ~1.85x. A 2.3x improvement that turns a published loss into a win. The whole deficit and the whole prize are the Python __len__ frame (48.5 ns of an 85.6 ns call); the PyO3 call inside it is only 10.5 ns of that.

BLOCKER I EXPECTED AND THEN DISPROVED: I assumed the native AdjacencyView (views.rs:990) was Graph-only, since it holds Py<PyGraph>, which would have forced a Graph-only ship and a class asymmetry across graph types. DiAdjacencyView exists at digraph.rs:16004. Both graph types are covered and no asymmetry is needed.

IMPLEMENTATION PATH. Do NOT swap what G.adj returns wholesale; that is what makes this risky.
  1. Rust: add the subclass (and dict) pyclass attrs to views.rs:989 AdjacencyView and digraph.rs:16004 DiAdjacencyView, plus a new-constructor taking the graph.
  2. Python: define subclasses of BOTH the native class and the existing Python AdjacencyView, i.e. class _NativeAdjacencyView(_fnx.AdjacencyView, AdjacencyView). The MRO puts the native C slots for __len__ and __contains__ ahead of the Python definitions while every other behaviour still comes from the existing Python class.
  3. Use them ONLY at the two outer construction sites, __init__.py:2021 _graph_adj_view and :2033 _digraph_adj_view, the ones that already pass owner=self and native_len=. Filtered, reverse, reconstructed, snapshot and inner-row views keep the pure-Python class and its native_len-is-None fallback untouched.

WHY THE MRO ROUTE RATHER THAN RETURNING THE NATIVE VIEW DIRECTLY: inheriting preserves _fnx_atlas_cache (br-r37-c1-spg9n), the native-iter binding, keys/items/values, __eq__, copy and pickling (_reconstruct_adjacency_view at __init__.py:1974) with zero reimplementation. Returning the native view directly would require reimplementing all of it.

SEMANTICS THAT MUST HOLD (verified for __len__, must be re-verified for __contains__):
  * The native AdjacencyView __len__ returns g.inner.node_count(). _GRAPH_ADJ_NATIVE_LEN is Graph.number_of_nodes captured at __init__.py:2000, BEFORE the private-aware wrappers are installed at :45328, so it is the RAW native count. The two agree.
  * Proof they must agree, and that len(owner) does NOT: on a 3-node fnx.Graph with G._node assigned a 5-node dict, len(G) == 5 and G.number_of_nodes() == 5, but native_len() == 3 and len(G.adj) == 3. nx agrees with 3 because its AdjacencyView is built over _adj, not _node. The len(owner) shortcut is refuted in br-r37-c1-bmrbc and must not be re-proposed.
  * The native __contains__ (views.rs:1004) still uses node_key_to_string (heap String) rather than the borrowed with_node_key_str from br-r37-c1-oe93x. Fix that in the same commit only if measured, otherwise the migration could regress n in G.adj.

VERIFY: full Python suite (baseline on ELF 675707ac is 50678 passed / 1081 skipped, plus the one pre-existing br-r37-c1-vniyv coverage-doc failure), then a before/after on the balanced-square substrate including negative controls that cannot reach the change.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED by OliveDesert 2026-08-08. The migration WORKS and hits the predicted ceiling mechanism, but it leaks memory as specified, and the fix is bigger than this bead's spec said. Everything below is tested, not predicted.

WHAT WORKED. The MRO route is sound and needs no redesign:
  * Rust: added subclass + dict pyclass attrs and a new-constructor taking the graph to views.rs AdjacencyView and digraph.rs DiAdjacencyView. cargo check clean.
  * Python: _native_len_adjacency_view(native_base) building class _NativeLenAdjacencyView(native_base, AdjacencyView), used at the two outer construction sites only.
  * VERIFIED on both Graph and DiGraph: type(G.adj).__len__ became a wrapper_descriptor (the C slot), MRO = [AdjacencyView, AdjacencyView/DiAdjacencyView, AdjacencyView, Mapping, Collection], and len/contains/getitem/iter/repr/bool/copy all returned correct values with __getitem__ still returning the parity AtlasView.
  * Explicitly binding __getitem__, __iter__, __repr__, __str__ back to AdjacencyView's and __contains__ back to Mapping's is REQUIRED and works — without it the native base wins those too and you lose _fnx_atlas_cache, the native-iter binding and the nx-style repr.

WHY IT WAS REVERTED — AN UNCOLLECTABLE REFERENCE CYCLE. Once the Python view subclasses the native one, G.adj is cached ON the graph while the native base holds a Py<PyGraph> pointing back AT it. That Rust field is invisible to CPython's cyclic GC, so the graph pins itself forever through its own adjacency view. Full suite: 50674 passed, 4 NEW failures (plus the pre-existing vniyv coverage-doc one):
  test_view_descriptor_parity.py::test_cached_accessor_owner_cycle_is_collectable[Graph-adj]
  test_view_descriptor_parity.py::test_cached_accessor_owner_cycle_is_collectable[DiGraph-adj]
  test_view_descriptor_parity.py::test_direct_edge_attribute_self_reference_is_stored_and_collectable[Graph]
  test_view_descriptor_parity.py::test_direct_edge_attribute_self_reference_is_stored_and_collectable[DiGraph]
Failure mode: `assert reference() is None` -> `Graph(nodes=4, edges=5) is not None`. The existing tests caught it immediately; they are a good gate and must stay.

__traverse__ ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — I TRIED IT. Added fn __traverse__ visiting self.graph to both native views, rebuilt, and all four tests still failed identically. Traverse lets the collector SEE the cycle; breaking it also needs tp_clear on a member of the cycle, and PyO3 only emits tp_clear when the class implements __clear__.

THE REAL REMAINING WORK, which is why this is not a one-lever change: __clear__ must be able to null the handle, so `graph: Py<PyGraph>` has to become `Option<Py<PyGraph>>` in BOTH native views, and every method that reads self.graph must handle the cleared state — __len__, __contains__, __getitem__, __iter__, __repr__, __bool__ in views.rs AdjacencyView, the same set in digraph.rs DiAdjacencyView, plus new_adjacency_view and the DiGraph constructor. __len__ returns usize and __bool__ returns bool, so a cleared view needs a defined answer (0 / false) rather than a panic. Budget it as a real change with its own review, not an afternoon.

SEQUENCING ADVICE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: land the Option + __traverse__ + __clear__ GC work on the two native views FIRST, as its own commit, verified by the four tests above with the views still unsubclassed (they pass today, so that commit must keep them passing). Only then add the subclass/dict attrs and the Python MRO wiring as a second commit. Doing both at once is what made this attempt unlandable.

STILL TRUE AND STILL WORTH IT: the ceiling measurement in br-r37-c1-bmrbc stands unchanged — 0.8062x today against a measured 1.8500x native-slot ceiling, with the entire gap being the 48.5 ns Python __len__ frame. Nothing learned here reduces the prize; it only prices the work correctly.

title: MST + EdgeDataView perf: 250x+ speedups from removing O(N) hot-path scans
description:
Two real perf bugs uncovered while perf-probing fnx vs nx:

(1) minimum_spanning_tree (br-r37-c1-mstsync): public API routed any graph with a weight attribute through an fnx->nx->fnx parity detour because the Rust MST kernel read stale weights after post-construction g[u][v]['weight']=w mutation. The _sync_rust_edge_attrs helper (br-r37-c1-sjf4t) exists to push Python-visible dicts back into Rust storage — but the MST wrapper never called it. Wire it up and skip the nx detour: 1293ms -> 5ms on a 200-node Watts-Strogatz (~250x speedup). MultiGraph still routes through nx (to preserve type), NaN-weight routes through nx (to preserve ValueError contract).

(2) _FailFastEdgeIterator (br-r37-c1-edgesdataperf): __next__ did  +  (O(N) tuple-build + O(N) compare) on EVERY edge. For a 200-node 1000-edge graph this turned  into a 1.4s op. Replace per-next tuple walk with O(1) length probes — matches nx's contract (dict raises on size-change, not on key-permutation) without the quadratic overhead. 1422ms -> 2.67ms (530x speedup) on the same graph; cascades through every algorithm that touches edges(data=True).

Combined: all 17506 Python tests pass; 293 spanning-tree tests pass.
notes: Fixed in same commit that filed this bead. MST: skip nx detour for non-MultiGraph non-NaN cases, sync edge attrs first. EdgeIterator: replace per-next O(N) tuple compare with O(1) length check.

LEVERS (all need shared/contended substrate work + coordination, agent mail down): (a) extend node-set fast path to edge-filtered views by intersecting visible_keep with the filter_edge membership set; (b) precompute the visible-node set once per _edges walk and use O(1) set membership instead of per-neighbor _node_visible; (c) reorder _node_visible to test _filter_node first to short-circuit filtered-out neighbors before the slow contains (safe only if filter_node is a pure predicate over possibly-absent nodes); (d) speed Graph.__contains__ itself (hottest shared method). Note dict(adjacency()) 0.55x and adjacency_data 0.76x are PyDict-allocation substrate floors (native kernel already used; Rust not faster than CPython at building O(V+E) dicts).

So the gap is the foundational CONSTRUCTION tax in PyGraph::add_edges_from -> add_edge (crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs): per edge it does 2x node_key_to_string + ~5 String clones of the node names across node_key_map/node_py_attrs/inner/edge_key/remember_edge_key + 2-3 PyDict allocs + MultiGraph edge-key machinery (PyGraph is MultiGraph-backed). raw add_edges_from(20k edges)=64ms. TRIED + REVERTED (proven zero-change, golden 911ebb2b bit-identical to nx 7 cases incl mutation/independence): eliminating the per-edge 'merged' PyDict in add_edges_from for plain/key edges -- before 64.1ms after 64.9ms, no effect (merged was negligible vs add_edge). REAL FIX = a bulk add_edges_from fast-path (plain 2-tuples, no data) that resolves node keys once and batches inner+Python-map population, bypassing per-edge add_edge overhead -- larger/riskier effort (must preserve multigraph key assignment + isomorphism). Deferring as a bulk-construction rewrite. grid_2d (6.78x, biggest) additionally pays repr() per tuple node in node_key_to_string.

title: [bug] DiGraph.to_undirected diverges from nx on reciprocal-edge attrs (32/60)
description: The Python-visible DiGraph.to_undirected (binding: fnx-python/src/digraph.rs ~3563, TealSpring-locked) merges reciprocal directed edges a<->b with the WRONG winner: 32/60 random DiGraphs (with differing edge weights) diverge from networkx on the merged undirected edge's attrs, + 8/60 on edge order. nx iterates G.edges()=node->successor order and the LATTER direction's attrs win; the fnx binding iterates in a different (edges-map/insertion) order. FIX: iterate edges in node->successor (edges_ordered) order, like nx. The SUBSTRATE DiGraph::to_undirected was already canonicalised in 6c721e942 (so substrate is correct); the binding needs the same. Repro: a=DiGraph; a.add_edge(0,1,weight=1); a.add_edge(1,0,weight=2); a.to_undirected()[0][1]['weight'] should match nx. Probe reciprocal edges with differing attrs +/- a remove_node.
close_reason: Fixed cbffefac7: PyDiGraph::to_undirected now iterates inner.edges_ordered() (node->successor order, deterministic) and merges reciprocal a<->b with nx's latter-wins dict.update (was: edge_py_attrs HashMap order + first-wins -> random/seed-dependent winner, up to 32/60 divergence after remove_node). 200-case randomized differential vs nx (reciprocal+extra-keys+removes) 0 mismatches, deterministic, golden 39a131ad, full suite 21281 passed.

title: fix(astar): respect edge direction on DiGraphs + match nx FIFO tie-break
description: Two A* defects: (1) DIRECTION: the Rust _raw_astar_path kernel is undirected-only (astar_path(graph: &Graph)) and the PyO3 binding fed it gr.undirected() even for DiGraph/MultiDiGraph, so astar_path/astar_path_length silently ignored edge direction and returned paths over non-existent reverse edges (e.g. [0,4] when only 4->0 exists; nx returns the correct long route). dijkstra/bellman_ford honour direction. (2) TIE-BREAK: among equal f-scores the kernel broke ties on node identity, but nx uses FIFO insertion-counter (next(c)); on unit-weight grids astar_path returned a different valid shortest path than nx. Fix: directed graphs delegate to nx (no native directed astar kernel yet); undirected Rust kernel now carries a monotonic counter for FIFO tie-break. Found via weighted shortest-path tie-break probe.
close_reason: Fixed both: directed graphs delegate to nx (kernel was undirected-only, dropped direction -> invalid paths); undirected Rust kernel now uses FIFO insertion-counter tie-break matching nx. 0 mismatches vs nx (directed+undirected); 68 astar tests pass; clippy clean. Regression test added (8 cases). Follow-up: native directed A* kernel.

title: nested subgraph edges() yields divergent node-iteration order vs nx (orientation flips)
description: PRE-EXISTING (present on HEAD before br-r37-c1-kum9v fix; 14/80 exact-order + 6/80 even-sorted-orientation divergences on G.subgraph(outer).subgraph(inner).edges()). Undirected nested subgraph edges yield (u,v) with source picked by a node-iteration order that differs from nx for some nested cases -> orientation flips (fnx ('13','7') vs nx ('7','13')). Single-level subgraph edges are fine; only NESTED (subgraph-of-subgraph) diverges. Likely the nested _nbunch/node-order resolution. NOT a perf issue — pure ordering parity. Repro: build random Graph, subgraph(outer).subgraph(inner), compare list(.edges()).
close_reason: FIXED. Root cause: nx COMPOSES a subgraph-of-subgraph onto the ORIGINAL graph (nested view._graph IS the root), so node iteration uses root length for the node_ok_shorter threshold (2*len(keep)<len(root)) and yields keep-set order. fnx CHAINED (._graph = outer VIEW, length=outer) -> took the other branch -> outer-filtered node order -> divergent edge orientation. Fix: _subgraph_with_view collapses a pure node-set/default-edge-filter chain onto its concrete root (filt already only holds nodes visible up the whole chain). Nested node-order/edge/degree bit-exact 0/4000 (all 4 classes, self-loops, keys/data) + 0/1000 quadruple-nesting; edge_subgraph-then-subgraph (non-default edge filter) correctly does NOT compose; full pytest 22104. BONUS: composing to root lets the native-row fast paths fire on nested subgraphs too.

title: perf(lookup): has_node 0.4955x is now SLOWER than its own dunder 'n in G' 0.8053x — the ordering INVERTED after padm6
description:
Measured by OliveDesert 2026-08-08 on HEAD, quiet host (1-min load 1.87 of 64), balanced-square same-invocation substrate with dual A/A nulls, ELF bench_elf_sha256=80488d1e0014e4ca2907f8166df60fdf15a9de6eab6bd11685d260917fc7041d. All four rows DECIDABLE with null half-widths 0.0013-0.0028:

  G.has_node(present) x512   0.4955x  CI95 [0.4948, 0.4964]  nulls 1.0007/1.0005
  G.has_node(missing) x512   0.6085x  CI95 [0.6081, 0.6101]  nulls 0.9994/0.9994
  n in G (present)    x512   0.8053x  CI95 [0.8027, 0.8067]  nulls 1.0020/1.0013
  len(G.adj)          x500   0.7993x  CI95 [0.7986, 0.8000]  nulls 0.9983/0.9999

TWO FINDINGS.

(1) THE PROJECT-ORDERS NUMBERS ARE REAL, NOT STALE. The orders named has_node 0.52x and len(G.adj) 0.79x. On HEAD they are 0.4955x and 0.7993x. len(G.adj) reproduces to two decimals; has_node is if anything slightly WORSE than published. Anyone about to apply the usual 'named losses are stale, re-measure first' heuristic here should stop — these two are not stale.

(2) THE ORDERING INVERTED, AND THAT IS THE LEVER. The recorded history was 'n in G' 0.27x vs has_node 0.64x — the dunder was the laggard, because a dunder cannot use the per-instance method-shadow escape that has_node uses. br-r37-c1-padm6 fixed the dunder by moving the private-override probe into native __contains__. It is now the reverse: the dunder is 0.8053x and the METHOD is 0.4955x. has_node is now ~1.6x slower than the identical logical operation reached through 'in'.

That is not a canonicalization claim and is NOT what the CloudyTurtle 2026-07-26 node-key-interning HOLD fences (that predicate demands >=30% self-time attributed to node_key_to_string before interning may be reopened). This is narrower and checkable: two entry points to the same membership test now have a 1.6x spread, so one of them is carrying overhead the other has already shed. Read what native path __contains__ takes after padm6 and why has_node does not take it.

BEWARE the trap padm6 itself documented: has_node must keep supporting the per-instance method shadow, and __contains__ must keep working without it. Any unification has to preserve BOTH, plus copy/deepcopy/pickle/subclass behaviour and the eager hash() exception on unhashable keys.

RE-DECIDE on the same substrate; do not publish from a bare-tuple rebuild (see br-r37-c1-qqj23).
close_reason:
SHIPPED AS MAINTENANCE, TARGET STILL A LOSS. G.has_node(present) 0.5178x -> 0.6937x.

FIRST: THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE WAS WRONG, and I filed it. I claimed has_node pays a Python wrapper (_private_aware_has_node -> _private_override -> raw native) that __contains__ sheds natively. FALSE. grep -n '_private_aware_has_node' returns exactly ONE hit — its own def at __init__.py:44976. It is never called. Graph.has_node is <method 'has_node' of 'franken_networkx.Graph' objects>, the raw native method; line 45328 assigns the natively-captured method back, a no-op restore. The ordered lever 'route has_node through the direct backend fast path' was ALREADY in place. I read a wrapper definition and never proved it was installed — the pyo3_wrapper_can_itself_be_dead trap.

PROFILE (the native has_node has an identity-int path that returns BEFORE canonicalization, so key type splits the cost without a profiler; net of an empty-loop floor, 512 probes/call):
  nx  has_node int  37.6 ns/probe
  fnx has_node int  41.2 ns/probe   -> only 3.6 ns behind; PyO3 call overhead is NOT the problem
  nx  has_node str  40.4 ns/probe
  fnx has_node str  90.6 ns/probe   -> 50.2 ns behind
  fnx str-vs-int delta 49.4 ns = 54.5% of the call (nx's own delta: 2.7 ns)

REAL CAUSE: write_canonical_str_key built the canonical with write!(cursor, "str:{}:{s}", s.len()) through std::io::Write. The form is a fixed ASCII prefix + decimal length + colon + raw bytes, so core::fmt's per-argument dynamic dispatch WAS the whole cost of what is two copy_from_slice calls and a 1-3 digit decimal. Replaced with direct byte writes. Byte-identical output — swept by a new test across every length either side of the 128-byte boundary, multi-byte input, digit-width transitions, embedded NULs, and keys that already look canonical.

MEASURED (balanced ABBA square, 41 rounds, taskset -c 40-47, live nx 3.6.1 in-invocation, load 5.4->4.2; before ELF 80488d1e, after ELF 675707ac, identical Python sources). Every row measured is reported:
  G.has_node(present) str  0.5178x -> 0.6937x
  G.has_node(missing) str  0.6071x -> 0.8696x
  n in G (present)    str  0.7840x -> 1.1129x   <- crosses to a win
  G.has_edge(u,v)     str  0.4340x -> 0.6502x
  G.degree(n)         str  0.4222x -> 0.4247x   (unchanged)
  CONTROL has_node(int)    0.9192x -> 0.9448x
  CONTROL len(G.adj)       0.7899x -> 0.7987x
All 14 DECIDABLE; every null median 0.9977-1.0015, CI half-widths 0.0014-0.0050.

THE CONTROLS ARE THE POINT: a before/after spans two invocations and carries across-run drift the within-run nulls do not cover. has_node(int) never reaches the edited function and len(G.adj) touches no node key; they moved +2.8% and +1.1%, which IS the measured drift floor. degree moved +0.6%, inside it, so no claim for degree. The four string rows moved +34/+43/+42/+50%.

DISCARDED RUN, disclosed: an earlier before/after at load 22.3 widened the nulls to a 0.0553 half-width and returned NOT DECIDABLE for has_node(present). Thrown away, not published.

TESTS: full Python suite on the new ELF 50678 passed / 1081 skipped / 1 xpassed, plus one PRE-EXISTING failure already filed as br-r37-c1-vniyv (coverage.md 178 vs 175, RED on main independent of in-flight work) — NOT regenerated here. clippy -D warnings clean, cargo test -p fnx-python --lib 77 passed, cargo fmt clean.

NOT A CAMPAIGN RESULT: has_node is still 0.6937x. The n in G crossover to 1.1129x is real and recorded, but is not banked as campaign output from this row; it needs its own row and preflight.

DO NOT reopen node-key interning on the 54.5% attribution — that was measured against the OLD core::fmt implementation and is now spent. Re-split the string path by key type on the new ELF first. G.degree(n) at 0.4247x is untouched by this lever and is the larger remaining loss on this surface.

title: [parity] add_node(node, **attr) with attr keyed 'n' raised TypeError (param named 'n' collided) — broke read_graphml/gml/pajek for graphs with an 'n' attr
description: FOUND+FIXED this session. The Rust add_node binding used #[pyo3(signature=(n, **attr))]; an attr dict containing key 'n' (e.g. from _from_nx_graph's add_node(node, **attrs) on a read graph) bound the node positionally to n AND received n=<val> via kwargs -> 'multiple values for argument n'. Broke every readwrite reader (graphml/gml/pajek/...) for graphs carrying a node/edge attr literally named 'n'. Fix: rename the param to nx's public 'node_for_adding' across all 4 classes -> exact nx collision parity (nx only collides on a 'node_for_adding' attr). 18-case cross-impl readwrite probe + 4-class direct collision battery + full pytest 21841.
notes: FIXED+CLOSED candidate: param rename n->node_for_adding across all 4 add_node bindings (lib.rs x2, digraph.rs x2). Exact nx collision parity. Pinned test_add_node_attr_param_collision.py (9 cases). Probe artifacts in 20260607T-add-node-n-collision-cc. title: perf(batch): the keyed shape's edge growth is NOT key-assignment — shared MultiGraph edge cost; my lka35 flag was over-read from one run
description: Follow-up probe of the loose thread flagged when br-r37-c1-lka35 closed.
close_reason:
NO KEYED-SPECIFIC DEFECT — MEASURED, NO EDIT MADE, AND THIS CORRECTS MY OWN FLAG.

When br-r37-c1-lka35 closed I recorded that the keyed (u,v,key,dict) shape had the steepest EDGE sweep of the nine collectors measured (x1.72), called it a different mechanism from the whole-node-set clone, and said it needed its own probe before anyone touched it. Probed. It is not keyed-specific, and the x1.72 was over-read from a single run.

DISCRIMINATING PROBE: same edge-count sweep run on keyed 4-tuples AND attributed 3-tuples into the same MultiGraph class, nodes fixed at 2000, k=8, load 0.93, ELF daf4d388d215ecab95c3b6fdc5b4f0ecc91e6abe2738ce4c1c77071409c5daf4. If only the keyed arm grew, the cost is key assignment/lookup; if both grow, it is shared multi-edge structure cost.

      E    keyed 4-tuple       attributed 3-tuple    keyed/attr
   1000     3860.4 ns x1.00      2758.4 ns x1.00        1.40
   4000     3164.8 ns x0.82      2764.0 ns x1.00        1.15
  16000     4941.2 ns x1.28      3495.7 ns x1.27        1.41
  32000     6034.0 ns x1.56      4996.3 ns x1.81        1.21

BOTH ARMS GROW TOGETHER, and at E=32000 the ATTRIBUTED arm grew MORE (x1.81) than the keyed one (x1.56). The keyed/attr ratio stays flat across two orders of magnitude of edge count (1.40, 1.15, 1.41, 1.21) with no divergence, so keyed carries a roughly constant ~1.2-1.4x premium over attributed rather than a growing one.

CONCLUSION: there is no key-assignment mechanism to fix. The edge-count growth is shared MultiGraph multi-edge structure cost, present in both shapes, and the x1.72-vs-x1.24 gap I flagged from single runs of each is inside run-to-run variation — this probe shows the ordering can reverse. My lka35 note over-read one measurement; treat that flag as withdrawn.

DO NOT chase a keyed key-assignment optimization on the strength of the lka35 note. If the shared MultiGraph edge-count growth is ever worth attacking it is a separate question about the multi-edge structure itself, affects both shapes equally, and needs its own bead and its own attribution — none of which this probe provides.

Script: scratchpad/keyed_edge_growth.py.

title: rch does not intercept 'maturin'; rch exec -- maturin build fails open to a LOCAL build (AGENTS.md prescribes it)

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: FIXED in 56d01b4f2. The claim is confirmed by RCH's own diagnostic, not by inference or by watching for a stray target/ tree.

    $ rch diagnose -- maturin build --release --features pyo3/abi3-py310
        Kind: none
        Confidence: 0.00 (no compilation keyword)
        Decision: WOULD NOT INTERCEPT
        Reason: Command not classified as compilation

    $ rch diagnose -- cargo build --release
        Kind: CargoBuild
        Confidence: 0.95 (cargo build)
        Decision: WOULD INTERCEPT

    $ rch diagnose -- rch exec -- maturin develop --features pyo3/abi3-py310
        Kind: none / 0.00 / WOULD NOT INTERCEPT

So the exact form AGENTS.md prescribed classifies as a non-compilation command. RCH offloads by
compilation KEYWORD; maturin is not one, and the 'rch exec --' prefix does not change the
classification.

AGENTS.md now says so plainly, replaces the misleading line with the local wheel build the
benchmarks actually consume (env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR maturin build --release ...), and records the
two consequences that bite in practice:
  1. A maturin build competes for LOCAL CPU. That is not academic - it is more than enough load to
     trip perf_harness.py's host-wide exclusivity gate and abort an in-flight measurement. I hit
     exactly this earlier in the session.

title: perf(classes): incremental add_edge 0.2469x vs nx — per-mutation CGSE decision-record allocation
description:
RE-MEASURED ON HEAD (2026-08-04, CoralIsland, maturin .so sha256 e3fe742c366f7c9a88550708ea6779336e0118d394c45e6d307274677b007d8d, taskset -c 40-43, 21 interleaved rounds, A/A null 1.0021x):

  nx Graph.add_edge          661.0 ns/edge
  fnx Graph.add_edge (public) 2079.1 ns/edge -> 0.2469x vs nx
  fnx Graph.add_edge (raw, no Python shim) 1692.9 ns/edge -> 0.2983x vs nx
  bare PyO3 call floor         34.1 ns
  fnx has_node                 95.0 ns
  fnx add_node (raw)          819.3 ns vs nx 335.3 ns

So the Python None/hash shim is only a 1.13x tax; the NATIVE path is already 2.6x slower than
nx's pure-Python dict work. Prime suspect: Graph::add_edge_with_attrs calls record_decision
TWICE per edge, and each DecisionRecord heap-allocates operation/rationale/EvidenceTerm
signal+observed_value Strings from &'static str plus a unix_time_ms() clock read, then pushes
into an unbounded Vec. add_node records once (819ns vs nx 335ns fits the same shape).

Lever: make the record cheap WITHOUT changing what is recorded (Cow<'static, str> for the
static operation/rationale/signal/observed_value fields; serde-transparent). Measure the ledger
cost with a committed #[ignore]d paired A/B first; report a negative-evidence entry if the
ledger is not the dominant term.
close_reason: Landed 5017ed857: EvidenceLedger residency bounded, 1.3004x on the isolated same-invocation ledger arm (46.7% -> 21.3% of add_edge_with_attrs), 4 new tests. vs-nx add_edge ratio NOT decidably moved — reported as a loss, follow-up filed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
EVIDENCE (CoralIsland, 2026-08-04), landed in 5017ed857.

ATTRIBUTION — crates/fnx-classes ledger_record_cost_ab, one invocation, 21 interleaved rounds,
n=20,000 edges, release, rch worker hz2:
  A0 unbounded ledger (incumbent) : 782.3 ns/edge   (2 records/edge)
  B  build evidence terms only    :  96.8 ns/edge
  C  terms + unix_time_ms         : 156.3 ns/edge
  D  terms + clock + DecisionRecord: 169.4 ns/edge
  add_edge_with_attrs total       : 1676.1 ns/edge
  -> clock                         :  59.5 ns/edge
  -> static-str clones             :  13.2 ns/edge
  -> ledger push + retention       : 612.9 ns/edge  == 46.7% of add_edge_with_attrs
The cost was RETENTION, not materialisation: the records and the 5 heap strings each hangs onto
were kept for the graph's whole life, so every build faulted in fresh pages proportional to its
mutation count.

LEVER EFFECT — same test after the bound, same invocation, rch worker ovh-a:
  A0 unbounded (incumbent) vs A bounded: 1.3004x   (527.0 -> 353.5 ns/edge of retention)
  ledger share of add_edge_with_attrs : 46.7% -> 21.3%

1a70c0cf03c0349b597a1a48be8eff51cce2535b6df87cb6a94bc573a58371d6:

  after  (load 27)  : 0.3701 / 0.4112 / 0.4208x no-attrs, 0.2832 / 0.3001 / 0.2921x weight,

graph (a 1M-edge build retained 2M DecisionRecords, each holding 5 heap strings). It is now capped
at 8192 resident records; FullValidate/FailClosed decisions are never retired, so the audit
contract the security doctrine names is strengthened, not weakened, and total_recorded() keeps the

title: fix(current_flow): closeness/information/edge-betweenness return dict keys in a different order than networkx
description:
Found on 55f8245b7 while verifying br-r37-c1-nhbni. Values agree to 1e-9; only the dict KEY ORDER diverges, which this project treats as observable contract (see the relabeling/key-order bead family).

EXECUTED, fresh graphs per call, Graph([(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0),(0,2)]):

  current_flow_closeness_centrality        nx [0, 1, 2, 3]   fnx [1, 2, 0, 3]   values MATCH
  information_centrality  (nx alias)       nx [0, 1, 2, 3]   fnx [1, 2, 0, 3]   values MATCH
  edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality nx [(1,0),(0,3),(2,0),(1,2),(2,3)]
                                           fnx [(1,2),(1,0),(2,0),(2,3),(0,3)]  values MATCH

CONTROL - the sibling that is FINE, so this is not a blanket family problem and the fix should not
be applied blindly across the module:
  current_flow_betweenness_centrality       key order MATCHES nx

NOT AN INPUT ARTIFACT: both graphs report identical node iteration order [0,1,2,3] and identical
edge order [(0,1),(0,3),(0,2),(1,2),(2,3)]. DETERMINISTIC: fnx returns [1,2,0,3] on three repeats
with a fresh graph each time, so it is a stable ordering rule, not nondeterminism.

LIKELY CAUSE (unverified, for whoever takes it): these kernels build results from an internal
solver/index ordering (Laplacian row order or a reverse Cuthill-McKee-style permutation) and emit in
that order, where nx emits in G-node order. Same class as the harmonic_centrality ordering noted in
br-r37-c1-8otik - EXCEPT that there nx does not preserve order either, so fnx matching nx was the
contract. Here nx IS in node order and fnx is not, so this one is a real divergence.

SEPARATE, do not conflate: approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality differs in VALUES, not
just order - it is the approximate/sampled variant and was probably called unseeded. Needs its own
look before anyone calls it a bug.
close_reason: All three functions fixed: current_flow_closeness_centrality and information_centrality in a6eadfa30 (result was keyed in RCM rank order instead of G's node order), and edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality in 2ea337143 (the DEFAULT solver='full' took a Rust fast path that emitted a non-nx edge order, while lu/cg were already correct). Verified across 3 solvers x normalized True/False and 5 graph shapes including string labels; 18 tests added, 177 pass in the broader current_flow selection. Values were never affected — key order only.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: 2 of the 3 FIXED in a6eadfa30; the third has a different root cause and stays open here.

FIXED: current_flow_closeness_centrality and its alias information_centrality now key on G's node
order. before nx [0,1,2,3] / fnx [1,2,0,3]; after both [0,1,2,3], values unchanged.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed against nx's source, not guessed): both implementations permute into RCM order
for the Laplacian solve. nx keys its accumulator off the RELABELED graph, dict.fromkeys(H), whose
node order is [mapping[v] for v in G] - so ordering[node] maps each key straight back to G's order.
fnx returned {ordering[i]: ... for i in range(n)}, i.e. RCM RANK order. Fixed by indexing
centrality_arr by rank and iterating G, on the Python path, plus a dict rebuild in G order after the
Rust fast path.

The Rust kernel is deliberately NOT touched: target/release/lib_fnx.so is the exact ELF the
br-r37-c1-oe93x measurement queue is running against right now, and rebuilding it mid-queue would
invalidate those arms. The Python-side rebuild is O(n) against an O(n^3)-ish solve, so it is not a
perf concern; a kernel-side fix can supersede it later at no behavioural cost.

STILL OPEN - edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality. It diverges on BOTH the Rust path and the
solver='full' Python path, so it is not the Rust kernel. THE OBVIOUS HYPOTHESIS IS WRONG, recorded so
the next person does not re-derive it: I checked whether fnx's relabeled graph iterates edges
differently, and it does NOT -
    rcm ordering   nx [1,2,0,3]                              == fnx [1,2,0,3]
    H node order   nx [2,0,1,3]                              == fnx [2,0,1,3]
    H edge order   nx [(2,0),(2,3),(2,1),(0,1),(1,3)]        == fnx identical
yet the final dicts differ: nx [(1,0),(0,3),(2,0),(1,2),(2,3)] vs fnx [(1,2),(1,0),(2,0),(2,3),(0,3)].
So the divergence is introduced after the relabel, somewhere between _flow_matrix_row and the final
comprehension. Values match to 1e-9 throughout.

ALSO SEPARATE, do not conflate: approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality differs in VALUES.
It is the sampled variant and was called unseeded, so that is probably expected - needs its own look.

TESTS: tests/python/test_current_flow_key_order_parity.py, 7 passed. The fixture is chosen so RCM is
a NON-identity permutation and carries a guard asserting that stays true - on a graph where RCM is
the identity the bug is invisible and the whole file would prove nothing. Covers both spellings,
plain-float value types, string-labelled nodes, and pins current_flow_betweenness_centrality (already
correct) as a control. 166 passed across the broader current_flow selection.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: edge variant FIXED in 2ea337143; all three reported functions now match nx.

LOCALISED by parametrizing the solver instead of assuming a shared cause:
    solver=full  (DEFAULT)  order DIVERGED   <- takes the Rust fast path
    solver=lu               order MATCHED    <- Python path
    solver=cg               order MATCHED    <- Python path
So the Python implementation was always correct and the kernel named
edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_nx_ordered_rust was not. Because 'full' is the DEFAULT
argument, every default call was affected - the widest-blast-radius of the three.

My earlier relabel hypothesis was WRONG and stays recorded so nobody re-derives it: the relabelled
graph's edge order is identical on both sides.

FIX: reorder in the wrapper, O(E), no relabel_nodes copy. nx's key sequence is G's edge order with
each pair oriented by RCM rank (lower rank first). I verified that rule reproduces nx's EXACT
sequence on path, star, complete, barbell, chorded-cycle and string-labelled fixtures BEFORE writing
the fix, rather than fitting it to one graph afterwards.

The Rust kernel is deliberately not rebuilt: target/release/lib_fnx.so is the ELF the br-r37-c1-oe93x
queue is measuring right now, and swapping it mid-queue would put some arms on one binary and some on
another. A kernel-side fix can supersede this wrapper reorder later at no behavioural cost - worth
doing, since the kernel's own name says it should already be nx-ordered.

FULL MATRIX VERIFIED: 3 solvers x normalized True/False = 6 combinations, key order AND values match
live nx 3.6.1 in every one.

TESTS: 18 passed in tests/python/test_current_flow_key_order_parity.py (was 7), including a
5-shape sweep because different shapes give different RCM orderings and one fixture is not enough.
177 passed across the broader current_flow selection. ubs 0 critical 0 warning.

RESIDUAL, still not a bug as far as I know: approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality differs
in VALUES, but it is the sampled variant and was called unseeded. Left alone deliberately.

comments.text:
ProudBasin: the two earlier BLOCKER comments were right that the suite already exempts harmonic key-order — but neither verified that the EXEMPTION is correct, and the exemption left a hole. Both handled in f4b823ce8.

THE EXEMPTION IS CORRECT (executed, 5-node graph, relabel 0..4 -> e,d,c,b,a):
    nx  harmonic_centrality keys after relabel : ['d','b','c','a','e']
    order if it were preserved                 : ['e','d','c','b','a']
    fnx keys after relabel                     : ['d','b','c','a','e']
networkx does NOT preserve harmonic key order under relabeling, so the original strict assertion
demanded more of fnx than the oracle does. fnx's key order and values are identical to nx's. This
matters because relaxing an assertion without oracle evidence is gate-weakening; with this evidence
it is a gate CORRECTION.

CORRECTLY SCOPED, not blanket: degree_centrality and closeness_centrality both preserve relabelled
key order on nx AND fnx, so they keep the strict assertion. Only harmonic is exempt.

THE HOLE THE EXEMPTION LEFT: 'we do not assert an order' is not 'our order is right'. With harmonic
skipped, fnx could drift to some third order and every assertion in the file would stay green.
Added test_harmonic_centrality_key_order_matches_networkx_after_relabeling, which pins the exempted
order to the oracle directly (same graph, same mapping, both sides, exact key sequence + values)

description: Sweeps 11 directed predicates (strong/weak connectivity, SCC/WCC counts, aperiodic, DAG, reciprocity, in/out degree, transitivity, pagerank) x 7 directed degenerate shapes (empty/single/self-loop/one-arc/2-cycle/3-cycle/path/cycle+loop) + multigraph & multidigraph parallel-edge/self-loop parity. value+exception-type parity. close_reason: THE BEAD NAMES "multigraph & multidigraph parallel-edge/self-loop parity" AND THAT HALF WAS TWO FIXED DEGREE CHECKS. The predicate sweep - 11 directed predicates over 8 degenerate shapes, compared on FULL OUTCOME (value or exception type), which is the right shape and I left it alone - runs on DiGraph only. Multigraph coverage in the file was test_multigraph_parallel_edges_and_self_loops and test_multidigraph_parallel_arcs, both comparing degree dicts and edge counts, plus some targeted strongly-connected cases. So no multigraph ever reached the eleven predicates. THE EXCEPTION HALF IS WHERE THE VALUE IS: 14 of the 77 combinations RAISE, and all 14 agree with nx on the exception TYPE. transitivity hits its not-implemented guard on every multigraph shape; is_aperiodic errors on parallel arcs and on a disconnected graph; is_strongly_connected, is_weakly_connected and is_aperiodic raise NetworkXPointlessConcept on the empty graph; overall_reciprocity raises NetworkXError on empty and on a single node. A pure value-parity sweep would have missed all of that. I added a guard requiring at least 8 of the combinations to keep raising, because an all-ok matrix would silently reduce the sweep to comparing numbers - the same vacuity protection I have used on the planarity and matching beads. ONE MISSING SHAPE in the pre-existing directed sweep: every one of its 8 shapes is a single component or empty, so no predicate that has to look PAST the first component was ever exercised. title: fix(private storage): G.copy() rebuilds from native storage where nx rebuilds from the assigned _node
description:
Split out of br-r37-c1-s8obc (fixed in this session) rather than folded into it — different mechanism, different path, and s8obc's own repro did not cover it.

s8obc fixed the COPY PROTOCOL: copy.copy / copy.deepcopy / pickle now carry an assigned private store exactly as networkx's default __dict__ copy does. G.copy() is not part of that protocol — it is networkx's own method, which rebuilds a graph by reading self._node and self.adj.

EXECUTED on Graph() with add_node('native') then g._node = {'private': {'tag': 1}}:
    nx  G.copy()  -> private=True,  native=False, len=1   (rebuilt from the assigned mapping)
    fnx G.copy()  -> private=False, native=True,  len=1   (rebuilt from native storage)
    nx  copy.copy -> private=True,  native=False, len=1
    fnx copy.copy -> private=True,  native=False, len=1   <- now matches, via s8obc

So the remaining gap is exactly one path. nx's Graph.copy() does add_nodes_from((n, d.copy()) for n, d in self._node.items()), so the assigned mapping IS the source of truth for it.

CURRENTLY PINNED, deliberately: tests/python/test_view_descriptor_parity.py::test_native_contains_switches_to_private_node_mapping_and_resets_on_copies asserts fnx's current G.copy() behaviour with a comment naming this bead. Whoever fixes this must flip those three lines to nx parity in the same commit — do not leave the pin claiming a contract that has changed.

WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether G.copy() should read the override at all, or whether the override should feed the native store on assignment. The second would fix this path and any other rebuild-from-_node path at once, but it is a much larger behavioural change than s8obc's, so measure the blast radius before choosing.
close_reason: Fixed in 85fcfa92d: G.copy() now rebuilds from an assigned _node exactly as nx does, on all four graph classes — nodes from the override unioned with endpoints reachable through _adj ('a','b' return, 'native' does not). One guard: skip the native fast path when _captured_private_overrides is non-empty. Only possible after br-r37-c1-ka7fd made the edge view read the adjacency; before that the generic rebuild raised KeyError, which is why this was filed blocked. Ordinary graphs still take the native clone with node and edge order identical to nx and a 2000-edge copy at 4.74x nx. The pinned assertion in test_native_contains_switches_..._resets_on_copies was flipped to nx parity in the same commit, as this bead's own text required. 10320 passed in the copy|private|view|edge|adj|subgraph selection.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: BLOCKED on br-r37-c1-ka7fd (dependency recorded). Investigated to the point of knowing exactly what the fix is and why it cannot land yet.

WHAT NX ACTUALLY DOES, measured rather than assumed - Graph() with add_edge('a','b'), add_node('native'), then g._node = {'private': {'tag': 1}}:
    nx  G.copy() -> nodes ['a','b','private'], edges [['a','b']], len 3
    fnx G.copy() -> nodes ['native'],          edges [],          len 1
nx's copy is add_nodes_from(self._node.items()) then add_edges_from(self.edges(data=True)): nodes come
from the assigned override, edges from the still-native _adj, and the two are UNIONED - which is why
'a' and 'b' reappear even though they are absent from the override.

WHERE FNX DIVERGES: _copy_preserving_insertion_order routes exact Graph/DiGraph/MultiGraph/
MultiDiGraph through the native Rust _native_copy(), which rebuilds from native storage and never
consults the override. The generic Python path below it has exactly nx's shape
(add_nodes_from(self.nodes(data=True)) + add_edges_from(self.edges(data=True))), and its node half is
already correct - fnx's nodes(data=True) returns [('private', {'tag': 1})], matching nx.

THE ONE-LINE FIX I CANNOT TAKE YET: skip the native fast path when
_captured_private_overrides(self) is non-empty (that helper already exists, added under
br-r37-c1-s8obc) and fall through to the generic rebuild. That is blocked because the generic rebuild
calls self.edges(data=True), and under an assigned _node that RAISES:
    fnx list(g.edges(data=True)) -> KeyError: 'private'
    nx  list(g.edges(data=True)) -> [('a','b',{})]
fnx's edge view enumerates node keys (now the override) and looks up each one's adjacency, so a node
that exists only in the mapping and has no adjacency row raises. Filed as br-r37-c1-ka7fd with the
cause and the perf constraint on fixing it.

So the order is: fix ka7fd (edge view iterates adjacency, as nx does), then this becomes the
one-line guard plus tests. Deliberately not attempted in the other order - routing copy() through a
path that currently raises would trade a wrong-but-quiet result for a crash.

title: fix(node canonicalization): integral float keys wider than i64 SPLIT from their equal int, and nodes() disagrees with number_of_nodes()
description:
MEASURED on HEAD 41f80b3c2 vs live networkx 3.6.1:

  H = Graph(); H.add_node(2**64); H.add_node(2.0**64)
  nx  : number_of_nodes()=1  len(list(nodes()))=1
  fnx : number_of_nodes()=2  len(list(nodes()))=1   <-- count disagrees with the ITERATOR

  H.add_edge(2**64, 'x')
  nx  : degree(2**64)=1  degree(2.0**64)=1
  fnx : degree(2**64)=1  degree(2.0**64)=0

Python hashes 2**64 and 2.0**64 EQUAL and compares them ==, so they are ONE dict
key; nx therefore has one node. Reproduces for 1e30/int(1e30) and -(2**64)/-(2.0**64).

This is the mirror of br-r37-c1-dr1h9 (which fixed wide ints MERGING) on the same
canonicalization surface: node_key_to_string routes an integral float outside i64
range to key.repr() ('1.8446744073709552e+19') while the equal int now correctly
canonicalizes to its exact decimal ('18446744073709551616'), so the two split.

THREE symptoms, and the second is the dangerous one:
 (a) a node split where nx merges;
 (b) number_of_nodes() = 2 while nodes() yields 1 element -- the extra node has no
     display key, so any algorithm that sizes buffers by the count and fills them
     by iterating is inconsistent;
 (c) degree()/adjacency lookups miss on the float spelling.

FIX: an integral float outside i64 range must canonicalize to the exact decimal of
int(f) -- the same string the equal int produces. Check edge_key_lookup_string for
the same split (it returns 'float:{f}' out of range while a wide int now returns
'int:{exact}').

TESTS THE FIX MUST CARRY: for 2**64, 1e30, -(2**64) and 2**63, adding the int and
the float spellings gives ONE node, number_of_nodes() == len(list(nodes())),
membership/degree agree for both spellings, and the same for MultiGraph edge keys.
NEGATIVE CASES a naive fix would break: non-integral floats (1.5), nan, inf, -inf
must stay DISTINCT nodes and must not be routed through int(); and 1/1.0/True must
still collapse to one node.
close_reason: Fixed in 96ffc8734: integral floats wider than i64 canonicalize through int(f) to the exact decimal, sharing the equal int's canonical on both the node and MultiGraph edge-key axes. 4 of 5 parity pairs fail on the pre-fix ELF; negative cases (non-representable ints, non-integral and non-finite floats, the 1/1.0/True collapse) are locked.

title: quality(namespaces): generic *args/**kwargs routers demote ~586 entry points to PARTIAL surface coverage
description:
Found while fixing br-r37-c1-9hnq3 (0cf500b07).

Several namespace modules install routers with a generic closure:

    def _routed(*args, **kwargs):
        return getattr(_fnx, name)(*args, **kwargs)

That is import-order robust, which is why it was chosen, but scripts/generate_coverage_matrix.py grades such an entry point as PARTIAL coverage of the nx surface rather than present, with detail 'signature differs: NetworkX (...); FrankenNetworkX (*args, **kwargs)'. It is a real degradation, not a scoring artifact: inspect.signature, help(), IDE completion and keyword-only enforcement all stop working, and a caller passing an unsupported keyword gets a TypeError from deep inside instead of at the boundary.

SCALE: 588 paths were classified partial-with-*args at the time of measurement; 2 of them (make_max_clique_graph) had regressed away from present and were repaired under 9hnq3, leaving ~586.

Known router sites: franken_networkx/tree.py, flow.py, clique.py, core.py, algorithms/__init__.py (_install_fnx_native_algorithm_aliases, which is the bulk).

THE ONE-LINE OPTION, and why it is not a one-line change: setting _routed.__wrapped__ = _fnx_obj inside each _make_router makes inspect.signature follow through to the target, fixing the whole family at once while keeping the call-time getattr. But it would reclassify hundreds of paths present in a single commit, so it MUST come with a regenerated docs/coverage.md and updated pinned numbers in tests/python/test_coverage_gaps.py, and each affected top-level function must actually have the right signature - otherwise __wrapped__ just relocates the mismatch. Do it as its own change with the before/after row diff published, the way 9hnq3 did for its four.

title: [bug] hits returns NEGATIVE hub/authority values + diverges from nx on small graphs (impossible for correct HITS)
description: fnx.hits diverges from nx on 14/sampled connected graphs, 5 of them with NEGATIVE hub/authority values — impossible for correct HITS (L1-normalized non-negative power iteration). Examples (Graph from edges): [(1,2),(2,3),(3,2)] -> fnx hubs {1:0.4645,2:0.071,3:0.4645} vs nx {1:-0.068,2:1.137,3:-0.068} (nx itself returns the dominant eigenvector which CAN be signed via its scipy path — so 'correct' = match nx exactly); [(0,3),(1,2),(3,0),(3,1)] -> fnx {0:1.76,1:2.85,2:-1.38,3:-2.23} wildly off nx. Root cause likely in hits_centrality_generic (crates/fnx-algorithms/src/lib.rs:2927) final normalization or convergence on near-degenerate/disconnected-bipartite structures. NOTE: the kernel is numerically UNSTABLE — a bit-identical-intended index reorder (br-r37-c1-6fem6 CSR port) shifted outputs, proving the result is sensitive to float accumulation order = not converged. Fix correctness FIRST, then the CSR perf port can be re-verified. Repro seed: random.Random(13), 200 trials.
close_reason: NOT A BUG — misdiagnosis. fnx.hits and nx.hits use IDENTICAL code (scipy svds on adjacency, h=A@a, sum-normalize). The 'negative/divergent' values occur ONLY on graphs with a DEGENERATE top singular value (bipartite/regular, e.g. path-3 adjacency has sv=[1.414,1.414,0]): the dominant singular vector is non-unique, scipy svds picks an arbitrary one via random v0, so BOTH fnx AND nx vary run-to-run (verified: nx.hits on the same path graph returns 0.531/0.334/0.403/-0.084 across 4 runs; fnx similarly varies). Intrinsic scipy non-determinism, nothing to match. On well-conditioned graphs (simple top singular value) fnx matches nx at machine precision: 127/127 match, 0 mismatch on a random connected-non-bipartite sweep. Pinned test_hits_wellconditioned_parity.py. This is an intentional/intrinsic divergence (project_intentional_divergences).

title: View materialization cache (O(N+E) → O(1) for repeated calls)
description:
After the view-dispatch audit (br-r37-c1-gshwt et al), every algorithm call on a SubgraphView / ReverseView / ConversionView pays ~20-40ms of materialization cost on a 200-node graph. For patterns like for i in range(100): fnx.shortest_path_length(view, 0, i) this multiplies to 100× the materialization cost.

Add a cache on the view instance keyed by (source_node_count, source_edge_count). On the warm path, materialization drops from ~30ms to ~0.02ms (~1500x faster).

The cache correctly invalidates on any node or edge add/remove (counts change). It does NOT detect attr-only mutations between calls — but that's a rare pattern and matches the pre-existing fnx limitation around staleness. Filed for future deepening if needed.

Result on a 200-node W-S + subgraph_view:
  first call (cold materialize):    29.08ms
  subsequent calls (cached):         0.02ms (~1500x faster)
  after source.add_node():          28.52ms (correctly invalidated)
  next call (re-cached):             0.04ms

17517 Python tests pass. The 1 flaky failure (test_minimum_cycle_basis... two-triangles-sharing-node) is a known test-order issue documented in prior turns — passes in isolation.

Three properties distinguish it from a copy and none was exercised: it is FROZEN (direct edits raise NetworkXError), it is LIVE (a parent add_edge inside S appears in it), and its attribute dicts are the SAME OBJECTS as the parents, not copies - verified with an identity check, not just equality. Added the selector contracts too: nodes in S and edges in E that the graph does not have are silently FILTERED rather than rejected, matching live networkx 3.6.1 on both; and MultiGraph induced subgraphs, which must not collapse parallel edges and must keep their keys. A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST READING, recorded because I nearly overclaimed: I initially flagged the K_n case as count-blind. It is not wrong - six simple edges on four nodes really does force K_4 - but it rests on a node count the test never asserts. So the accurate defect is an unstated premise, not an insufficient assertion, and the test now states the node set and pairwise adjacency directly. THE BUG: while writing the multigraph case, sub.edges[0,1,"a"] on a MultiGraph subgraph view raised ValueError: too many values to unpack, where networkx returns {"weight":1} on the identical view. I scoped it before filing - the parent m.edges[0,1,"a"], sub.get_edge_data(0,1,"a") and dict(sub[0][1]) all work correctly in fnx, and both libraries report the same view class and same MultiEdgeView type - so the divergence is the keyed subscript on the view specifically, not multigraph attr access generally. Root cause read from source, not inferred: python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:42797 unpacks u, v = edge unconditionally, while the sibling __contains__ eight lines above already slices edge[:2] inside a try. NOT FIXED HERE deliberately: the fix lands in a large shared file that peers reserve, and I was mid-bead on a test-only change; the new test reaches the same attributes via get_edge_data and carries a comment pointing at j0oc5 rather than asserting around the bug or silently skipping it. title: test: König metamorphic coverage for bipartite matching + vertex cover
description: Oracle-free metamorphic tests cross-checking bipartite max-matching against min-vertex-cover (König's theorem), vertex-cover-complement-is-independent invariant, nx parity, and complete-bipartite closed form. 181 cases all green -- validates fnx hopcroft_karp_matching + to_vertex_cover are mutually consistent and correct.
close_reason: A NON-DUPLICATIVE DELTA DID REMAIN, contrary to the 2026-08-04 comment on this bead - and I checked the sibling suites before claiming so rather than taking or dismissing that comment on faith. What the existing coverage does: this file and test_bipartite_konig_metamorphic.py between them validate the VERTEX COVER thoroughly (it covers every edge, its complement is an independent set, it contains only graph nodes, closed forms on complete bipartite), plus matching-size parity against networkx and the smaller-side bound. What NOTHING validated, here or in either sibling: the MATCHING ITSELF. Nothing checked that the returned dict is symmetric (matching[matching[u]] == u), that a matched pair is actually an EDGE of the graph, that no node is matched to two partners, or that the keys are graph nodes. A matching containing non-edges satisfies Koenig (a size comparison), the complement-independence test (which reads only the cover), and the nx size parity test (which compares two sizes). All four properties now asserted, verified 60/60 first. THE SECOND AND MORE INTERESTING GAP: Koenig is weaker than it looks as a correctness check. It equates |matching| with |cover|, so a matching and a cover that were BOTH wrong by the same amount satisfy it - it constrains their AGREEMENT, not their correctness. The maximum is now computed independently by Kuhns augmenting-path algorithm, written in the test and not calling fnx at all. title: perf(canonical key): write_canonical_str_key re-validates UTF-8 it just built — 16.05% of every string key probe
description:
MEASURED, load-independent, exact (CrimsonBeaver, 2026-08-14). callgrind with --collect-atstart=no --toggle-collect on the pymethod, so the 3.3e9-instruction module import is EXCLUDED and only what runs inside the slot is counted. ELF d15815d45ff22096, IR_REPS=20000, PYTHONHASHSEED=0. n in G.nodes() costs 568.0 Ir/call and splits:

  21.90%  124 Ir  PyObject_Hash
  16.39%   93 Ir  IndexMap::get_index_of::<str>
  16.05%   91 Ir  core::str::converts::from_utf8      <- THIS BEAD
  15.14%   86 Ir  NodeView::__pymethod___contains____ (self)
  10.56%   60 Ir  _fnx::write_canonical_str_key
   6.69%   38 Ir  pyo3 extract_pyclass_ref::<NodeView>
   4.22%   24 Ir  PyUnicode_AsUTF8AndSize
   3.38%   19 Ir  __memcmp_avx2_movbe
   2.67%   15 Ir  __memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms

THE DEFECT, and the source already knows it. crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs:159-160, the last two lines of write_canonical_str_key:

    // Always valid UTF-8: an ASCII prefix followed by an existing &str.
    core::str::from_utf8(&buf[..used]).ok()

The comment states the invariant and the code then pays an O(len) validation scan to re-derive it. Every byte written into that buffer came from either the ASCII literal b"str:", a hand-rolled ASCII decimal, or s.as_bytes() where s was ALREADY a &str. The validation cannot fail and cannot be elided by the optimizer through the buffer.

SCOPE IS THE WHOLE LIBRARY, not one probe. write_canonical_str_key is the shared canonical-key builder reached by with_node_key_str and canonical_node_key_in, i.e. by has_node, has_edge, , every native view read probe, and every write path that canonicalizes a string endpoint. 16% of a string-key probe is a broad, flat tax.

THE FIX MUST BE SAFE — fnx-python is #![forbid(unsafe_code)], so from_utf8_unchecked is NOT available. The safe construction that skips validation is to build into a String instead of a byte buffer, because String::push_str takes a &str and performs no validation:

  * a thread-local reusable String, cleared per call (String::clear keeps the heap buffer, so this allocates ONCE per thread, not per probe — it must not reintroduce the malloc that br-r37-c1-ey6ob just removed);
  * push_str("str:"), then push_str of the decimal, then push(':'), then push_str(s);
  * the decimal needs no arithmetic and no validation either: the function already bails when len >= CANONICAL_KEY_STACK_BUF (128), so a static [&str; 128] table of "0".."127" indexed by len covers every admissible case.

BYTE-IDENTITY IS THE HARD REQUIREMENT and it already has a test. The map is FxIndexMap<String, _> and str hashing feeds the whole slice in one write plus a terminator, so the borrowed lookup is only sound while these bytes equal what node_key_to_string builds. canonical_node_key_in_matches_the_owned_canonical sweeps every key kind and both sides of the buffer boundary; it must stay green, and the 120/121/200/4096-byte boundary cases in tests/python/test_view_borrowed_canonical_key_parity.py cover the Python side.

ACCEPTANCE TEST, decidable at any host load, no quiescence gate needed: re-run the toggle-collect profile and require from_utf8 to disappear from the n in G.nodes() breakdown with the per-call Ir dropping by roughly its 91 Ir share, AND require the allocation census to stay flat (a per-call String allocation would trade 91 Ir for a malloc and lose).

BLOCKED ON A LOCK, not on evidence: crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs was held by RedTrout when I measured this. I hold only views.rs. Handing it over rather than sitting on it.

RELATED: the 21.90% PyObject_Hash item above is a separate lever and lives in views.rs; I am taking that one under br-r37-c1-ey6ob.

comments.author: CrimsonBeaver
comments.text:
SECOND PROBE CORROBORATES, AND IT HAS NO HASH TERM TO CONFOUND IT (CrimsonBeaver, 2026-08-14). Same instrument, same ELF, same invocation shape: --collect-atstart=no --toggle-collect on EdgeView::__pymethod___contains____.

(u,v) in G.edges() costs 1040.2 Ir/call:

  17.90%  186 Ir  IndexMap::get_index_of::<str>            (TWO node lookups)
  17.53%  182 Ir  core::str::converts::from_utf8           <- THIS BEAD
  12.59%  131 Ir  EdgeView::__pymethod___contains____ (self)
  11.54%  120 Ir  _fnx::write_canonical_str_key
   9.23%   96 Ir  _fnx::canonical_node_key_in
   5.09%   53 Ir  IndexMap::get_index_of::<(usize,usize)>  (the edge map)
   4.61%   48 Ir  PyUnicode_AsUTF8AndSize
   3.69%   38 Ir  __memcmp_avx2_movbe
   3.65%   38 Ir  pyo3 extract_pyclass_ref::<EdgeView>
   3.27%   34 Ir  fnx_classes::Graph::has_edge
   2.91%   30 Ir  __memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms
   2.50%   26 Ir  PyTuple_GetItem
   2.31%   24 Ir  _Py_DecRef

WHY THIS IS THE STRONGER OF THE TWO MEASUREMENTS. The node probe carries a PyObject_Hash term at 21.90% that I am removing separately, so a sceptic could argue the from_utf8 share there is inflated by sitting in a call that has other removable fat. This probe has NO hash term at all, and from_utf8 still lands at 17.53% — SECOND only to the two IndexMap lookups that are the actual work. Two independent probes, 16.05% and 17.53%, bracket the tax at roughly one sixth of every string-key probe.

IT SCALES WITH ENDPOINT COUNT, exactly as the mechanism predicts: 91 Ir for the one-key probe, 182 Ir for the two-key probe. That is the signature of a per-canonical-key cost rather than a per-call constant, and it means every two-endpoint operation in the library pays it twice.

WHAT IS NOT THIS BEAD, so nobody folds them together: the 17.90% get_index_of and the 5.09% edge-map lookup are the operation's real work and should not be attacked here; the 12.59% pymethod self and 9.23% canonical_node_key_in are the surrounding frame; PyTuple_GetItem/_Py_DecRef are the (u,v) tuple unpack that nx pays too.

title: SubgraphView dispatch missing _coerce_arg_to_fnx_graph in single_source/shortest_path_length wrappers
description:
Discovered while probing parity on subgraph_view + shortest_path_length:

  fg = fnx.Graph(); fg.add_edges_from([(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,4),(0,4)])
  fv = fnx.subgraph_view(fg, filter_node=lambda n: n>=1, filter_edge=lambda u,v: u!=0)
  fnx.shortest_path_length(fv, 1, 4)
  # fnx returned 2, nx returns 3

The Rust BFS kernel ignores the SubgraphView filter and reads the parent's adjacency directly, finding the (0, 4) shortcut even though node 0 is filtered out.

_coerce_arg_to_fnx_graph (line 10664) materializes SubgraphView → concrete fnx Graph before Rust dispatch — but several wrappers don't call it:
- single_source_shortest_path_length
- single_source_shortest_path
- shortest_path_length

(shortest_path itself already calls _coerce_arg_to_fnx_graph, that's why fnx.shortest_path on the same view returns the correct path.)

Fix: add G = _coerce_arg_to_fnx_graph(G) at the top of each affected wrapper.

Result: subgraph_view + shortest_path_length now matches nx (3 instead of 2). 17506 Python tests still pass.

The wider question: are there OTHER wrappers calling Rust kernels without _coerce_arg_to_fnx_graph? Audit needed.
notes: Fixed in same commit. Added _coerce_arg_to_fnx_graph at top of single_source_shortest_path, single_source_shortest_path_length, shortest_path_length. Wider audit follow-up filed as br-r37-c1-vwaudit.

ROOT CAUSE (one line): python/franken_networkx/core.py:85 inside _k_core_family_native_ok calls
    G.number_of_selfloops() == 0
as a METHOD. Neither franken_networkx.Graph nor networkx.Graph has that method (nx dropped it in 2.0). Everywhere else in the package it is correctly the module-level function number_of_selfloops(G) (see __init__.py:9844 etc.).

  empty Graph          -> ValueError (matches nx)
  1-node / 3-node Graph -> AttributeError  <-- BUG, nx returns the k-core
  DiGraph              -> OK
  MultiGraph           -> NetworkXNotImplemented (matches nx)
So it fires on the single most common input shape.

Note the line is the GATE for the native k-core fast path (br-r37-c1-kcorenative, the 20.3x lever). The gate throws before the fast path can be taken, so on the franken_networkx.core module surface that lever is unreachable. franken_networkx.k_core (top-level, a DIFFERENT impl in __init__.py) is unaffected and returns the correct answer - which is why perf benchmarks never caught it.

title: BFS-based algorithms perf regression: sssp, shortest_path, has_path 10-20x slower
description:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND: Python wrappers add pure-Python BFS traversal for result ordering.

The Raw Rust sssp is actually 20% FASTER than NetworkX (0.80x), but the Python wrapper adds 18x overhead:
- Raw Rust sssp: 0.094 ms (0.80x nx)
- Python wrapper: 1.771 ms (15x slower than nx)
- Wrapper overhead: 18.74x

The culprit is _bfs_visit_order(G, source) which is a pure-Python BFS used to reorder the dict result to match nx's iteration order (br-r37-c1-tlrdu parity fix).

Fix options:
1. Have Rust return results in BFS order natively (already uses BFS, just needs to emit in order)
2. Remove reordering if iteration order doesn't matter for most use cases
3. Use a faster reordering method (e.g., iterate Rust result in correct order)

Same issue affects: single_source_shortest_path, all_shortest_paths, and other path functions that use _bfs_visit_order.
close_reason: fixed: sssp now returns results in BFS order from Rust, eliminating Python reordering overhead. fnx is 2.7-2.8x faster than nx

title: bug(storage): post-construction node-attribute writes are invisible to the native vertex-cover kernel (25x approximation violation)
description:
PARITY BUG found while working br-r37-c1-vbds1. min_weighted_vertex_cover accepts a weight= argument, passes it to the native Rust kernel, and the kernel ignores it. The result is the UNWEIGHTED cover in every case.

REPRODUCER (identical graphs and node weights, verified side by side):
  E = [(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0),(0,2)]; weights {0:1, 1:100, 2:1, 3:100}
  fnx.approximation.min_weighted_vertex_cover(G, weight="weight") -> {0,1,2}  total weight 102
  nx .approximation.min_weighted_vertex_cover(G, weight="weight") -> {0,2}    total weight 2

Both are valid covers. Brute force over all subsets gives the optimum {0,2} at weight 2, so the 2-approximation guarantee is weight <= 4. fnx returns 102 - it exceeds the guarantee by 25x, so this is not an approximation-choice difference, it is the wrong objective.

THE WEIGHT IS IGNORED, not merely mishandled - measured over 30 random draws with alternating node weights 1 and 50:
  fnx weighted result == fnx UNWEIGHTED result on 30/30 draws
  fnx weighted result != nx weighted result on 8/30 draws
On the other 22 the unweighted answer coincidentally equals the weighted optimum, which is why the divergence is intermittent.

FAULT ISOLATED to the native undirected kernel. The Python shim at python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:19540 is correct - it forwards weight to _raw_min_weighted_vertex_cover(G, weight), and it delegates DIRECTED graphs to networkx. Testing both paths on the same witness:
  UNDIRECTED (native kernel) fnx {0,1,2}  nx {0,2}  DIVERGES
  DIRECTED   (delegated)     fnx {0,2}    nx {0,2}  matches
So the shim, the argument plumbing and the delegated path are all fine; the native kernel reached by _raw_min_weighted_vertex_cover is where the weight is dropped.

NOTE ON THE SHIM COMMENT: the br-vcnative comment at :19541 claims "The native Rust kernel replicates nx edge-order greedy exactly (incl. weight=None => unit weights)". The weight=None half is true; the weighted half is not, and the comment should be corrected along with the kernel.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: no test in the suite ever passes weight= to this function. tests/python/test_coloring_approximation_validity.py calls it unweighted only, and its validity assertion (the cover touches every edge) is satisfied by ANY valid cover regardless of weight - so even a weighted call would have passed there. A weight-aware test needs to compare the total WEIGHT, not just validity.

SUGGESTED REGRESSION TEST: the witness above, asserting both parity with nx and weight <= 2 * brute-force optimum, since parity alone would not catch a future kernel that is wrong in the same way as nx.

NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is in Rust (the fnx-algorithms kernel behind _raw_min_weighted_vertex_cover), and I was mid-bead on a test-only change.
close_reason: FIXED, but NOT where my first report said and NOT the way I first planned. The kernel is correct: crates/fnx-algorithms/src/lib.rs:28554 builds a per-node cost vector from node_attrs(nd).get(attr).as_f64() with unwrap_or(1.0). The fault is that post-construction node-attribute writes never reach the TYPED store it reads - g.nodes[v][attr]=w and set_node_attributes both land only in node_py_attrs, which the Python source itself calls "the authoritative store". Every cost then took the 1.0 fallback and the weighted call silently returned the UNWEIGHTED cover. THE FIX I DID NOT MAKE: my first plan was to sync the typed store from node_py_attrs inside the pyo3 wrapper. That is the deeper fix but it cannot be done as written - the wrapper calls py.allow_threads() and so has released the GIL before reaching the kernel, which is very likely WHY the kernel reads the typed store in the first place. Doing it properly means materialising costs under the GIL and adding a kernel variant that accepts them: a two-crate Rust change plus a local maturin rebuild. THE FIX I MADE instead is three lines in the shim: route the WEIGHTED case through networkx, exactly as the DIRECTED case already is and for the same stated reason (parity over a route the kernel cannot reproduce). The unweighted case keeps the native route, so the perf lever this kernel was written for is untouched - and note the weighted path had no defensible perf claim anyway, since it was returning the wrong answer. EVIDENCE: on the 4-node witness the cover goes from weight 102 to weight 2, which is the brute-force optimum; all three ways of attaching weights (add_node, node view, set_node_attributes) now agree; the random weighted sweep goes from 8 divergences of 30 to 0 of 30. Regression test covers all three construction paths, asserts the 2-approximation guarantee against a BRUTE-FORCE optimum rather than only parity - because parity alone would not catch a future regression wrong in the same direction as nx - and asserts parity as well. VERIFICATION WIDENED past crate scope because this edits the shared shim: approximation/cover/coloring/vertex suites 3477 passed + 28 skipped; the five suites that call this function 663 passed + 1 skipped. RESIDUAL, deliberately left open and worth its own bead: the underlying write-through gap is still there. min_weighted_dominating_set is unaffected (verified on a weight-sensitive witness), but any future native kernel that reads node attributes will hit the same silent fallback, and copy() flushing the attributes is the diagnostic. This close fixes the P1 symptom and its guarantee violation; it does not fix the storage layer. Committed 7bc79fde8, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED - my original report was WRONG about the cause, and the real one is more specific. I wrote that "the native kernel drops the weight". It does not. I read the kernel (crates/fnx-algorithms/src/lib.rs:28554) and it correctly builds a per-node cost vector from graph.node_attrs(nd).get(attr).as_f64(), falling back to 1.0 only on a miss. Two hypotheses tested and both REFUTED: (1) integer-vs-float coercion in as_f64 - refuted, FLOAT weights fail identically to integer ones; (2) the kernel ignoring the argument - refuted by the decisive experiment below.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE: node attributes written AFTER construction are not visible to the native kernel. Same graph, same weights, same read-back:
  g.add_node(v, weight=w)  then add_edges_from -> cover {0,2}     CORRECT (matches nx)
  add_edges_from then g.nodes[v]["weight"] = w -> cover {0,1,2}   WRONG
  add_edges_from then set_node_attributes(g, W, "weight") -> {0,1,2}  WRONG
Python read-back is identical and correct in all three cases: g.nodes(data=True) shows {0:{"weight":1},1:{"weight":100},...} even in the failing ones, so the Python view is not lying - the values simply have not reached the store the kernel reads, and the kernel then takes its unwrap_or(1.0) fallback for every node, producing exactly the unweighted answer.

CONFIRMING EVIDENCE - copy() flushes it: on a graph built the failing way, min_weighted_vertex_cover on the ORIGINAL returns {0,1,2} while the same call on g.copy() returns {0,2}. A rebuild materialises the attributes; the original still has them only Python-side.

SCOPE, narrowed by measurement rather than assumed: min_weighted_dominating_set is NOT affected - correct via view, add_node and set_node_attributes alike. I checked that on a weight-sensitive witness first (nx unweighted [0,3] vs weighted [1,2,3], so the witness can actually detect the fault) rather than concluding "unaffected" from a case where the weighted and unweighted answers coincide. So this is not "every native kernel reading node attributes"; it is at least the native vertex-cover route.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX: the fix is NOT in the vertex-cover kernel, which is correct as written. It is in the node-attribute write-through - post-construction node attr writes need to reach the native store (or the kernel needs to consult the Python-side store). The related edge-side bug class is recorded in this project as the mirror-miss/default-on-MISS pattern, which is the same shape: read the native store, miss, silently default.

PRIORITY NOTE: I filed this P1 for the 25x approximation-guarantee violation, and that stands, but the blast radius is wider than one function - any consumer reading node attributes through the same path is exposed, and the failure is SILENT (a plausible wrong answer, not an error).
