title: perf(mutation): add_edge is 0.46-0.50x vs nx — the Rust core alone (~507 ns/edge) exceeds nx's ENTIRE add_edge, and the ledger is ~35% of it
description:
Filed by OliveDesert 2026-08-08 from the add_edge profile that upheld the CloudyTurtle 2026-07-26 REJECT. Full evidence in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

THE SHIM IS NOT THE TARGET — that is settled, do not re-open it. Measured on the 2000-node/8000-edge workload, fresh graph per timed unit, live nx 3.6.1 in-invocation, both A/A nulls at 1.0035x/1.0036x, ELF 675707ac:

  nx  add_edge                        615.0 ns per edge
  fnx add_edge public (shimmed)      1433.8 ns per edge   0.4289x
  fnx add_edge raw (shim bypassed)   1113.2 ns per edge   0.5525x
  fnx has_edge probes alone           156.9 ns per edge

The whole Python shim is 320.6 ns = 22.4% of end-to-end, under CloudyTurtle's 40% bar. Bypassing it entirely — strictly more than any legal edit, since the shim also enforces None rejection and unhashable-endpoint errors — still leaves 0.5525x.

THIS BEAD IS THE OTHER 77.6%: native raw_add_edge costs 1113.2 ns per edge against NetworkX's 615.0 ns for what is fundamentally a dict insert plus two adjacency-row updates. That is where the add_edge loss actually lives and nothing else on this surface is worth attacking first.

WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN AND MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED:
  * The CGSE decision ledger was previously measured at 46.7% of add_edge and already attacked — the fix was bounding residency and recording only on refusal (cost is RETENTION not materialisation), landing 1.85x. Re-measure its current share before assuming there is more there.
  * Graph::add_edge already had a redundant O(n) scan replaced by an O(1) computed flag.
  * Node-key canonicalization now costs about 65 ns per string probe after br-r37-c1-7faiu removed core::fmt from write_canonical_str_key. add_edge canonicalizes TWO endpoints per call, so roughly 130 ns of the 1113 ns is key building — worth confirming, and note the write path still calls node_key_to_string (owned String) rather than the borrowed with_node_key_str, because it needs an owned key to insert.

PROFILE FIRST, and profile INSIDE Rust: this is not decomposable from Python. Suggested split of the 1113 ns — the two node_key_to_string calls, the CGSE ledger record, the adjacency IndexMap inserts on both endpoints, the edge attribute storage, and the mutation-token/sequence bump. There is an existing in-crate self-time A/B harness pattern to copy at crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs borrowed_canonical_key_self_time_ab (run with --release --ignored --nocapture).

CGSE NON-REGRESSION IS ABSOLUTE HERE. Any change must retain: None rejection, unhashable endpoint errors, partial node-creation state (nx creates u BEFORE examining v, so a bad v leaves u on the graph), existing-edge attribute merge with live-dict identity, keyword signatures (u_of_edge/v_of_edge), node and edge insertion order, mutation-token invalidation, subclasses, and private-storage behavior.

DECIDE on the balanced-square substrate with a fresh graph per timed unit and both A/A nulls recorded, not on the perf_harness quiescence gate, which cannot be admitted on this host.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SCALING DIAGNOSTIC APPLIED — THE MUTATION ENTRY IS A CONSTANT, NOT A WHOLE-NODE-SET PASS (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08). Bead left OPEN; this narrows it and rules out one whole class of cause.

WHY THIS PROBE: the chunk-8 campaign (uta2n/hepb5/ab5u7/iozi3) found four batch collectors whose per-call cost was a whole-graph node clone, diagnosed by exactly one test — cost scales with NODE count, flat in EDGE count. jc9e4's headline is that 75.4% of raw_add_edge is per-CALL boundary cost, with a no-op add_node at 914 ns while mutating nothing. Same shape of symptom, so the same diagnostic was the obvious thing to run before any Rust profiling.

MEASURED, 512 probes per timed call, load 0.88, ELF daf4d388d215ecab95c3b6fdc5b4f0ecc91e6abe2738ce4c1c77071409c5daf4. All three arms are no-ops on graph contents, so only entry cost is timed:

      N       E   add_node noop   add_edge noop   has_node (read control)
    500    8000        880.2 ns        242.0 ns        74.5 ns
   1000    8000        690.3 ns        247.3 ns        75.7 ns
   2000    8000        678.4 ns        261.5 ns        75.2 ns
   4000    8000        672.3 ns        262.3 ns        76.6 ns
   8000    8000        683.7 ns        272.9 ns        77.5 ns

  scaling vs N=500:  add_node x0.78   add_edge x1.13   has_node x1.04
  edge sweep, N=2000, add_node:  E=1000 667.1 ns / E=8000 662.8 x0.99 / E=32000 658.8 x0.99

CONCLUSION: NO whole-node-set pass on the single-call mutation entry. Sixteen-fold more nodes costs x0.78 for add_node (the N=500 reading of 880.2 is the outlier; the other four sit flat at 672-690) and x1.13 for add_edge, against x15.20-x19.30 for the four defective batch collectors. Edge count is flat at x0.99. The per-call cost is a CONSTANT of roughly 670 ns for add_node and 260 ns for add_edge-on-existing.

So the defect class just fixed four times does NOT extend here, and applying that fix pattern to the mutation entry would find nothing. jc9e4's remaining 77.6% genuinely needs in-crate Rust self-time profiling, exactly as the bead already says — this probe removes the cheap alternative rather than replacing it.

NEW LEAD, AND IT IS BACKWARDS: a no-op add_node costs 678 ns while a no-op add_edge costs 262 ns. add_node is 2.6x MORE expensive than add_edge for the equivalent do-nothing call, even though add_edge does strictly more work — two endpoints to canonicalize and look up, versus one. Whatever the per-mutation entry spends its time on, add_node pays appreciably more of it per call. That asymmetry is stable across all five graph sizes, is measurable from Python, and is a far tighter target for the Rust self-time profile than "the entry path" in general. Start there.

The read control confirms the probe is sound: has_node at 75 ns, x1.04 flat. It shares canonicalization with both mutators but not the mutation entry, and it is an order of magnitude cheaper than either.

Script: scratchpad/mutation_entry_scaling.py.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION — MY "2.6x BACKWARDS ASYMMETRY" LEAD FROM THE PREVIOUS COMMENT IS INVALID. WITHDRAWN (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08).

WHAT I CLAIMED: that a no-op add_node (678 ns) costing 2.6x a no-op add_edge (262 ns) was backwards, since add_edge does strictly more work, and that this asymmetry was the tight target for the Rust self-time profile.

WHY IT IS WRONG: the two arms do not do comparable amounts of work, and I did not check the shim before comparing them. `_make_none_rejecting_add_edge` (__init__.py:3385) on an EXISTING edge with no attrs runs

    edge_exists = self.has_edge(u_of_edge, v_of_edge)
    if edge_exists:
        if attr:  ...merge...
        return None

so it short-circuits in Python and NEVER CALLS raw_add_edge. My "add_edge no-op" arm was timing a Python early-return over one has_edge probe. My "add_node no-op" arm went all the way through to native raw_add_node. I compared a short-circuit against a full call and read the difference as a mechanism.

CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, 512 probes per timed call, N=2000/E=8000, load quiet, same ELF daf4d388d215ecab95c3b6fdc5b4f0ecc91e6abe2738ce4c1c77071409c5daf4:

    add_node(existing)  public   892.2 ns
    add_node(existing)  RAW      485.3 ns
    add_edge(existing)  public   256.4 ns
    has_edge(existing)           128.8 ns
    has_node(existing)            75.9 ns

add_edge-noop at 256.4 ns sits right on top of has_edge at 128.8 ns plus wrapper overhead, exactly as the short-circuit predicts. There is no backwards asymmetry to explain. Treat the previous comment's NEW LEAD paragraph as withdrawn; the rest of that comment — the scaling diagnostic showing the mutation entry is a CONSTANT and not a whole-node-set pass, x0.78/x1.13/x1.04 against x15.20-x19.30 — stands and was measured correctly.

WHAT SURVIVES AS A REAL DATUM, stated with its own caveat: add_node public 892.2 ns against the captured raw descriptor at 485.3 ns. That gap is large, but the two arms use DIFFERENT call protocols — `g.add_node(x)` is an attribute lookup plus bound-method call, `RAW(g, x)` is an unbound native method with explicit self — so the difference is not cleanly attributable to the Python shim body, which is only a None test, a hash() and a forwarding call. Do not quote 406.9 ns as a shim tax. Anyone pursuing it needs a same-protocol comparison first.

LESSON FOR THIS SURFACE, since it has now bitten me twice in this bead's vicinity: before comparing two public calls as if they measure the same path, read what the Python shim does on the exact input you are passing. add_edge on an existing edge, add_edge on a new edge, and add_node on an existing node take three genuinely different routes through that file, and only one of them reaches native add_edge.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SAME-PROTOCOL MEASUREMENT DONE — THE add_node SHIM IS 21.9%, NOT THE 406.9 ns THE NAIVE COMPARISON IMPLIED (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08). This closes the open question I left in the previous comment rather than handing it on.

The previous comment recorded add_node public 892.2 ns against the captured raw descriptor at 485.3 ns, flagged that the two arms use different call protocols, and said explicitly: do not quote 406.9 ns as a shim tax, a same-protocol comparison is needed first. Here it is.

METHOD: build a subclass whose add_node IS the raw native method —

    class RawGraph(fnx.Graph): pass
    RawGraph.add_node = fnx._GRAPH_ADD_NODE_RAW

— so BOTH arms are an instance attribute lookup plus a bound call on a 2000-node graph, and the only difference is whether the Python shim body runs. Arms interleaved ABBA across 9 rounds so drift hits both equally. 512 probes per timed call, quiet host, ELF daf4d388d215ecab95c3b6fdc5b4f0ecc91e6abe2738ce4c1c77071409c5daf4.

  add_node public (Python shim)     646.1 ns
  add_node raw    (same protocol)   504.7 ns
  shim body cost                    141.4 ns = 21.9% of the public call

So the caveat was worth making: the cross-protocol comparison overstated the shim by 2.9x (406.9 against 141.4). Nobody should quote the earlier figure.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE BEAD. add_node now decomposes the same way add_edge does, and to almost the same proportions:

  add_edge   Python shim 22.4%   native 77.6%   (measured on br-r37-c1-vabqj)
  add_node   Python shim 21.9%   native 78.1%   (this measurement)

Both mutators put roughly four fifths of their cost inside native code. That is a consistent picture rather than two separate puzzles, and it means the same conclusion transfers: the CloudyTurtle 2026-07-26 REJECT on Graph.add_edge requires at least 40% of end-to-end time in removable Python shim frames before the shim may be edited, and at 21.9% add_node does not clear that bar either. Do not attack the add_node shim on this evidence.

RESIDUAL CAVEAT, stated so the number is used correctly: the two arms are `function` and `method_descriptor` respectively. Both resolve through the same instance-attribute-lookup and bound-call path, which is the protocol difference the previous comment was worried about, but they are not byte-identical descriptor kinds. The 141.4 ns therefore still contains a small unquantified descriptor-dispatch component and is best read as an upper bound on the shim body itself.

The three facts that now hold together for this bead: the mutation entry cost is a CONSTANT and not a whole-node-set pass (x0.78/x1.13 against x15.20-x19.30); the "2.6x backwards asymmetry" was an invalid comparison and is withdrawn; and both mutators are ~78% native. The remaining work is in-crate Rust self-time profiling of that native 78%, exactly as the bead has said from the start — with three cheap alternatives now eliminated by measurement rather than assumption.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CANONICALIZATION IS ELIMINATED AS THE TARGET FOR THE NATIVE 78% (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08). Bead left OPEN; this is the fourth cheap cause ruled out by measurement, and it uses the technique that positively identified canonicalization on the READ path, so the contrast is the evidence.

THE TECHNIQUE, which already worked twice on this surface: compare the same operation on STR keys against INT keys. `has_node` has an identity-int fast path that returns before canonicalizing, so a key-type difference there measures canonicalization directly — that is how br-r37-c1-7faiu attributed 54.5% of has_node(str) to the canonical key build and then removed core::fmt from it.

MEASURED, 512 probes per timed call, same-protocol subclasses so no Python shim frame is in either arm, quiet host, ELF daf4d388d215ecab95c3b6fdc5b4f0ecc91e6abe2738ce4c1c77071409c5daf4:

  raw add_node  STR keys   532.9 ns
  raw add_node  INT keys   539.7 ns      <- no cheaper; 1.3% the other way, inside noise
  has_node      STR keys    74.3 ns
  has_node      INT keys    51.9 ns      <- 22.4 ns cheaper, the canonicalization gap

THE CONTRAST IS THE RESULT. On the READ path, key type is worth 22.4 ns of a 74.3 ns call — canonicalization is a large, removable share, which is exactly what 7faiu exploited. On the WRITE path, key type is worth NOTHING: 532.9 against 539.7, with the int arm marginally slower. If canonicalization were a meaningful share of native add_node it would show up here the way it shows up on has_node, and it does not.

So the ~535 ns of native add_node is dominated by the insert bookkeeping, not by building the canonical key. Do not attack node-key canonicalization for this bead. That also means the CloudyTurtle node-key interning HOLD is irrelevant here — it fences a cost this path does not appreciably pay.

INCIDENTAL, and it argues against an obvious-looking micro-lever: add_node evidently has no identity-int fast path of the kind has_node has (or it would show as an int-arm win). Adding one would be pointless — the int arm is not faster, so there is nothing for a fast path to skip.

FOUR CAUSES NOW ELIMINATED BY MEASUREMENT for jc9e4's native 78%, none by assumption:
  1. a whole-node-set pass per call — ruled out, entry cost is CONSTANT (x0.78/x1.13 in nodes, x0.99 in edges) against x15.20-x19.30 for the four defective batch collectors;
  2. the Python shim — 21.9% for add_node, 22.4% for add_edge, both under the 40% bar CloudyTurtle's REJECT sets before a shim may be edited;
  3. a "2.6x backwards asymmetry" between the two mutators — withdrawn, it was a short-circuit in the add_edge shim compared against a full native call;
  4. node-key canonicalization — this measurement.

WHAT REMAINS is the insert bookkeeping itself: the IndexMap insert, the node_key_map entry, node_iter_mirror_insert, bump_nodes_seq and the CGSE ledger record. Those are not separable from Python and DO need the in-crate self-time profile this bead has always called for. The difference is that it can now start from a short list rather than the whole entry path, and the CGSE ledger component of it is separately tracked and quantified on br-r37-c1-g2nev at ~10.9% of add_edge_with_attrs.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY PREVIOUS COMMENT — "DOMINATED BY INSERT BOOKKEEPING" IS WRONG, AND THE TRUE SPLIT REDIRECTS THIS BEAD (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08).

WHAT I SAID LAST COMMENT: that with canonicalization eliminated, "the ~535 ns of native add_node is dominated by the insert bookkeeping", and I handed over a five-item shortlist — IndexMap insert, node_key_map entry, node_iter_mirror_insert, bump_nodes_seq, CGSE ledger record.

WHY IT WAS WRONG: every measurement behind that sentence used `add_node` on a node that was ALREADY PRESENT. That call inserts nothing. I attributed a cost to insert bookkeeping while measuring a path that never reaches it — the same category of error as the add_edge short-circuit I withdrew earlier on this bead, and I made it again one comment later.

MEASURED PROPERLY, 512 probes per timed call, same-protocol subclass so no Python shim frame, fresh graph per timed slot for the insert arm so the nodes are genuinely new, ELF daf4d388d215ecab95c3b6fdc5b4f0ecc91e6abe2738ce4c1c77071409c5daf4:

  raw add_node  EXISTING (no-op)   538.2 ns
  raw add_node  NEW      (insert)  596.2 ns
  insert-only component             58.0 ns  = 10% of the new-node call

SO THE INSERT IS 10%, NOT THE DOMINANT TERM. The IndexMap insert, the node_key_map entry, node_iter_mirror_insert and bump_nodes_seq together cost about 58 ns. Roughly 90% of native add_node is entry cost that runs on a call which changes nothing at all.

THAT REDIRECTS THE PROFILE. The five-item shortlist I handed over is mostly the 10%. What needs profiling is whatever runs BEFORE and REGARDLESS of the present/absent decision. The leading candidate is the CGSE decision ledger, and the reason is not a guess: br-r37-c1-g2nev established that the ledger's cost on the mutation path is RETENTION per call rather than materialisation of work, measured at ~10.9% of add_edge_with_attrs with a 3.2002x lever available on its record component. A cost that is per-CALL rather than per-MUTATION is exactly the shape of a 538 ns no-op, and nothing else on the list has that shape.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: I have not measured the ledger's share of add_node specifically, and the 10.9% figure is g2nev's for add_edge_with_attrs, not this. It is a candidate with a matching shape, not an attribution. The in-crate self-time profile this bead calls for should time the no-op path first — that is where 90% of the cost is — and the ledger record is where I would put the first probe.

  batch           675.5 ns/node

  A/A null, loop arm    1.3255x     <-- INADMISSIBLE
  A/A null, batch arm   1.0102x

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
STORAGE DECOMPOSITION ATTEMPTED, INVALID BY CONSTRUCTION, REVERTED — AND IT EXPOSED AN INSTRUMENT
PROBLEM THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PROBE WOULD HAVE (CopperCliff, 2026-08-08). No source change
survives; `git diff` on fnx-classes is empty and the harness is exactly as committed.

WHAT I TRIED. Two arms calling the REAL `add_edge_with_attrs` on workloads chosen to do strictly
less work, so nothing had to be reimplemented:

    full       grows the graph      -> autocreation + new edge + ledger
    preseeded  nodes pre-created    -> new edge + ledger
    duplicate  edge already present -> `changed` false: no adjacency push, no revision bump

with `full - preseeded` = autocreation and `preseeded - duplicate` = new-edge bookkeeping.

IT IS WRONG, and the arithmetic said so immediately:

    add_edge, nodes preseeded     479.2 ns/edge
    add_edge, edge already there  393.3 ns/edge
    -> endpoint autocreation      -69.4 ns/edge     <-- NEGATIVE

A component cannot cost negative time. The confound: the arms do not differ only by the work I meant
to isolate, they differ by NODE-MAP SIZE. `full` grows from empty, so at edge i it probes an IndexMap
of i+1 entries; `preseeded` and `duplicate` probe a full 20,001-entry map from their first iteration.
The larger map costs more per lookup than autocreation saves. Workload choice cannot isolate
autocreation, because the workload difference IS the map growth — that separation needs
instrumentation inside the function, not a different input.

THE INSTRUMENT FINDING, which is the part to carry. Adding those two arms moved the UNTOUCHED
denominator by about 20%:

    with the two extra arms present   add_edge_with_attrs  409.8 ns/edge
    after reverting them (3 runs)                          507.5 / 515.1 / 506.9 ns/edge

Same code, same host, same load band, only the arm set differs. The arms in `ledger_record_cost_ab`
are NOT independent: each one allocates and frees whole graphs and ledgers, so the ones that follow
run against a differently warmed allocator. Consequences, all of which apply to figures already on
this bead:

  * A share read WITHIN one run is fine — that is why A1/full = 34.9% stands, it was taken with the
  committed arm set and both numbers came from the same invocation.
  * Comparing ABSOLUTE ns across runs with DIFFERENT arm sets is invalid. The same run that gave the
  bogus -69.4 also reported the share as 44.0% rather than 34.9%, purely from the denominator moving.
  * Anyone who adds an arm must re-baseline every figure quoted off this harness, not just read the
  new arm.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY DECOMPOSE THE STORAGE HALF, for whoever takes it: instrument inside
`add_edge_with_attrs` (a cfg-gated timer or a counted-work probe around the autocreation branch, the
edge entry, and the adjacency push) rather than trying to construct workloads that differ by one
component. Everything cheap has been ruled out; the remaining ~330 ns of non-ledger work in a ~507 ns
call is real, and it needs a finer instrument than input selection.

STANDING FIGURES UNCHANGED by this: add_edge_with_attrs ~507 ns/edge, ledger 34.9%, and the
Python-side 0.46-0.50x range with the shim at 332.6 ns / 26.5%.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
THE INSTRUMENT THIS BEAD WAS BLOCKED ON, BUILT AND RUN (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit eaf8da86b. Bead stays OPEN — this supplies the instrument, it does not answer the question.

WHY IT IS COUNTED WORK. CopperCliff's last entry named the blocker exactly: perf_event_paranoid=4 on this host, cfg-gated timers are a large fraction of a ~500 ns function, and the ledger_record_cost_ab arms are not independent (adding two arms moved the untouched denominator ~20%). His recommendation was counted work rather than time. crates/fnx-classes/tests/mutation_allocation_census.rs is that. It ran at load 158/64 and produced byte-identical numbers in debug and release — a state in which no timing arm on this bead would have been admissible.

WHERE THE UNSAFE WENT, since fnx-classes carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]: an integration test is its own crate root and is not bound by that attribute, so the counting allocator lives in tests/ and the library keeps its guarantee. Four GlobalAlloc methods bump a relaxed counter and forward to System unchanged.

MEASURED, min over 9 rounds x 2000 calls, every arm steady-state on an EXISTING node/edge so nothing is inserted and no map grows — the ~90% of the call this bead measured at 538.2 ns no-op vs 58.0 ns insert:

  add_edge_with_attrs, existing edge   6.000 allocs/call
  add_node_with_attrs, existing node   3.000 allocs/call
  has_node (read control)              0.000 allocs/call
  caller-built AttrMap (charged in)    2.000 allocs/call
  add_node_with_attrs, pre-owned key   2.000 allocs/call
  -> add_edge entry, caller attrs out  4.000 allocs/call
  -> owned key per endpoint            1.000 allocs/call

GRADED BY HOW FIRMLY ESTABLISHED, because this bead has been burned seven times by readings presented as mechanisms:

1. MEASURED. The read control allocates NOTHING — has_node shares key handling with both mutators and costs zero allocations, so everything below is the mutators' own. An owned node key costs EXACTLY ONE allocation: arm 5 pre-builds every key outside the counted window, so the gap to arm 2 is that key and nothing else. Discriminator, not reading.

2. ARITHMETIC ON MEASUREMENTS. add_edge entry 4 = 2 endpoint keys + 2. add_node entry 3 = 1 endpoint key + 2. The SAME residue of 2 on a one-endpoint and a two-endpoint call — the shape of a per-CALL cost independent of endpoint count, which is the shape this bead's 538 ns no-op has always demanded.

3. A READING THAT FITS, EXPLICITLY NOT CLAIMED. Those 2 are consistent with the CGSE record's evidence Vec plus the one genuinely dynamic edge_attr_count/attrs_count.to_string(). NOT an attribution. The clean discriminator would be an arm reaching the SAME function with the record suppressed; extend_nodes_unrecorded is a different function that skips other work too, so it would repeat the inconclusive batch-vs-loop comparison already withdrawn on this bead. Whoever takes it should add a cfg-gated no-record path to add_node_with_attrs rather than switch functions.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE BEAD. The residual is no longer "a fixed per-call cost of roughly 500 ns" with an unknown composition. On the allocation axis the entry is fully accounted: keys are 1 each and measured, everything else is 2 per call and independent of endpoint count. Two obvious levers now have a countable acceptance test rather than a timing one — a small-int static table for the count to_string() (byte-identical output, kills 1 alloc on BOTH mutators), and avoiding the owned key on the write path (the bead already notes add_edge canonicalises to an owned String because it needs one to insert). Either can be accepted or rejected by re-running this census at any host load.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: no timing, no ratio, no incumbent arm, so nothing here is a perf claim or campaign output. add_edge remains a decisive loss vs nx at 0.46-0.50x.

IT ALSO LOCKS br-r37-c1-g2nev. The assertions are exact counts, not ceilings, so any allocation ADDED to the mutation entry fails them. A single pre-g2nev add_edge record materialised 14 owned Strings; restoring .to_owned() on any constant evidence field now fails this test even though the recorded VALUE would be unchanged and every parity assertion would still pass.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes --test mutation_allocation_census green in debug AND release (identical figures), cargo clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, cargo fmt --check clean.

comments.text:
FIRST LEVER TAKEN OFF THE CENSUS, AND IT SETTLES THE READING I REFUSED TO CLAIM (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit e65041030. Bead stays OPEN.

Last entry I reported the entry's allocations as 4 (add_edge) / 3 (add_node), graded them, and put "the residue of 2 is the evidence Vec plus the count to_string()" in the READING THAT FITS bucket rather than claiming it — this bead has been burned seven times by readings presented as mechanisms, so it needed an arm, not an argument.

count_evidence is that arm AND the lever at the same time. It borrows the ledger's count values from a 0..=32 table of decimal literals (owned String past it, so batch counts behave as before). Re-running the census:

                                        before   after
  add_edge_with_attrs, existing edge     6.000   5.000  allocs/call
  add_node_with_attrs, existing node     3.000   2.000  allocs/call
  add_edge entry, caller attrs out       4.000   3.000  allocs/call
  owned key per endpoint                 1.000   1.000
  has_node (read control)                0.000   0.000

The residue went 2 -> 1. So the removed allocation WAS the count's to_string(), and the survivor IS the record's evidence Vec. That is now measured, not read: one arm changed one thing, and the census is byte-identical in debug and release at any host load.

WHERE THAT LEAVES THE ENTRY. Fully accounted on the allocation axis:
  add_edge entry 3 = 2 owned endpoint keys + 1 evidence Vec
  add_node entry 2 = 1 owned endpoint key  + 1 evidence Vec
Both remaining terms are named, measured, and each has an acceptance test that runs at any load. That is a different position from "a fixed per-call cost of roughly 500 ns" of unknown composition, which is where this bead sat for its whole life.

THE TWO REMAINING ALLOCATION LEVERS, in the order I would take them:
  1. The evidence Vec — one per call on BOTH mutators, so it is the larger prize. A fixed-capacity inline container would remove it; the obvious crate for that is a dependency, and dependency smuggling is a named forbidden pattern here, so it wants either an in-tree small-vec sized to the 2-and-4-term records the mutators actually build, or a records() API that takes terms by slice. Not obviously cheap; scope it before starting.
  2. The owned endpoint key. The bead already records WHY it is owned — the write path needs an owned String to insert, unlike the read path's borrowed with_node_key_str, which is exactly why has_node measures 0.000 allocs and add_node measures 1. Removing it is the node-key interning question, which is fenced by the CloudyTurtle HOLD.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: no timing, no ratio, no incumbent arm. One allocation of four is maintenance, and add_edge remains a decisive loss vs nx at 0.46-0.50x. Nothing here is campaign output.

A METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING, because it is the reason this entry is short. The census's exact-count assertions FAILED when the lever landed, before I updated them. That is what a real detector does — a ceiling would have swallowed the change silently. They were then updated DOWNWARD (4->3, 3->2): the budget tightened because the code improved, which is the opposite of relaxing a gate to admit a change.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (92 lib + census, 0 failed), -p fnx-runtime (130, 0 failed), census green in debug AND release with identical figures, clippy/fmt clean, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean. Byte-identity checked across 0..200 by count_evidence_matches_usize_to_string_and_borrows_small_values, including past the table where it must still allocate.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
SECOND LEVER OFF THE CENSUS — add_node NO LONGER OWNS ITS KEY (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit 738e646a5. Bead stays OPEN.

Graph::add_node_with_attrs_unrecorded opened with `let node = node.into();`, so a &str caller allocated an owned String on EVERY call — including the calls that insert nothing, where it existed only to probe the map and was dropped by `entry` on the occupied branch. It now probes borrowed and owns only on the vacant path. MultiGraph's was worse and simpler: it built an owned String purely to hand set_node_attrs a borrow, since that method already takes &str and owns internally only when it inserts; that .into() is gone outright.

                                        before   after
  add_node_with_attrs, existing node     2.000   1.000  allocs/call
  owning the key costs (arm 2 - arm 5)   1.000   0.000
  add_edge entry, caller attrs out       3.000   3.000  (unchanged)
  has_node (read control)                0.000   0.000

Arm 5 reading 0.000 is the confirmation, not an inference: handing the call a &str and handing it a ready-made String now cost the same because neither allocates. The arm is kept so a nonzero reading flags a regression.

WHERE THE ENTRY NOW STANDS on the allocation axis, all measured:
  add_node, existing node : 1 = the record's evidence Vec
  add_edge, existing edge : 3 = 2 owned endpoint keys + the evidence Vec

add_edge IS UNCHANGED and I am not implying otherwise. It owns both endpoint keys in its OWN preamble (`let left = left.into(); let right = right.into();`), not via add_node, so that is a separate edit inside a CGSE-critical function — the same borrow-probe shape, but it must survive the self-loop compare, edge_pair_key, the autocreation branch and the outcome record, all of which currently consume owned Strings. Worth doing, wants a scoped pass, roughly 2 of add_edge's 3.

DECLINED, WITH REASONS, so nobody re-derives it: recycling the retired records' evidence Vec. It is mechanically possible with no dependency — retirement currently frees those Vecs inside `retain`, and `retain_mut` could harvest them into a pool instead, with the pool taken out of `self` first to satisfy the borrow checker. I did not take it. EvidenceLedger derives Serialize/Deserialize/PartialEq, so a pool field puts unobservable state into an audit type and needs #[serde(skip)] plus a hand-written PartialEq, all to remove one allocation worth roughly 2% of add_edge. That fails the no-tech-debt bar for a CGSE structure. If someone disagrees, the census gives an exact acceptance test — but weigh the ledger's cleanliness first.

WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS BEAD, ordered:
  1. add_edge's two endpoint keys (above) — the largest remaining allocation item, and the only one with a clean shape.
  2. The evidence Vec — declined above; revisit only with a design that keeps EvidenceLedger's derives honest.
  3. Everything non-allocation. The census bounds the ALLOCATION axis only. add_edge is ~1245 ns end-to-end and three allocations do not explain that, so the next axis (map probes, the attr extend, the revision/token bump) still wants its own instrument. Counted work worked here; something similar for probe counts would keep the load-independence.

NOT A PERF CLAIM: no timing, no ratio, no incumbent arm. add_edge remains a decisive loss vs nx at 0.46-0.50x.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (92 lib + census, 0 failed), census green in debug AND release with identical figures, clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, fmt clean, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean (confirms no caller relied on the old `impl Into<String>`-only bound).

comments.text:
THE ALLOCATION AXIS OF THIS BEAD'S ENTRY PATH IS CLOSED (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit 27b00d650. Bead stays OPEN, and the last section says why that is not a formality.

add_edge_with_attrs opened with `let left = left.into(); let right = right.into();` and then handed `left.clone()` / `right.clone()` to autocreation — up to four owned Strings per call, none of which the function keeps. Every use of the keys is a comparison, a map probe, or a forward to add_node_with_attrs_unrecorded, and that callee (738e646a5) now owns the key only on the vacant path. Keys stay borrowed; the one allocation an insert genuinely needs happens inside the callee, exactly when a node is created.

                                        before   after
  add_edge_with_attrs, existing edge     5.000   3.000  allocs/call
  add_edge entry, caller attrs out       3.000   1.000  allocs/call
  add_node entry                         1.000   1.000
  has_node (read control)                0.000   0.000

ACROSS THE THREE LEVERS on this bead, entry allocations per steady-state call:
  add_edge  4 -> 3 (count_evidence) -> 3 -> 1 (endpoint keys)
  add_node  3 -> 2 (count_evidence) -> 1 (key) -> 1
Both mutators now sit at exactly ONE allocation, and it is the same one: the decision record's evidence Vec. The 3.000 still showing on add_edge is 2 caller-built AttrMap allocations, which the census charges to the caller, not the entry.

THAT ONE REMAINING ALLOCATION IS THE ONE I DECLINED, and the reasoning stands unchanged from 738e646a5: removing it means recycling the evidence Vec that retirement currently frees, and EvidenceLedger derives Serialize/Deserialize/PartialEq, so a pool field puts unobservable state into an audit type for ~2% of add_edge. Three of this bead's levers have now landed against a measure that was never the cost — they are justified as provable removals of work, and none of them is a perf claim, but nobody should read "entry is down to 1 allocation" as "the entry is cheap". What now dominates is unmeasured: the String-keyed IndexMap probes (add_edge does contains_key + get_index_of per endpoint plus an edges entry, all hashing the key), the attr extend, and the revision/token bump.

A probe COUNTER (hash lookups per call) built the same way would attribute the map work without needing quiescence. comments.text:
ENDPOINT DOUBLE-PROBE REMOVED (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit ab8949e1e. Bead stays OPEN. Read the LIMITS section — it matters more than the change.

Closing the allocation axis made the next thing visible without needing the probe counter I proposed last entry: add_edge_with_attrs hashed each endpoint key TWICE against the same map. contains_key decided whether to autocreate, then get_index_of fetched the index a few lines later, and get_index_of already answers both questions. Each endpoint is now resolved by ONE get_index_of, autocreating on the None arm. A self-loop does not probe the second endpoint at all: left == right makes the indices equal by construction.

  steady-state, non-self-loop : 4 String hashes -> 2
  self-loop                   : 3 -> 1

Same class as the double-lookup CopperCliff removed from this same function, and the same justification: a PROVABLE REMOVAL of redundant work, not a measured win.

LIMITS, stated plainly because four levers have now landed on this bead against measures that were never the cost:
  * I am NOT quoting a number for this. Load was 116/64, and the allocation census — the only load-independent instrument on this bead — does not measure probes. It appears in the verification only as a CONTROL: 3.000/1.000, unchanged, confirming no allocations moved.
  * The probe counter I proposed last entry is still unbuilt, and it is still the right instrument. I skipped it because this particular redundancy was provable by reading the two calls; a counter is needed for the rest (the edges entry pair, the attr extend, the revision/token bump), which are NOT provable by inspection.
  * Nothing here changes that add_edge is ~1245 ns end-to-end. Four allocations and two hashes do not explain that number, and no one should read this sequence of landings as converging on it.

CGSE NON-REGRESSION was the delicate part, not a formality. Resolving the left endpoint EARLY is only safe because IndexMap appends, so autocreating the right endpoint cannot move the left index; the left endpoint is still resolved and autocreated first; and the self-loop branch still reports right_autocreated as a copy of left_autocreated.

NEW TEST add_edge_endpoint_resolution_preserves_autocreation_and_order locks precisely what the edit restructured, read off the ledger evidence that carries it: self-loop that creates its node (true/true, one node), self-loop on an existing node (false/false, nothing added), left-exists-right-new (false/true), both-new (true/true), plus node indices 0..3 in left-then-right insertion order. It discriminates: writing `true` into the self-loop branch, or resolving right before left, fails it.

STATE OF THIS BEAD AFTER FOUR LANDINGS. Entry allocations per steady-state call went 4 -> 1 (add_edge) and 3 -> 1 (add_node), both now the decision record's evidence Vec, which was scoped and declined. Endpoint probes 4 -> 2. What is still unmeasured and now dominant: the self.edges contains_key + entry pair (integer-keyed, so cheaper but still doubled), the attr extend, the revision/token bump, and whatever the PyO3 boundary adds above all of it. The probe counter is the unblocked next step.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (93 lib incl. the new test + census, 0 failed), census unchanged in debug AND release, clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, fmt clean, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean.

comments.text:

I added DiGraph arms to the allocation census BEFORE touching digraph.rs, and they read the undirected pair's PRE-lever numbers:

  DiGraph add_edge entry           3.000   1.000  allocs/call
  DiGraph add_node, existing node  2.000   1.000  allocs/call

APPLIED, all three: borrowed-key probe with ownership only on the vacant path in add_node_with_attrs_unrecorded; both endpoint keys borrowed in add_edge_with_attrs (it used to own both AND clone each again for autocreation); one get_index_of per endpoint instead of contains_key + get_index_of, with a self-loop not probing the target at all.

STILL NOT MEASURED WINS. No timing, no ratio, no incumbent arm; load was 66/64. The census measures ALLOCATIONS and says nothing about the probe counts above — those are justified as provable removals of redundant work, same standing as the undirected ones.

CGSE: source still resolved and autocreated before target; IndexMap appends so autocreating the target cannot move the source index; self-loop still reports target_autocreated as a copy of source_autocreated.

NEW TEST digraph_add_edge_endpoint_resolution_preserves_autocreation_and_direction mirrors the undirected lock and adds the directed-only risk: has_edge asserted in BOTH directions. The succ/pred rows are now filled from reused indices, and swapping them would be invisible to every other assertion in the suite — that is the failure this test exists for.

NOT DONE, stated rather than left silent: MultiGraph and MultiDiGraph have the same shape (MDG's add_node_with_attrs_unrecorded at digraph.rs:2459 still opens with `let node = node.into();`) and have no census arm yet. Same recipe, same order — add the arms first, confirm they read the pre-lever numbers, then mirror.

WHAT HAS NOT CHANGED AFTER FIVE LANDINGS, and it is still the thing that matters on this bead: add_edge is ~1245 ns end-to-end and 0.46-0.50x vs nx. comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
NODE SIDE OF THE FAMILY COMPLETE, AND THE CENSUS FOUND A 4x OUTLIER (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit 9e8bd5c03. Bead stays OPEN.

Arms for MultiGraph and MultiDiGraph went in BEFORE any edit, same recipe as the directed pair:

                                  before   after
  MultiDiGraph add_node, existing  4.000   1.000  allocs/call
  MultiGraph add_node, existing    1.000   1.000  (already converted, confirmed)
  Graph / DiGraph add_node         1.000   1.000  (controls, unchanged)

MultiDiGraph was allocating FOUR times per call on a node that already exists, against three siblings at 1. I would not have predicted that from reading; the arm found it. Cause: entry() allocates its key eagerly whether or not the slot is vacant, and this function used entry() three times — node.into() for the probe, entry(node.clone()) for `nodes`, entry(node.clone()) for `successors`, original moved into `predecessors`. On an existing node all three were built only to be dropped.

The MultiGraph arm reading 1.000 unchanged is the other half of the same measurement's value: it confirms the NX150 conversion held, so this is not one family-wide assumption applied blind to four types.

ALL FOUR GRAPH TYPES ARE NOW AT 1.000 add_node allocations per call, and that one is the decision record's evidence Vec — the allocation I scoped and declined earlier for putting unobservable state into EvidenceLedger.

THE ROW SWAP IS THE REAL RISK IN THIS COMMIT, so it is worth naming: I replaced `entry(node.clone()).or_default()` on successors/predecessors with contains_key + insert-when-absent. I deliberately did NOT take the shortcut of skipping those rows whenever the node already exists — nothing here may assume every path that inserts into `nodes` also created the rows. A missing row would surface later as a LOST EDGE, not at the call, so multidigraph_add_node_creates_and_preserves_adjacency_rows exercises it: a node created by add_node (not by an edge) still gets usable successor AND predecessor rows; re-adding an existing node five times disturbs neither; parallel edges still accumulate afterwards.

WHAT REMAINS ON THE ALLOCATION AXIS: MultiGraph and MultiDiGraph add_edge_impl still own both endpoint keys, and neither has a census arm. Note for whoever takes it — their re-add path APPENDS a parallel edge rather than being a no-op, so the arm needs a different shape from arms 1/6 (which re-add an existing simple edge and mutate nothing). Copying the simple-graph arm would measure a growing graph and give a meaningless number.

WHAT HAS NOT MOVED after six landings, and it remains the honest headline of this bead: add_edge is ~1245 ns end-to-end and 0.46-0.50x vs nx. Allocations and probes are now well characterised and small; they do not explain that number. The probe counter is still unbuilt, and the dominant cost is still unattributed. Anyone picking this bead up for the ratio rather than for tidiness should build that instrument first rather than continue down the allocation axis.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (95 lib incl. the new test + census, 0 failed), census green in debug AND release with identical figures, clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, fmt clean, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
THE COST IS ATTRIBUTED. THE INSTRUMENT WAS INSTALLED ALL ALONG (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit 615b109c0. Bead stays OPEN, and two of my own conclusions are corrected below.

This bead has been blocked on an instrument since it was filed. CopperCliff recorded perf_event_paranoid=4 as killing sampling and cfg-gated timers as too coarse for a ~500 ns function. I added the allocation census, exhausted that axis over four commits, and wrote three times that the dominant cost was unattributed and someone should build a probe counter. Nobody, me included, checked for valgrind. It is installed — 3.25.1, with callgrind_annotate. Callgrind counts instructions by emulation, needs no privileges, and is immune to host load for exactly the reason the census is. The blocker was a missing CHECK, not a missing capability. Anyone who inherits a "no profiler on this host" claim on this fleet should verify it before building a bespoke counter, which is what I was about to do.

MEASURED: 100,000 steady-state add_edge calls, 204,734,119 Ir (~2,000 Ir/call), load 86/64 — a state in which no timing arm on this bead has ever been admissible. Self cost, grouped:

  allocator (malloc/free family, 8 entries)        ~25.7%
  attribute merge (BTreeMap insert/extend/drop)    ~17.7%
  add_edge_with_attrs itself                        17.4%
  CGSE ledger (record_decision + record + drop
    + clock + count_evidence)                      ~15.3%
  node-map probes (get_index_of + memcmp)          ~14.1%
  edge-map probe + entry                            ~3.9%

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN ENTRIES ON THIS BEAD:

1. I called the allocation axis "exhausted" and warned repeatedly that it "was never the cost". WRONG on the second half. The allocator is the LARGEST single group at ~26% of instructions. The four allocation levers were better targeted than I credited. What is true is that the axis is no longer reachable from the ENTRY: what remains is the caller's AttrMap (a BTreeMap node plus its String key, allocated and freed per call) and the evidence Vec. Attacking those means changing what the caller hands in, or the ledger's shape — not another borrow-probe.

2. The attribute merge is ~18% and I never named it in six entries. edge_attrs.extend(attrs) plus dropping the consumed map is the second-largest group, paid on a call that merges one IDENTICAL key into an existing edge. Nobody has looked at whether the merge can early-out when the incoming map is a subset of the stored one — the equality scan that sets `changed` already walks both.

NEW AND PREVIOUSLY UNNAMED: the ledger reads the CLOCK on every record. sub_timespec is 1.78% of instructions, but a wall-clock read costs far more in TIME than in instruction count, so its share of the 1245 ns is plausibly several times that. It is NOT a free lever — ts_unix_ms is part of the audit record, so any change is a CGSE question first and a perf question second. Flagging, not proposing.

LIMITS: instruction counts are NOT time. No incumbent arm, no ratio, so this is not a perf claim. Cache behaviour and the clock read in particular are under-represented in Ir. This attributes SHAPE, and it is the first evidence on this bead that does.

Caveat: the binary carries the census's counting allocator (one relaxed increment per allocation). It appears as its own entry rather than distorting others, but the allocator group is a slight over-count.

RANKED NEXT STEPS, now on evidence instead of inspection:
  1. Attribute merge (~18%) — the largest untouched group and nobody has scoped it.
  2. The caller's AttrMap allocation pair, which is most of the ~26% allocator group and is a boundary-layer question, not an fnx-classes one.
  3. The clock read — CGSE ruling needed before any perf work.
  4. Node-map probes (~14%) are already at the 2 the operation requires; do not re-attack without a different data structure.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (95 lib + census, 0 failed, profile target correctly ignored), clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, fmt clean. add_edge remains 0.46-0.50x vs nx.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
I PROFILED THE WRONG WORKLOAD LAST ENTRY. CORRECTED, AND THE ANSWER CHANGES (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit 12ffb0285. Bead stays OPEN.

615b109c0 profiled add_edge_profile_target, which loops on an edge that ALREADY EXISTS, and I presented its group shares as the attribution for this bead. They are not. This bead's headline — 1245 ns/edge, 0.46-0.50x — was measured on a FRESH graph per timed unit, so nearly every call creates an edge and autocreates an endpoint. Steady-state re-add and build run through different branches (autocreation, adjacency growth, an empty attr map to merge into), and I transferred conclusions across workloads without flagging it. That is the same error class this bead has recorded twice before under other names.

add_edge_build_profile_target profiles the headline path directly. 100,000 NEW edges, 495,976,975 Ir (~4,960 Ir/edge, 2.5x the steady-state call):

  group                          BUILD      steady-state (615b109c0)
  allocator (malloc/free)       ~47.1%      ~25.7%
  node-map probes + entry       ~14.1%      ~14.1%
  attribute merge               ~12.0%      ~17.7%
  CGSE ledger                    ~5.1%      ~15.3%
  edge-map entry                 ~2.7%       ~3.9%

THE RESULT: on the workload behind 0.46-0.50x, roughly HALF of all instructions are inside glibc malloc/free. malloc_consolidate alone is 5.61% and is ABSENT from the steady-state profile — that is heap coalescing, the signature of churning many small blocks per edge.

RE-RANKING MY OWN NEXT STEPS, which were derived from the inflated steady-state shares:
  * The CGSE ledger is ~5% on the build path, not ~15%. I flagged the per-record clock read as a candidate needing a CGSE ruling; at 5% for the whole ledger it is not worth opening that question. WITHDRAWN.
  * The attribute merge is ~12%, not ~18%, and it was my #1. It also has a semantic trap I found while scoping it: skipping the merge when the pre-scan reports no difference is NOT byte-identical, because CgseValue equality does not imply indistinguishability for floats (+0.0 == -0.0 compares equal but replacing changes the stored sign). Anyone taking it must handle that; it is not the free early-out it looks like.
  * The node-map probes are unchanged at ~14% and already at the 2 the operation requires. Still do not re-attack.

WHERE THE REAL PROBLEM IS. Per NEW edge this path allocates: the caller's AttrMap (a BTreeMap node plus its key String), the owned node key on autocreation, the adjacency row Vec, the per-edge BTreeMap the attrs merge into, and the evidence Vec — then frees the caller's map again. That is a BTreeMap-per-edge storage shape meeting glibc malloc, against nx's dict plus CPython's pooled small-object allocator. This is a storage-shape question and belongs with br-r37-c1-node-storage-materialization-wall-5fije and br-r37-c1-weighted-attr-rust-store-237hw, NOT another micro-lever inside add_edge. Six of my seven landings on this bead were micro-levers; this profile says the seventh should not be.

LIMITS: instruction counts are not time; no incumbent arm; not a perf claim. The 9.74% {closure#0} entry is add_edge_with_attrs INLINED into the test loop together with the caller's AttrMap construction, so I cannot separate fnx's share from the harness's inside it and am NOT quoting an "add_edge itself" figure for the build path. The binary carries the counting allocator, so the allocator group is a slight over-count.

BOTH TARGETS ARE COMMITTED AND REPEATABLE at any host load:
  cargo test -p fnx-classes --release --test mutation_allocation_census --no-run
  valgrind --tool=callgrind --callgrind-out-file=cg.out <binary> add_edge_build_profile_target --ignored --exact
  callgrind_annotate cg.out

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (95 lib + census, 0 failed, both targets correctly ignored), clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, fmt clean.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
FIRST LEVER OFF THE BUILD-PATH PROFILE, WITH A MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit 7b002c800. Bead stays OPEN.

Every previous landing on this bead was justified as a provable removal of redundant work, because nothing on this host could measure them. This one has an actual before/after, because callgrind gives instruction counts and those are decidable at any load.

THE LEVER: on a NEW edge the attribute bucket is empty, yet edge_attrs.extend(attrs) inserted the caller's entries one at a time into a freshly allocated destination and then dropped the caller's map. When the destination is empty the caller's map IS the answer, so it is moved in whole.

MEASURED, add_edge_build_profile_target, 100,000 new edges, same binary and invocation before and after, load ~86/64:

  Ir total   495,976,975 -> 471,956,779   -24,020,196   1.0509x
  per edge         4,960 ->       4,720   -240 Ir/edge
  BTreeMap IntoIter drop  27.6M -> 19.2M

BYTE-IDENTICAL: extending an EMPTY BTreeMap by attrs yields attrs, and BTreeMap orders by key either way. `changed` agrees — the scan being replaced reports every key of a non-empty attrs as missing from an empty bucket, and is skipped entirely when attrs is empty, which is exactly the two cases the new branch sets.

PINNED, not argued: add_edge_fresh_bucket_take_matches_merge_semantics covers the four bucket-state/incoming-attrs combinations the branch splits, including the non-obvious one — an edge that ALREADY EXISTS but carries no attributes still takes the empty-bucket branch on a later attributed add — plus that a non-empty bucket still merges and a differing value still overwrites rather than being lost to the take.

NOT APPLIED TO MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph, deliberately. Same shape at digraph.rs:2734 and :2886, but their `attrs` sits inside a loop where it may be reused or cloned per iteration, so the move is not obviously valid. This session has already produced two corrections from transferring a conclusion across contexts (the DiGraph levers that had not transferred, and profiling the wrong workload); I am not making it three. Whoever takes those should check the loop's ownership first — and note that if a clone IS involved, the clone is the bigger waste than the extend.

SCALE, stated plainly so nobody over-reads it: 4.84% of instructions on the build path. The same profile puts ~47% inside malloc/free, and this removes ONE alloc/free pair of several per edge. It does not change the standing conclusion that the remainder is a storage-shape question — BTreeMap-per-edge against nx's dict plus CPython's pooled small-object allocator — belonging to br-r37-c1-node-storage-materialization-wall-5fije and br-r37-c1-weighted-attr-rust-store-237hw rather than to another edit inside add_edge.

NOT A PERF CLAIM vs nx: instruction counts are not time, no incumbent arm, no ratio. add_edge remains 0.46-0.50x.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (96 lib incl. the new test + census, 0 failed), clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, fmt clean, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
MDG FRESH-BUCKET TAKE LANDED, AND THE PROFILE FOUND A BIGGER FISH (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09), commit c63ed8e7f. Bead stays OPEN.

This closes the loop 7b002c800 left open. That commit applied the take to Graph and DiGraph and explicitly did NOT apply it to the multigraphs because their `attrs` sits inside a loop and the move was not obviously valid. Checked, with three different answers:
  * digraph.rs:2744 — `for (source_idx, target_idx, key, attrs) in edges`, so attrs is destructured from the iterator item and OWNED per iteration. The move IS valid, but it is a batch path with its own `changed` accounting; left for a scoped pass rather than folded in.
  * digraph.rs:2896 — MultiDiGraph::add_edge_impl, attrs is the function's own owned parameter, identical shape to DiGraph. TAKEN.
  * MultiGraph::add_edge_impl (lib.rs:4766) does not have this shape at all — it reads through an edge_attrs() accessor against slab storage and writes separately. The lever does not apply. Nothing to mirror, and anyone looking for symmetry there should stop.

MEASURED WITH ITS OWN ARM, not inherited. multidigraph_build_profile_target added and profiled before and after, same binary and invocation, 100,000 new edges:

  Ir total   1,574,436,059 -> 1,541,486,218   -32,949,841   1.0214x
  per edge          15,744 ->       15,415    -329 Ir/edge

Absolute saving per edge is LARGER than the simple graph's (-329 vs -240) while the ratio is smaller, because the MDG baseline is 3.3x heavier.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE LEVER: MultiDiGraph costs ~15,400 Ir per built edge against Graph's ~4,720 on the same workload, same measurement, same binary. A 3.3x gap between graph types on the same operation. Every lever taken on this bead — seven of them now — is worth 1-5% each; this is worth 230%. It is measurable today at any host load with the two committed targets, and nobody has attributed it. If one thing is picked up from this bead next, it should be that, not another edit inside add_edge.

BYTE-IDENTICAL by the same argument as the sibling. Pinned by multidigraph_fresh_bucket_take_matches_merge_semantics, which covers the multigraph-only risk that the take lands on the wrong parallel edge: two parallel edges between the same endpoints are asserted to keep their own distinct attributes, plus a keyed edge created with empty attrs taking the branch later, plus a non-empty bucket still merging.

WHERE THIS BEAD STANDS. On the build path the profile says ~47% of instructions are glibc malloc/free, and the levers I can reach from inside add_edge are individually worth a few percent. The remainder is a storage-shape question — BTreeMap-per-edge against nx's dict plus CPython's pooled small-object allocator — and belongs to br-r37-c1-node-storage-materialization-wall-5fije and br-r37-c1-weighted-attr-rust-store-237hw. add_edge remains 0.46-0.50x and none of this session's work changes that.

NOT A PERF CLAIM vs nx: instruction counts are not time, no incumbent arm.

VERIFY: cargo test -p fnx-classes (97 lib incl. the new test + census, 0 failed), clippy -p fnx-classes --all-targets clean, fmt clean, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
add_edge RE-MEASURED LIVE vs networkx ON HEAD — UNDECIDABLE TWICE, AND I AM NOT QUOTING THE POINT ESTIMATES (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). Bead stays OPEN.

This session landed ten fnx-classes levers on this bead's path, none of which had ever been measured against networkx. This is that measurement, and it refuses.

SUBSTRATE: balanced [A B B A A B B A] square, live networkx 3.6.1 in the SAME invocation, dual A/A nulls per arm, 21 rounds, fresh graph per timed slot (this bead's stated workload, 8000 edges), bootstrap median CI, taskset -c 40-47. Extension built from HEAD by maturin, loaded from the repo tree via PYTHONPATH: _fnx.abi3.so sha256 016b512e35fe25979fb29aa5c649701eb79a8acbd6cba21520c68b57afe85e87. Host load 79-88 of 64.

  attempt 1 (8 warm-ups, no settle)      ratio 0.9291x  nulls nx 0.9798 / fnx 0.8015  UNDECIDABLE
  attempt 2 (40 warm-ups, gc per slot)   ratio 0.9663x  nulls nx 1.0289 / fnx 1.0299  UNDECIDABLE

BOTH REFUSED. The fnx arm's A/A null was 0.8015 on the first attempt — the arm's early rounds ran 20% faster than its late rounds, which is heap drift across the run, exactly the non-stationarity the standing note on mutation/build arms describes. Forcing a full gc between slots and quadrupling the warm-up moved the null from 0.8015 to 1.0299, so the mechanism is confirmed and the mitigation works in the right direction, but 1.03 is still outside [0.98, 1.02] and the run is inadmissible.

I AM NOT QUOTING 0.9291x OR 0.9663x, and nobody else should either. They are what an inadmissible run produced. The reason to state them at all is that they are FAR from the 0.44-0.50x this bead carries, so the honest position is: this bead's headline is unverified on HEAD, in BOTH directions. It may have improved a lot; the substrate did not let me establish it.

The has_node square in the SAME invocations admitted cleanly (nulls 1.0001-1.0045, see br-r37-c1-p80x1.48), which is the control that says the substrate itself is sound and the refusal is specific to the build arm.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT, for whoever picks this up:
  * a genuinely quiet host — every attempt this session ran at load 79-88 of 64;
  * or drop the fresh-graph-per-slot shape, which is what makes the arm non-stationary, and use the scaling-shape test the standing note recommends for build arms instead of a ratio;
  * the gc-per-slot settle is worth keeping either way, it halved the null deviation.

WHAT IS ALREADY MEASURED AND DOES NOT NEED REDOING: the instruction-level picture, which is load-independent and decided cleanly — Graph build 4,720 Ir/edge, MultiGraph 7,563, MultiDiGraph 14,576, with ~47% of the simple-graph build inside glibc malloc/free. Those came from the committed callgrind targets and stand regardless of this refusal.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
add_edge HAS AN ADMISSIBLE LIVE-vs-nx ROW AT LAST — 0.8990x, NOT 0.44-0.50x (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change. Bead stays OPEN, but its headline is now wrong by roughly a factor of two and should be corrected before anyone plans work from it.

This bead's figure has been unverified on HEAD all session: I landed ten fnx-classes levers on its path, then refused three times trying to measure them, because a fresh graph per timed slot makes the arm non-stationary and the A/A null reads heap drift rather than the arm.

FIXED BY REMOVING THE CAUSE, not by estimating around it. Every timed slot now runs in its own process, so each starts from an identical fresh heap; startup and fixture construction are outside the timed region. Balanced square, dual A/A nulls, live networkx 3.6.1, all unchanged.

  run 1   0.8990x  CI95 [0.8885, 0.9137]   nulls 0.9837 / 1.0026   ADMISSIBLE
  run 2   0.8997x  CI95 [0.8859, 0.9168]   nulls 1.0006 / 0.9744   UNDECIDABLE (fnx null 0.9744, marginal)

  nx 1043.0-1047.4 ns/edge    fnx 1161.5-1165.5 ns/edge

Two runs agreeing to 0.001 with one admitting, against a headline of 0.44-0.50x. The in-process attempts earlier today, all inadmissible, put it at 0.9291/0.9663/0.9316/0.9464 — a different substrate, a different absolute, and the same conclusion: this row is somewhere near 0.90-0.95x, and nowhere near 0.44x.

WHAT I AM CLAIMING AND WHAT I AM NOT. One admitted run is weaker than the four-run agreement behind the has_node range, so treat 0.8990x as a single admitted point rather than an established range. What is solid is the refutation: five independent estimates across two substrates, none below 0.89, against a recorded 0.44-0.50x. Whoever updates the README row should re-run this rather than copy my number.

CAVEAT ON THE SUBSTRATE, stated because it changes interpretation: a fresh process per slot removes drift but every slot then pays cold-heap costs a long-running program pays once. Both arms pay equally so the ratio is fair, but absolutes are higher (fnx 1161 ns/edge here against 1030-1050 in-process) and this is the FRESH-PROCESS build ratio, not a warm steady-state one. That distinction matters for this bead specifically, because its 1245 ns/edge and 928 ns/edge figures came from the in-process shape.

WHERE THAT LEAVES THE BEAD. The instruction-level picture is unchanged and still the useful part: Graph build 4,720 Ir/edge with ~47% inside glibc malloc/free, and the entry down to one allocation and two probes per call after this session's levers. The remaining question is no longer "why is add_edge 0.44x" — it is not — but whether the ~0.90x residual is worth further work given the allocator dominance, which is a storage-shape question belonging to br-r37-c1-node-storage-materialization-wall-5fije.

description: fnx.dag_longest_path_length(G, weight='weight') returns the hop count instead of the summed edge weight when edge weights were set via add_weighted_edges_from or post-creation mutation G[u][v]['weight']=w. Repro: D=fnx.DiGraph(); D.add_weighted_edges_from([(0,1,5),(1,2,3)]); fnx.dag_longest_path_length(D,weight='weight') == 2 (nx: 8). On a branching DAG it returns 2 vs nx 20. The dag_longest_path wrapper is unaffected (pure-Python, reads G.pred). title: View materialization cache silently returned stale results on count-preserving rewires (revert of br-r37-c1-a2rxy)
description:
Last turn's br-r37-c1-a2rxy added a (node_count, edge_count) cache key to _materialize_filtered_view to speed up repeated algorithm calls on subgraph_view / reverse_view inputs. The cache produced correct results on add_node, remove_node, add_edge, remove_edge in isolation — but silently returned STALE materializations on COUNT-PRESERVING rewires:

  fg = fnx.Graph(); fg.add_edges_from([(0,1),(1,2),(2,3)])  # path
  fv = fnx.subgraph_view(fg, filter_node=lambda n: True)
  fnx.shortest_path_length(fv, 0, 3)  # = 3 (warms cache key (4,3))
  
  fg.remove_edge(1, 2); fg.add_edge(0, 3)  # rewire to direct shortcut
  fnx.shortest_path_length(fv, 0, 3)  # returns 3 from cache; nx returns 1

Revert the cache (correctness > perf).  Locked the no-cache behaviour via test_view_materialization_invalidates_on_count_preserving_rewire.

Filed br-r37-c1-mutseq as the proper fix: expose a Rust-side monotonic mutation counter (nodes_seq + new edges_seq) to Python so the cache key can be tuple(seq) and ANY mutation invalidates correctly.
notes: Reverted in same commit; regression test landed.

title: test: Weisfeiler-Lehman graph hash invariants + parity
description: WL graph hash defining invariants: isomorphism invariance (relabel -> same hash), discrimination (path/cycle/star/complete all distinct), iso-relabeling equal hash + nx parity for graph hash, subgraph hashes, iterations param. Oracle-free invariants distinct from differential parity. 32 cases.
close_reason: A PREDICTION THAT CAME BACK NEGATIVE, then the real gap. I picked this bead expecting the classic hash defect - a test that checks only INVARIANCE, which a constant hash satisfies. It is not there: test_wl_hash_discriminates_distinct_structures already requires four 5-node structures (path, cycle, star, complete) to produce four distinct hashes, so a constant hash fails. I also checked whether the sweep relabel permutation ever lands on the identity, which would make the invariance check vacuous for that draw: 0 of 30. Both recorded rather than dressed up as findings. THE ACTUAL GAP - ATTRIBUTES: node_attr and edge_attr were untested, and the existing discrimination test structurally CANNOT reach them, because it compares graphs that already differ in structure. Both are now covered on pairs that are structurally IDENTICAL and differ only in one attribute value: without the parameter the two hash EQUAL (so the pair is a genuine control), with the parameter they differ, and both hashes agree with live networkx 3.6.1. THE PARAMETER-IGNORED PROBLEM: iterations was checked only for parity at iterations=5. Parity cannot see a parameter being dropped - if fnx ignored it, it would still match networkx wherever networkx own default agreed, and the two would be wrong together. The hash is now required to VARY across iterations 1, 2, 3 and 5 (4 distinct values measured). This is the same reasoning I applied to depth_limit on br-r37-c1-rqipa: parity plus "the parameter changes the answer" are different claims and both are needed. DISCRIMINATION WIDENED: it ran on four named graphs only; it now runs over the random family for pairs whose degree sequences differ, which the first WL refinement round separates by construction - measured 434 such pairs across the family with 0 hash collisions before I wrote the assertion. Evidence: file 32 -> 65 passed, no skips; 403 passed across the WL family (weisfeiler_lehman_hash_parity). Crate-scoped and inline with a timeout cap; no background jobs left running. Committed 194e32f84, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check. Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: HITS non-deterministic on degenerate-singular-value graphs (matches nx algorithm, inherits nx random-v0 ambiguity)
description: NOT A BUG / known acceptable divergence. fnx.hits is byte-for-byte nx algorithm (svds(A,k=1,v0=nstart) then A@a). On NON-degenerate inputs (simple dominant singular value) fnx matches nx at machine precision (verified 1.7e-17, 0.0 across seeds). When A top singular value is DEGENERATE (multiplicity>1 — disconnected DiGraph/MultiDiGraph and some small symmetric structures), svds returns an arbitrary vector from the top singular SUBSPACE chosen by ARPACK random v0, so BOTH fnx AND nx are non-deterministic and emit negative/sign-flipped components varying run-to-run with global numpy RNG (verified nx.hits gives different values on repeated calls). Documented in fnx.hits docstring (br-r37-c1-hitsdegen). Do NOT force a deterministic vector (would diverge from nx random-v0 contract). Future gauntlet/probes should skip HITS on degenerate graphs. Found via directed/multi gauntlet seed 213.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of already-closed br-r37-c1-a0466 (HITS degenerate-singular-value non-determinism). Already documented in memory project_intentional_divergences.md and locked by tests/python/test_hits_wellconditioned_parity.py. Re-discovered via gauntlet before checking the intentional-divergences ledger. The docstring note (283ce8408, br-r37-c1-hitsdegen) is still a net positive (inline doc was previously only the karate note) but the bead is redundant.

title: fix(views): G.edges() raises KeyError when a private _node mapping is assigned; nx returns the edges
description:
Found while implementing br-r37-c1-93mx3, which it BLOCKS.

EXECUTED on Graph() with add_edge('a','b'), add_node('native'), then g._node = {'private': {'tag': 1}}:

    nx   list(g.edges(data=True))  -> [('a', 'b', {})]
    nx   list(g.edges())          -> [('a', 'b')]
    fnx  list(g.edges(data=True)) -> KeyError: 'private'
    fnx  list(g.edges())          -> KeyError: 'private'
    both len(g) == 1              (agree)
    both g.nodes(data=True) == [('private', {'tag': 1})]   (agree)

So the node view correctly reads the assigned override while the EDGE view crashes on it.

CAUSE, from the traceback: fnx's edge view enumerates node keys (which now come from the override) and then looks up each node's adjacency, so 'private' - a node that exists only in the assigned mapping and has no adjacency row - raises KeyError at python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:1784. networkx's EdgeView iterates _adj directly and never consults _node, so a node present in _node but absent from _adj simply contributes no edges.

WHY IT BLOCKS br-r37-c1-93mx3: that bead needs G.copy() to rebuild from the assigned _node like nx does. nx's copy is add_nodes_from(self._node.items()) followed by add_edges_from(self.edges(data=True)) - nodes from the override, edges from native adjacency, unioned (verified: nx yields nodes ['a','b','private'] and edges [['a','b']]). fnx's generic rebuild in _copy_preserving_insertion_order takes exactly that shape, so it cannot be reached while self.edges(data=True) raises.

FIX DIRECTION: make the edge view iterate the ADJACENCY mapping rather than the node list, matching nx. Note the perf constraint before touching it - the adjacency iteration is a heavily optimised path (see the br-r37-c1-edgesubcopy and br-edgekeyedbatch notes in _copy_preserving_insertion_order), so a naive rewrite risks a regression on a hot surface. Measure before and after.

TESTS THE FIX MUST CARRY: a node present only in an assigned _node contributes no edges and does not raise (all four graph classes); edges() / edges(data=True) / edges(keys=True) shapes; and the existing private-storage suite in tests/python/test_private_store_copy_parity.py must stay green.
close_reason: Fixed in 109130216: G.edges() now reads the adjacency rather than the node view, matching networkx on all four graph classes under an assigned _node. Two defects: _AssignedPrivateEdgeView._nbunch(None) iterated the node view (that view exists only for the private-storage case, so ordinary graphs and edge order are untouched), and MultiAdjacencyView.__getitem__ gated membership on the node view so adj['a'] raised for a node with a real row — fixing only the first turned the multigraph classes from raising to silently empty. G.adj[missing] still raises as nx does. The explicit-nbunch path is separately divergent and pre-existing, filed as br-r37-c1-wzypa rather than absorbed. 25 new tests; 9262 passed in the edge|adj|private|view selection.

title: perf(current_flow): move the edge-betweenness nx key ordering into the Rust kernel
description:
Follow-up to br-r37-c1-8n5ni (fixed in 2ea337143).

edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality's default solver='full' path calls
_fnx.edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality_nx_ordered_rust, whose name asserts it emits nx's key
order. It does not - it emitted [(1,2),(1,0),(2,0),(2,3),(0,3)] where nx emits
[(1,0),(0,3),(2,0),(1,2),(2,3)]. The Python wrapper now reorders the returned dict in O(E) using
G's edge order oriented by RCM rank.

WHY IT WAS FIXED IN PYTHON, not Rust: target/release/lib_fnx.so was the exact ELF the br-r37-c1-oe93x
measurement queue was running against, and rebuilding it mid-queue would have split the arms across
two binaries. That constraint is gone once that measurement lands.

WHAT TO DO: emit the correct order inside the kernel and drop the wrapper reorder. The ordering rule
is stated exactly in the wrapper comment and is verified against nx on path, star, complete, barbell,
chorded-cycle and string-labelled fixtures.

COST OF LEAVING IT: one O(E) dict rebuild per call, against an O(V^3)-ish dense solve - almost
certainly unmeasurable. This is tidiness plus removing a misleading kernel name, NOT a perf
regression to chase. Do not spend a measurement window on it without first showing the rebuild is
visible at all.

GUARD ALREADY IN PLACE: tests/python/test_current_flow_key_order_parity.py parametrizes all three
solvers, so a kernel-side fix that regresses the order fails immediately.

title: test: assortativity parity + degree-assortativity==Pearson invariant
description: degree_assortativity_coefficient == degree_pearson_correlation_coefficient invariant (definitionally identical) + nx parity for degree/numeric/attribute assortativity + average_neighbor_degree. NaN-aware. 90 cases.
close_reason: THE PARAMETER HEURISTIC AGAIN, and it found three unexercised parameters. NOTHING IN THIS FILE BUILDS A DIGRAPH, so the x/y parameters of degree_assortativity_coefficient - which select four distinct directed coefficients (out/out, out/in, in/out, in/in) - were entirely unexercised. All four now compared against live networkx 3.6.1, WITH a guard asserting the four settings genuinely give four different values on the same graph: measured -0.666667, -0.612372, -0.408248, -0.375000, four distinct. Parity across four aliases of one number would prove nothing, which is why the guard matters. WEIGHT was never passed either, and by the reasoning I have now applied on four beads (depth_limit, iterations, wf_improved, and here), parity alone cannot see a parameter both libraries ignore - so the weighted coefficient must also DIFFER from the unweighted one. Same for average_neighbor_degree(weight=). Also added average_neighbor_degree(nodes=), which restricts the returned keys. CHECKED AND NOT A FINDING, recorded because it was my first hypothesis: the helper _close returns True when BOTH values are NaN, which would make every parity assertion in the file vacuous on a family where the coefficients are undefined - a real risk, since assortativity is NaN on regular graphs. Measured: NaN on 0 of 30 draws for degree, numeric and attribute assortativity alike. The existing comparisons are real and I left them alone. TWO OF MY OWN PROBE WITNESSES WERE BAD and I replaced them rather than reporting what they said: I first tested weight= on a 4-cycle, which is 2-regular, so the unweighted coefficient was NaN and the weighted one 0.0 - the comparison was meaningless; and I tested average_neighbor_degree(weight=) with an attribute the graph did not have, so it silently defaulted to 1 and showed no difference. Both redone on a non-regular graph carrying real weights, where the weighted coefficient is -0.363636 against -0.666667 unweighted. Evidence: file 90 -> 126 passed, no skips (the pre-existing too-few-edges guard fires 0 of 30); 352 passed across the assortativity family (assortativity_scalars_parity, assortativity_extensions_parity, assortativity_vectorized_parity). Crate-scoped and inline with a timeout cap; no background jobs left running. Committed cba4106ec, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check. Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: test: clustering-coefficient identities (clustering<->triangles<->transitivity)
description: Clustering identities cross-checking clustering/triangles/transitivity/degree: local clustering(v)=2*triangles(v)/(deg*(deg-1)); transitivity=3*triangles/triads; average_clustering=mean(local); sum(triangles)=3*total; range [0,1]; K_n clustering=1. Oracle-free cross-function identities. ~84 cases.
close_reason: The headline identity was checked against a total DERIVED FROM ITSELF. test_transitivity_and_average_clustering computed triangles_total = sum(triangles.values()) // 3 and then asserted sum(triangles.values()) == 3 * triangles_total, which reduces to 'the sum is divisible by 3' - satisfied by any multiple of 3, so the stated identity sum_v triangles(v) == 3T was never tested against an independent T. MUTANT, measured: multiplying every per-node triangle count by 3 keeps the sum divisible by 3 and passes the old check on 31/31 draws that have any triangle; the new independent enumeration oracle (direct combinations over node triples, computed without calling fnx.triangles) rejects it 31/31. The real identity holds 40/40 with 31 draws carrying at least one triangle, so the oracle is discriminating rather than vacuously agreeing on zeros. Added: the independent triangle oracle wired into the existing identity; the scalar and nbunch code paths clustering(G,v), triangles(G,v) and triangles(G,nbunch) agreeing with the dict forms (320/320 node checks across 40 seeds, 185 of those nodes carrying a triangle, plus 40/40 nbunch subsets); the K_n closed form T == C(n,3) for n=3..6; and the count_zeros=False contract for average_clustering, which changes the DENOMINATOR to the number of non-zero values and is undefined when every value is zero. On that last one I checked for a parity bug rather than assuming: fnx raises ZeroDivisionError on all-zero-clustering graphs, and so does live networkx 3.6.1 - 0 mismatches across all 40 seeds including the raising ones - so it is pinned as a contract in both directions, not reported as a defect. Evidence: file 81 -> 165 passed, no skips; 337 passed across the clustering family (clustering, cluster_module_parity, adjacency_walk_counting). Crate-scoped to those tests, not a workspace run.
