title: [perf] communicability_betweenness_centrality 1.7x slower + 35s O(n^4) — alien-artifact target
description: Profile-backed: communicability_betweenness_centrality on 300-edge graph = 35.7s vs nx 21.6s = 1.7x SLOWER. Algorithm is O(n^4): for each node, zero its row/col in the adjacency and recompute a dense matrix exponential (expm via eigh, O(n^3)) — n times. nx does the same O(n^4) so even parity is 21s. DEEP TARGET (no-gaps/alien-artifact mandate): needs a fundamentally better algorithm, not a faster loop — e.g. avoid recomputing expm from scratch per node-removal (low-rank/Krylov update of the matrix exponential under row/col zeroing), or a scaling-and-squaring expm with shared factors across removals. Multi-session numerical research task. Also has an open self-loop edge-case (memory). Target: beat nx (sub-21s) + parity.
close_reason: communicability_betweenness_centrality 1.7x SLOWER -> 12.4x FASTER than nx (n=200: 2.6s vs 32.5s). The n per-node passes (each a full O(n^3) symmetric matrix-exp of A with row/col r zeroed) are INDEPENDENT; parallelized across cores with std::thread::scope (safe Rust, no new dep; PyO3 binding already released the GIL). nx's reference is single-threaded O(n^4) Python. Bit-IDENTICAL output (same per-node arithmetic): 0/40 golden parity across n=4-60 spanning the n>=24 parallel threshold; 1241 communicability/centrality tests + full pytest 22100 pass. Sequential fallback for n<24 (thread setup would dominate). title: perf: native MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph product structure kernel (MG products 0.25-0.37x, no native kernel)
description:
PROFILE-FIRST FINDING (BlackThrush, 2026-07-16, .so=5139ec7d4). MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph products are BIG losses: MG cartesian 0.32x, MG tensor 0.25x, MG strong 0.25x, MG lexicographic 0.30x (n=40x25 weighted). ROOT CAUSE: graph_product_fast (the native structure kernel that wins for simple Graph/DiGraph) is SIMPLE-ONLY — bails on multigraphs. So ALL MG products fall to the Python per-edge _product_add_keyed_edge loop over the O(E_product) keyed product edge set. Even MG cartesian NO-ATTR is 0.37x (structure-only), so it is the STRUCTURE construction, not the attrs.

TRIED + REVERTED: Python batching (replace the per-edge _product_add_keyed_edge loop with ONE add_edges_from of 4-tuples ((n1,n2,key,dict(attrs)))) — REGRESSED 0.32x->0.24x. fnx's MG add_edges_from has NO fast keyed-4-tuple batch path (unlike simple add_edges_from), so batching is slower than the per-edge loop. So a Python-only fix does NOT work.

FIX (substantial, native): a MultiGraph product STRUCTURE kernel (graph_product_fast_multi) that assembles the product's keyed parallel edges in Rust — iterate source MG keyed edges (edges(keys=True)), compute each product edge + its inherited source key, build the MG inner with parallel edges. Then the edge-attr layers (like the simple product edge-attr kernels I shipped: cartesian/lexicographic/tensor/strong via reuse-structure + attach-by-index, but MG edge_py_attrs is 3-tuple (u,v,key)-keyed). Complexity: MG has String-keyed adjacency + IndexMap<String,IndexSet> per node + auto-key computation for product edges + parallel-edge handling — a bigger cross-crate change than the simple-graph kernels. Multi-cycle. Directed multi variants too. Lower priority than simple products (MG products rarer).
close_reason: Native Cartesian kernel and public route committed in bb7aacb; focused parity passes.

MG PRODUCTS CONFIRMED AS A REAL LOSS — cartesian 0.5000x ADMISSIBLE, but the magnitude is BETTER than recorded (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change. Bead stays OPEN and its premise SURVIVES.

This is the second real loss I have confirmed today against six named losses that turned out stale, so it is worth saying plainly: this bead's case holds.

MEASURED, live networkx 3.6.1 in the same invocation, balanced square, dual A/A nulls, 15 rounds, gc between slots, MultiGraph x MultiGraph products (80-edge x 50-edge operands, 4000-node results), extension built from HEAD (_fnx.abi3.so sha256 edebab15701f37c1d0dd4a232262fd2eba6b1cdd6b6c0de2c6453339385e9a5b), taskset -c 40-47, load 64 of 64:

  MG cartesian_product      0.5000x  CI [0.4935, 0.5046]  nulls 0.9980/0.9821  ADMISSIBLE
  MG tensor_product         0.4917x  CI [0.4859, 0.5009]  nulls 1.0450/1.0203  UNDECIDABLE
  MG strong_product         0.5051x  CI [0.4973, 0.5131]  nulls 1.0121/1.0224  UNDECIDABLE
  MG lexicographic_product  0.4403x  CI [0.4355, 0.4470]  nulls 0.9971/1.0230  UNDECIDABLE

Node and edge counts parity-gated against nx before timing on every row (4000n/8000e cartesian, 4000n/7920e tensor, 4000n/15920e strong, 4000n/204000e lexicographic).

CARTESIAN IS ADMISSIBLE AT 0.5000x — a clean, live-incumbent, dual-nulled LOSS. The other three refuse their nulls (these arms build a whole product graph per slot, the same non-stationarity that made add_edge and copy refuse today) and are not claims, but all four point estimates cluster tightly at 0.44-0.51x.

MAGNITUDE CORRECTION: the bead records 0.25-0.37x (MG cartesian 0.32x, tensor 0.25x, strong 0.25x, lexicographic 0.30x, n=40x25 weighted). I measure 0.44-0.51x on unweighted operands of a different size, so the row has improved by roughly 1.4-2x since 2026-07-16 without anyone working this bead — most likely from the general MultiGraph work that has landed since (the MgSlabStorage flip, and this session's endpoint-resolution and fresh-bucket levers). Re-measure on the bead's own weighted n=40x25 fixture before quoting a delta; mine is not the same workload.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: this is still a 2x-class loss with no native structure kernel, and the bead's diagnosis — graph_product_fast is simple-only and bails on multigraphs, so every MG product falls to the Python per-edge _product_add_keyed_edge loop — is untouched by this measurement. The prize it describes is real and is now the largest confirmed remaining loss I am aware of after colliders/v_structures (which I fixed 12.6x today).

NOTE ON THE PRIOR ATTEMPT recorded in this bead: a native multigraph_cartesian_product_fast was written, passed byte-exact parity when forced, and never fired because it was gated on edge_py_attrs.is_empty() while MG eagerly populates that mirror. The gate fix it calls for is still the stated next step and nothing here contradicts it.

title: perf(python): 'n in G' is 0.27x vs nx — the private-override probe in __contains__ costs more than the native lookup
description:
MEASURED ON HEAD (2026-08-04, CoralIsland, live nx 3.6.1 same invocation, PYTHONHASHSEED=0,
taskset -c 40-43, 41 rounds, 1200-node graph, 512 present string keys):

  nx    'n in G'         63.4 ns
  fnx   'n in G'        236.8 ns   -> 0.27x   <-- worse than the published has_node 0.46x
  fnx   G.has_node(n)    98.5 ns   -> 0.64x
  fnx   'n in G.nodes'  106.8 ns
  fnx   G.is_directed()  36.7 ns   (bare PyO3 call floor)

The native PyGraph::__contains__ and PyGraph::has_node are the SAME code, so the entire
236.8 - 98.5 = 138.3 ns gap is the Python _private_aware_contains wrapper. has_node escapes it:
Graph.has_node is bound to the raw native slot and private-storage graphs get a per-INSTANCE
method shadow instead. A dunder cannot be shadowed per instance (Python looks it up on the type),
so __contains__ pays the probe on every call for every graph.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND has_node: this is the dominant term in the published preferential_attachment
loss. nx's _apply_prediction and fnx's _link_prediction_validate_ebunch both do 2 'endpoint in G'
tests per pair, so the ebunch validation alone is 153.5 us for fnx vs 37.5 us for nx on 300 pairs
— 116 us of a total 127.5 us deficit (332.9 us vs 205.4 us). 91% of the preferential_attachment
loss is this one wrapper, not the scoring. Every algorithm that membership-tests nodes pays it.

STEP 1 (this bead): drop the per-call _private_override function frame and the vars() builtin from
_private_aware_contains — read self.__dict__ directly with the sentinel and the key bound as
closure locals.

STEP 2 (follow-up): move the probe into the native __contains__ so ordinary graphs pay nothing.
There is a single install funnel (_set_private_override, reached only by the four _node property
setters), so a native flag on PyGraph/PyDiGraph/PyMultiGraph/PyMultiDiGraph can make the check a
plain bool test.
close_reason: Step 1 landed 9eea9f3c6: 1.1950-1.2055x same-invocation on 'n in G' (236.8 -> 198.9 ns), 0.27x -> ~0.35x vs live nx, A/A nulls 0.994-1.001, parity asserted. Still a loss; step 2 (native flag) filed as follow-up.

title: fix(normalized_laplacian): match nx isolated-node diagonal (0 not 1)
description: normalized_laplacian_matrix computes I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2} with a constant identity, so an isolated (degree-0) node gets a diagonal of 1. nx computes D^{-1/2}(D-A)D^{-1/2}, where the D^{-1/2} D D^{-1/2} term is 0 (not 1) on isolated nodes — so nx's diagonal is 0 there. The two agree for all non-isolated nodes but diverge whenever the graph has an isolated node (incl. disconnected graphs): normalized_laplacian_spectrum gives a spurious 1.0 eigenvalue instead of nx's extra 0.0 (a k-component graph must have k zero eigenvalues). Fix: use nx's exact DH @ (D-A) @ DH form. Found via self-loop/isolated-node parity sweep.
close_reason: normalized_laplacian_matrix now computes nx's exact D^{-1/2}(D-A)D^{-1/2} form (was I - D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2} with constant identity), so isolated nodes get a 0 diagonal matching nx instead of a spurious 1. Disconnected graphs now yield the correct count of zero eigenvalues in normalized_laplacian_spectrum. Verified 0 matrix+spectrum mismatch across 400 random graphs (incl isolated/disconnected/self-loop/weighted); 57 new tests + full 19831-test suite pass.

title: bug(dijkstra_path): weighted path tie-break diverges from nx (seed 50: [0,1,2] vs [0,4,2])
description: PRE-EXISTING (not a cc regression — verified on committed HEAD before any cc change). test_weighted_path_adversarial_parity.py::test_dijkstra_path_and_length_parity[False] fails: over 300 seeds, seed 50 (s=0,t=2) diverges — fnx.dijkstra_path returns [0,1,2], nx returns [0,4,2]. Both are valid minimum-weight shortest paths (equal total weight); the divergence is a TIE-BREAK: fnx's dijkstra relaxes neighbors in a different order than nx, so on a weight tie it reconstructs a different (equally-optimal) path. dijkstra_path_length parity PASSES (the length is identical) — only the PATH choice differs. Same class as max_weight_matching tie-break (lmqwv) and bidirectional_dijkstra. FIX: align fnx's dijkstra neighbor-relaxation + heap tie-break order to nx's (nx iterates G[u] in adjacency/insertion order and its heap breaks ties by push order). Deep; the kernel is shortest_path_weighted / dijkstra in fnx-algorithms. Flagged by cc during fyxma3 conformance run.
close_reason: done

title: [perf][no-gaps] powerlaw_cluster_graph kernel: integer adjacency in clustering loop (6.5x slower than nx)
description: powerlaw_cluster_graph (fnx-generators lib.rs:4637) is 6.47x slower than nx. After the remove_edge fix (1d4b81488) it does NOT use remove_edge; its kernel hot loop calls graph.neighbors(&node_labels[target]) (allocates Vec<&str> + per-neighbor parse::<usize>) and graph.has_edge(source,neighbor) (String-keyed) every clustering step, plus graph.add_edge with String clones. 2. deepcopy fold: __deepcopy__ + deepcopy constructors (lib.rs ~5858/5877/5926/5949/9365/9387) do deepcopy_py_dict THEN py_dict_to_attr_map (2 passes). A deepcopy_py_dict_with_mirror helper (deep-copy value to mirror + py_value_to_cgse(orig) for Rust map, in one pass) folds them. The "does to_directed's empty Rust node attrs reach a node_attrs reader" concern is NOT reachable:

title: perf: native relabel/union/compose keeping attrs in Rust (attr round-trip floor 0.41-0.62x)
description:
PROFILE-FIRST FINDING (BlackThrush, 2026-07-16, .so=5060a3697, non-LTO). The graph-COMBINING operators (relabel_nodes copy=True, union, compose) are pure-Python in __init__.py and LOSE to nx SPECIFICALLY on attributed graphs, worsening with attr count:

| op | nattrs=0 | nattrs=3 | nattrs=8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| relabel_nodes | 1.62x (WIN) | 0.62x | 0.41x |
| union | 2.30x (WIN) | 0.76x | 0.50x |
| compose | 2.24x (WIN) | 0.85x | 0.59x |

ROOT CAUSE: with NO attrs fnx WINS (native inner clone). With attrs the Python impl does a full ATTRIBUTED ROUND-TRIP: G.nodes(data=True)+G.edges(data=True) MATERIALIZE every node/edge AttrMap into a fresh PyDict (Rust->Python), the comprehension rebuilds (new_key, dict) tuples, then add_nodes_from/add_edges_from RE-INGEST every dict back to a Rust AttrMap (Python->Rust). Cost is O((V+E) * attrs) of pure PyO3 conversion that nx (live-dict refs) never pays. relabel_nodes is at __init__.py:54971; union/compose similar. Already batched (add_*_from) and de-duplicated (cc-relabelnodict/br-norebuild) at the Python level — the residual IS the conversion, not batching.

FIX (native kernel, keeps attrs in Rust): _native_relabel_copy(mapping) on PyGraph/PyDiGraph — iterate the inner in node/edge order, resolve each new key from the mapping + canonicalize, and build a fresh inner via add_node_with_attrs/add_edge_with_attrs CLONING the store AttrMap Rust-to-Rust (NO PyDict materialization). union/compose can reuse the same primitive. 

SAFE GATING (parity): type is simple Graph/DiGraph; dict mapping (callable pre-resolved); NON-MERGING (all new canonicals distinct + no collision with unmapped nodes) — merging keeps the Python path; !edges_dirty AND node mirror clean (store authoritative; guarantees no py-only/non-CgseValue attr values are missed — a dirty/py-only attr forces fallback). Byte-exact vs the current Python path for these gated cases (store round-trips as identity for int/float/str/bool). Expected 0.41-0.62x -> ~2-4x on attributed graphs, neutral/win otherwise.

SIZE/RISK: ~cross-boundary kernel (new PyGraph construction incl node_key_map/mirrors/seqs + mapping canonicalization + collision detect + AttrMap clone). Bigger than a one-liner; needs its own cycle + full parity harness (self-loops, order, node-identity first-wins, graph-level attrs, DiGraph in/out order). Model H construction on the native copy().

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CAVEAT for the implementer (BlackThrush, follow-up): the CgseValue store is NOT always authoritative — the enum is only Bool/Int/Float/String/Map, NO py-object variant. Non-scalar attrs (tuples like pos=(x,y), lists, None, custom objects) live ONLY in the py mirror (node_py_attrs/edge_py_attrs), NOT the store; the current Python relabel is correct because edges(data=True) reads that mirror. So a native store-clone must GATE on all-scalar attrs (else it silently drops non-scalar values). Cheap gate idea: per node/edge compare store_attrs.len() vs py_mirror dict len (equal => all scalar => store complete). Also gate out non-empty adj_py_keys (hash-mixed keys 28/28.0/True need z6uka display overrides). Net: the safe native path covers scalar-attr graphs (the common weighted case, where the win is biggest); everything else falls back to the current Python path. This narrows scope but keeps parity guaranteed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
NOSHIP / REJECT the native-kernel approach (BlackThrush, 2026-07-16, implemented + reverted). Built _native_relabel_copy for simple Graph (subgraph-modeled: pass1 resolve+merge-detect->fallback, pass2 build via extend_nodes/edges_with_attrs_unrecorded batch, py_dict_to_attr_map_with_mirror preserves non-scalar attrs). PARITY PASSED byte-exact (8 seeds x mappings offset/str/tuple/shuffle/partial/identity x scalar+nonscalar+node/edge attrs + merging fallback + collide-unmapped). BUT it LOSES/REGRESSES: measured nx/fnx nattrs=0 0.90x (was 1.62x WIN!), nattrs=3 0.50-0.92x, nattrs=8 0.37-0.61x — WORSE than the Python path on both add_edge (eager mirror) AND add_edges_from (bulk) graphs.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis was WRONG): the loss is NOT a beatable 'round-trip'. The Python relabel already uses the hyper-optimized add_nodes_from/add_edges_from BATCHES. My native adds per-node pass-1 overhead (py_node_key + mapping.get_item + node_key_to_string) AND still pays py_dict_to_attr_map per attr'd element (attrs live in the py mirror, populated by BOTH add_edge and add_edges_from — the store is not lazy for these). No conversion saved + extra overhead => slower. RECLASSIFY: relabel/union/compose attributed loss is the SAME py->typed-Rust ATTR-CONVERSION FLOOR as from_edgelist(attrs)/Graph(dod) construction (fnx converts py dicts to CgseValue AttrMaps; nx keeps py-dict refs). It is architectural (fnx's typed storage), NOT a round-trip. Beating it needs a fundamentally different attr-storage strategy (e.g. store the Py<PyDict> directly for attr'd edges), a large risky change. Recommend CLOSING this bead as won't-fix / needs-storage-redesign. Reverted cleanly; no code shipped.

comments.text:
ATTRIBUTED OPERATOR ROWS RE-MEASURED — relabel STILL A LOSS, compose/union NEAR PARITY (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change. Bead stays OPEN and its relabel half survives; its compose/union half does not, on these numbers.

This bead records relabel/union/compose at 0.41-0.62x on ATTRIBUTED graphs, attributed to a py->typed-Rust attr-conversion floor, with a native attempt built and reverted. Six named losses have turned out stale on this project today, so these were measured before anything was planned from them — and unlike the others, one of them held.

MEASURED, live networkx 3.6.1 in the same invocation, balanced square, dual A/A nulls, 15 rounds, gc between slots, 600 nodes / 2400 edges with edge weight+label and node color, extension built from HEAD (_fnx.abi3.so sha256 edebab15701f37c1d0dd4a232262fd2eba6b1cdd6b6c0de2c6453339385e9a5b), taskset -c 40-47, load 64 of 64:

  relabel_nodes (ATTRIBUTED)  0.7353x  CI [0.6963, 0.7689]  nulls 1.0538/1.0969  UNDECIDABLE
  compose       (ATTRIBUTED)  0.9770x  CI [0.9049, 1.0071]  nulls 0.9704/0.8671  UNDECIDABLE
  union         (ATTRIBUTED)  0.9501x  CI [0.9148, 0.9959]  nulls 0.9708/0.9092  UNDECIDABLE

ALL THREE REFUSED their nulls — these arms allocate a whole result graph per slot, the same non-stationarity that made add_edge and copy refuse repeatedly today — so none of these is a claim. What the point estimates say, with that caveat carried:

  * relabel is still clearly BELOW parity and in the neighbourhood of this bead's 0.41-0.62x band. Its half of the premise survives.
  * compose and union are at 0.95-0.98x, i.e. essentially at parity and well above the recorded band. Their half does not obviously survive, and a native compose/union rewrite should not be started on the 0.41-0.62x figure without re-measuring first.

PARITY GATED BEFORE TIMING: relabel's node set, edge count and full node-attr dicts compare equal to nx; compose and union node/edge counts match.

SELF-CORRECTION POSTED ELSEWHERE, because it matters here: earlier today I reported relabel_nodes at 1.7137x ADMISSIBLE on br-r37-c1-5fije and called its 0.82x refuted. That run used an ATTR-LESS graph and I did not say so. The two shapes sit on opposite sides of parity (1.71x attr-less, 0.735x attributed), so the refutation was scoped narrower than stated and is withdrawn as written. Corrected on that bead directly.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE: the subprocess-per-slot substrate that admitted add_edge and MultiDiGraph.copy today (fresh heap per timed slot, so the arm is stationary by construction). These three rows are the obvious next users of it.

title: to_undirected/to_directed views fail isinstance checks
description:
fnx.to_undirected(G) and G.to_undirected(as_view=True) return view classes that don't pass isinstance(result, fnx.Graph) checks, breaking NetworkX parity.

NetworkX: isinstance(nx.to_undirected(G), nx.Graph) returns True
FrankenNX: isinstance(fnx.to_undirected(G), fnx.Graph) returns False

The view class is named Graph but inherits from _UndirectedGraphConversionView, not from fnx.Graph. This breaks code that type-checks graph results.

Fix: Either make the view classes inherit from the corresponding base graph classes, or return actual graphs (like nx does for Graph.to_undirected which returns a shallow copy).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
REJECT — architectural floor, not a removable inefficiency (CoralIsland, 2026-08-04).

The 0.7901x is real and reproducible (6/6 decidable, see the bead body), but the cost decomposes
into work that cannot be removed without making the view itself native. Absolute per-call medians,
n=2000 m=8000, 41 rounds, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, taskset -c 40-43:

  nx  len(g.adj)                82.9 ns
  fnx len(g.adj)               103.7 ns    <- the 0.80x
  fnx len(view) hoisted         88.4 ns
  fnx native_len() called direct 34.8 ns
  nx  len(g._adj) dict direct    36.4 ns
  nx  g.adj accessor             22.9 ns
  fnx g.adj accessor             25.5 ns
  attribute load, both sides     13.4 ns each

Two things fall out. First, OUR NATIVE CALL IS NOT THE PROBLEM — a no-arg PyO3 node-count call is
34.8 ns, actually slightly FASTER than nx's C-level len() on its adjacency dict at 36.4 ns, and the
.adj accessor is at parity (25.5 vs 22.9). Second, the whole deficit is the Python
AdjacencyView.__len__ frame that wraps it: unbound AV.__len__(av) is 69.6 ns against nx's
type(nv).__len__(nv) at 56.1 ns, and the body is already only three operations (load
self._fnx_native_len, test it against None, call it). There is no redundant work left to delete —
dropping the None test by always populating the slot would buy ~3 ns of 89.

Why the frame cannot be removed: len() dispatches through type(v).__len__(v), so any native __len__
slot must accept the VIEW as self. Our native length is a method bound to the GRAPH
(_GRAPH_ADJ_NATIVE_LEN.__get__(self, Graph)), so a class-level native slot on AdjacencyView cannot
reach it, and a PyO3 slot borrowed from another type would reject a foreign self. A subclass carrying
its own __len__ still needs a Python frame to hop from view to owner. The only way out is for the
view object itself to be the native object — that is docs/ZERO_COPY_VIEW_PRIMITIVE.md, whose own
note says block storage cannot be landed incrementally because the layout IS the change.

Checked and rejected as explanations: __slots__ is present (attribute access is 13.4 ns, identical
to nx's), there is no __getattr__ on the MRO, and there are ZERO 'type(...) is AdjacencyView'
identity checks in __init__.py, so a spoofed-name subclass would have been safe — it just would not
have helped.

RETRY PREDICATE: reopen only when the zero-copy native view primitive lands, at which point
len(G.adj) should collapse to roughly the 34.8 ns native call plus the 25.5 ns accessor, i.e. about
1.6x vs nx's 82.9 ns — a WIN rather than a 0.79x loss. Re-measure with the adj-descriptor suite,
6+ repetitions, and report the decidable/vetoed count.

The README now lists the measured 0.7901x so the loss is visible rather than silently absent.

title: perf(substrate): node-key PyObject materialization wall (live-PyDict/interned node storage) — convergent cap on colliders/relabel/construction/iteration
description:
CONVERGENT ROOT CAUSE (measured 2026-06-21, CopperCliff). Multiple residual vs-nx perf gaps all reduce to ONE substrate wall: fnx stores nodes canonical-String-keyed with LAZY Python display objects, so any operation yielding node KEYS must re-materialize a PyObject per occurrence via py_node_key/py_pred_key/py_succ_key, whereas nx reuses its stored node objects. fnx pays O(V) or O(E) PyObject allocations nx does not.

MEASURED EVIDENCE this wall caps (not speculation — built+measured):
- dag.colliders/v_structures: native _native_predecessor_keys_bulk added to PyDiGraph + routed (f54b6e536), correctness 30/30 byte-identical, but STILL 0.66x/0.38x because the bulk still materializes every predecessor node-key PyObject. REVERTED.
- relabel_nodes 0.82x: native clone+rename built+reverted (parity-bound by per-node label PyO3 round-trips, not edge structure).
- graph iteration ~35x cap (nodes(data)/dict(adjacency)) per prior memory (4b5ie/9hkgu node/adj mirror).
- construction tax (relabel/BA/convert residuals) — per-node Python-object materialization.

LEVER: interned / live-PyDict node storage — keep a persistent ordered Python node object store (interned display objects) so key-yielding ops reuse objects instead of re-creating them. Deep core-PyGraph rearchitecture touching every graph type (crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs PyGraph + digraph.rs PyDiGraph/etc). High-risk, multi-day, needs a dedicated clean-tree effort + full conformance. This is THE highest-value remaining perf lever (broad impact); all per-function routes to it have been measured as losses. Evidence: docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-06-21 entries.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
THE WALL'S NAMED ROWS RE-MEASURED — ONE IS NOW A 1.71x WIN, THE OTHERS ARE 2.5-7.5% LOSSES (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change. Bead stays OPEN, but the cost/benefit of the rearchitecture it proposes is now quantified and it is much worse than the bead implies.

WHY I CHECKED. This bead proposes "interned / live-PyDict node storage — deep core-PyGraph rearchitecture touching every graph type, high-risk, multi-day, needs a dedicated clean-tree effort". Unlike the other large proposals checked today, its rows are attributed to a MECHANISM nobody has since fixed (per-occurrence node-key PyObject materialization), so I expected them to hold. Two of four did not.

MEASURED, live networkx 3.6.1 in the same invocation, balanced square, dual A/A nulls, 21 rounds, n=2000/8000 edges, extension built from HEAD (_fnx.abi3.so sha256 016b512e35fe25979fb29aa5c649701eb79a8acbd6cba21520c68b57afe85e87), taskset -c 40-47, load 62 of 64. Every row parity-gated before timing.

  row                        bead says        measured                       verdict
  relabel_nodes(copy)           0.82x   1.7137x CI [1.7078, 1.7179]   ADMISSIBLE  (WIN)
  list(G.nodes(data=True))   iteration   0.9250x CI [0.9154, 0.9478]   ADMISSIBLE  (loss)
  dict(G.adjacency())        iteration   0.9754x CI [0.9719, 0.9852]   ADMISSIBLE  (loss)

relabel_nodes is REFUTED — it is a 1.71x win, not a 0.82x loss, and the bead records a native clone+rename having been built and REVERTED for it. Nobody should re-attempt that.

THE ITERATION ROWS ARE REAL LOSSES AND I AM NOT EXPLAINING THEM AWAY — but they are 7.5% and 2.5%, both admissible. That is the honest size of the prize on these two rows. Against "high-risk, multi-day, deep core rearchitecture touching every graph type", recovering 7.5% on nodes(data=True) and 2.5% on adjacency() is a poor trade, and it is the first time this bead has had numbers to weigh that against.

NOT MEASURED, stated rather than implied: dag.colliders (0.66x) and v_structures (0.38x), the two largest losses the bead names. Neither is exposed at top level in either library — networkx has them at `networkx.algorithms.dag.colliders` / `.v_structures`, and franken_networkx exposes neither name at top level. So they need a different call form than the one I used, and my run skipped them rather than guessing. THOSE TWO ARE NOW THE WHOLE CASE for this bead: they are the only named rows still carrying a large loss, and the bead itself says a native bulk predecessor-keys path was built for them, measured byte-identical 30/30, and still came out 0.66x/0.38x. Whoever picks this up should re-measure exactly those two first, through `networkx.algorithms.dag`, and decide the rearchitecture on them alone.

PATTERN WORTH NOTING, because this is the sixth today: named losses on this project are systematically stale in the loss direction. has_node (0.52x -> 0.68-0.72x), len(G.adj) (0.79x -> 1.56-1.61x WIN), preferential_attachment (loss -> 2.18x WIN), MG/MDG copy (0.44-0.82x -> 2.31x/3.78x WINS), the weight= family (0.53-0.80x -> 1.39x-50x), and now relabel_nodes (0.82x -> 1.71x WIN). comments.text:
FOUND THE REAL LOSS — colliders 0.0710x, v_structures 0.0888x, ADMISSIBLE. AND A REVERTED LEVER LOOKS ~9x BETTER THAN HEAD (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change. Bead stays OPEN, and this is now its whole case.

My previous entry re-measured this bead's other rows and found relabel_nodes had flipped to a 1.71x WIN and the iteration rows had shrunk to 2.5-7.5% residuals, leaving colliders/v_structures as the only named rows still carrying a large loss and explicitly unmeasured. Measured now, through the correct call form (neither name is top level: networkx.algorithms.dag / franken_networkx.algorithms.dag):

  colliders      0.0710x  CI95 [0.0700, 0.0732]   nulls 1.0121 / 1.0015   ADMISSIBLE
  v_structures   0.0888x  CI95 [0.0881, 0.0896]   nulls 0.9967 / 0.9957   ADMISSIBLE

  nx 0.95-1.21 ms    fnx 13.40-13.64 ms     2000-node DAG, 620 collider tuples

Parity gated element-by-element on all 620 tuples for both functions before timing — these are generators whose consumption order is observable. Live networkx 3.6.1 in the same invocation, balanced square, dual A/A nulls, 21 rounds, 25 warm-up passes (6 was not enough — the first attempt refused with nulls 1.11/0.74), extension built from HEAD (_fnx.abi3.so sha256 016b512e35fe25979fb29aa5c649701eb79a8acbd6cba21520c68b57afe85e87), load ~70 of 64.

THIS IS THE FIRST LARGE ADMISSIBLE LOSS I HAVE FOUND TODAY, against six named losses that turned out stale in the other direction. It is also ~10x WORSE than the 0.66x/0.38x this bead records.

WHY: `franken_networkx.algorithms.dag.colliders` IS networkx's own function — `@nx._dispatchable`, networkx's source — running duck-typed over an fnx graph. fnx has no implementation of its own here. So every `G.predecessors(node)` in nx's loop crosses the PyO3 boundary and materializes node-key PyObjects, which is precisely the wall this bead describes. The algorithm is identical; the graph interface is the entire 14x.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, and I want it checked rather than taken on my word. Commit f54b6e536 records three variants:
    native _native_predecessor_keys_bulk (built, routed, 30/30 byte-identical)  0.66x / 0.38x
    pure-Python reimplementation                                                0.42x

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
TRIED THE CHEAP FIX FOR colliders/v_structures — IT CANNOT WORK, AND THE REASON RULES OUT A WHOLE CLASS (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change survives; `git diff` on python/franken_networkx/dag.py is empty. Bead stays OPEN.

THE ATTEMPT. nx's colliders is three lines — `for node in G.nodes: for p1, p2 in combinations(G.predecessors(node), 2): yield (p1, node, p2)` — and the cost on an fnx graph is the O(V) `G.predecessors(node)` crossings, not the algorithm. `python/franken_networkx/dag.py` already has a purpose-built override point with an established precedent (`has_cycle`, gated on `G.is_directed() and backend is None`, falling back to nx verbatim), so the obvious cheap fix is to build the predecessor rows ONCE from a single pass over `G.edges()` — two crossings instead of O(V) — and have `v_structures` test its non-adjacency against a set built in the same pass instead of two `has_edge` crossings per collider. No Rust, no rebuild.

IT FAILS PARITY, AND NOT MARGINALLY. Same tuple COUNT (620), different content:

    first divergence   nx ('13', '34', '1')   reconstructed ('1', '34', '13')
    nx / fnx  G.predecessors('34')  ->  ['13', '1']
    reconstructed from G.edges()    ->  ['1', '13']

WHY, and this is the part worth keeping. `_pred[v]` preserves the order in which edges INTO v were added. `G.edges()` does not iterate in edge-addition order — it walks the successor structure, so it emits edges grouped by SOURCE node. For node '34' the edge (13,34) was added before (1,34), but '1' sorts before '13' in node order, so the edge walk sees (1,34) first and reverses the row. The predecessor order is genuine insertion history and is NOT RECOVERABLE from the edge list in any order it can be iterated.

THAT RULES OUT THE WHOLE CLASS of cheap fixes: any reconstruction of predecessor rows from edges(), adjacency(), or successors cannot reproduce the observable order, and colliders/v_structures are generators whose tuple order IS the contract. The rows have to come from the graph's own predecessor structure. That is exactly why the reverted f54b6e536 work took the shape it did — a NATIVE bulk that reads the pred rows in Rust — and it is very likely why the "pure-Python reimpl" recorded in that commit only reached 0.42x: it must have kept calling `predecessors()` per node.

MEASUREMENT UNCHANGED AND RE-CONFIRMED on the reverted tree, so the target is not going anywhere:

    colliders      0.0711x  CI95 [0.0702, 0.0731]   nulls 1.0183 / 1.0126   ADMISSIBLE
    v_structures   0.0894x  CI95 [0.0886, 0.0903]   nulls 0.9904 / 0.9931   ADMISSIBLE

(earlier run: 0.0710x / 0.0888x — the row is stable.)

WHAT REMAINS THE RECOMMENDATION, now with one alternative eliminated by test rather than by argument: reinstate f54b6e536's `_native_predecessor_keys_bulk` on PyDiGraph. Note for whoever does it — that commit is DOCS ONLY (17 lines in NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md); the code was never committed. The method exists on HEAD only for PyMultiDiGraph (crates/fnx-python/src/digraph.rs:5629), so PyDiGraph needs the mirror written, and then dag.py's `colliders = _nx_dag.colliders` / `v_structures = _nx_dag.v_structures` re-exports are the routing point. The parity gate to use is element-by-element over all tuples on a 2000-node DAG; it caught this attempt immediately.

title: perf(lookup): node_key_to_string heap-allocates a canonical String on every str-keyed READ — G.has_node 0.477x
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-04 (RainyCave), scripts/perf_harness.py node-primitives, live nx 3.6.1 in the same
invocation, 21 interleaved rounds, corrected three-clause median gate, all rows decidable, A/A null
medians 0.9993-1.0005 with half-widths ~0.001, parity IDENTICAL, thread_count_actually_used=1 on
both arms, ELF sha256 ee7363ceb00ddbc8710d66a2ae135c414bd6b26597a52b59248db362cb7d8301 self-reported
from inside the process. Host thinkstation1, governor performance, affinity 0-3.

  G.has_node(present) x512 [nx/fnx]   0.4768x  CI [0.4762, 0.4781]   nx 29.10us / fnx 61.02us
  G.has_node(missing) x512 [nx/fnx]   0.6084x  CI [0.6068, 0.6089]
  n in G (present)    x512 [nx/fnx]   0.7188x  CI [0.7179, 0.7200]   nx 34.75us / fnx 48.33us
  membership x512 [contains/has_node] 0.7831x  CI [0.7782, 0.7843]

Per call on 512 present str keys: fnx has_node 119.2ns, fnx 'n in G' 94.4ns, nx has_node 57.0ns,
nx 'n in G' 67.9ns. This is the named campaign loss (brief: 'G.has_node 0.46x'), CONFIRMED at
0.4768x rather than inherited.

TWO SEPARABLE COSTS, and the measurement splits them:

(1) ~24.8 ns/call is the CPython CALL PROTOCOL, not our code. PyGraph::has_node and
PyGraph::__contains__ are byte-identical Rust (same identity-int fast path, same
node_key_to_string, same inner lookup) — verified by reading both bodies — and neither carries a
Python wrapper (has_node is a method_descriptor, __contains__ a wrapper_descriptor). The
contains/has_node row measures the difference between a slot dispatch and a method call in ONE
invocation: 0.7831x. Not obviously attackable; recorded so nobody re-derives it.

(2) THE LEVER — the remaining ~94ns vs nx's 57ns is dominated by a heap allocation per READ.
node_key_to_string (crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs:97) does, for the overwhelmingly common str key:
    if let Ok(s) = key.downcast::<PyString>() { return Ok(format!("str:{}:{s}", s.len())); }
so every has_node / 'n in G' / has_edge / get_edge_data / G[u][v] / neighbors call mallocs and
frees a String purely to probe FxIndexMap<String, AttrMap>. networkx probes a C dict with zero
allocation, which is exactly why a PYTHON has_node (57ns) beats our NATIVE one (119ns).

PROPOSED FIX (safe Rust, no new deps): build the canonical bytes in a STACK buffer for short keys
and look up by &str, falling back to format! beyond the buffer. A borrowed-key Equivalent<String>
impl is the tempting alternative but is a TRAP: the map is hashed with FxHasher and str hashing
feeds the whole byte slice in one Hasher::write plus a 0xff terminator, so hashing the canonical
form in three pieces ('str:', the length digits, the key) does NOT reproduce the same hash and the
lookup silently misses. The stack buffer hashes the identical single slice, so it cannot diverge.

BLAST RADIUS: read-only paths only. Write paths legitimately need the owned String to insert.

TESTS THE FIX MUST CARRY: (a) a key longer than the stack buffer still resolves (the fallback
path); (b) keys at exactly buffer-1/buffer/buffer+1 bytes; (c) non-ASCII/multi-byte str keys, whose
byte length differs from their character count — the 'str:{len}:' prefix uses s.len() in BYTES, so
a fix that used character count would corrupt the key and this is the negative case; (d) str keys
that collide with the int/float canonical forms are unaffected; (e) round-trip against nx for a
graph mixing str, int, float, bool and None keys.

RETRY PREDICATE: same suite, same three rows, same gate, host load comparable to this baseline
(loadavg was 7.4 at admission). Report has_node present/missing AND 'n in G' — the allocation is on
BOTH paths, so a fix that moves only has_node is suspect. The whole-family rows (has_edge,
get_edge_data) should move too; if they do not, the attribution above is wrong.
close_reason: Six-arm paired measurement admitted and published (ledger ba3a7f493). The lever is real where applied: has_node/'n in G' moved 1.08-1.19x build-over-build with disjoint CIs. Classified SELF-SPEEDUP, campaign_output=false — G.has_node is still 0.5199x vs the live incumbent, so nothing was won; the preflight gate rejected my initial KEEP framing and was correct. The bead's family clause is FALSIFIED: seven of eight edge rows are flat-to-worse, because the lever was never applied to has_edge/get_edge_data despite a status comment claiming it was (Graph::has_edge uses the owned node_key_to_string exclusively). Follow-ups split out as br-r37-c1-vz4v9 (extend the lever, measured headroom) and br-r37-c1-pvl3v (unattributed MultiDiGraph.has_edge 0.924x).

title: maximal_independent_set wrong error message when nodes=None and seed-picked node causes failure
description: fnx.maximal_independent_set(G) with no nodes arg on a graph that fails (e.g. selfloop graph) raises NetworkXUnfeasible('[] is not an independent set of G') — the Rust binding emits an empty list. nx picks one random node, wraps in a set, and reports it: NetworkXUnfeasible('{0} is not an independent set of G'). title: P0: HEAD panics 'RefCell already borrowed' in Graph.has_edge — the afiq8 thread-local scratch is re-entered by nested with_node_key_str
description:
HEAD IS BROKEN FOR EVERY AGENT. Graph.add_edge panics on ordinary string-keyed inserts (CrimsonBeaver, 2026-08-14).

REPRO, deterministic, 4/4:

  PYTHONPATH=<repo>/python python3 -c "
  import franken_networkx as fnx
  g = fnx.Graph()
  nodes = [f'n{i}' for i in range(2000)]
  g.add_nodes_from((n, {'color':'r'}) for n in nodes)
  g.add_edge(nodes[0], nodes[1])"

  -> pyo3_runtime.PanicException: RefCell already borrowed

Repo ELF fdb27c8111714879 PANICS. The older site-packages ELF ee7363ceb00ddbc8 does NOT, so this arrived with today's in-flight work.

BACKTRACE names it precisely:

  thread panicked at crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs:263:43: RefCell already borrowed
     2: core::cell::panic_already_borrowed
     3: <_fnx::PyGraph>::has_edge::{closure#0}
     4: <_fnx::PyGraph>::__pymethod_has_edge__

CAUSE. br-r37-c1-afiq8 was implemented by replacing the [u8; CANONICAL_KEY_STACK_BUF] stack buffer in with_node_key_str with a thread_local! RefCell<String> scratch:

    thread_local! { static CANONICAL_STRING: RefCell<String> = ... }
    return CANONICAL_STRING.with(|scratch| { let mut scratch = scratch.borrow_mut(); ... });

But PyGraph::has_edge canonicalizes TWO endpoints by NESTING the helper inside its own closure:

    with_node_key_str(py, u, |u_c| {
        with_node_key_str(py, v, |v_c| self.inner.has_edge(u_c, v_c))
    })?

The inner call re-enters the same thread-local and borrow_mut() panics. With the old stack buffer each call had its own [u8; 128] in its own frame, so nesting was safe by construction. A single shared scratch makes the helper NON-REENTRANT, and every two-endpoint probe nests it.

BLAST RADIUS: Graph.add_edge calls has_edge on every insert (__init__.py:3479), so ordinary graph construction dies. Any other nested with_node_key_str site has the same fault — audit all of them, not just this one.

MY SHARE OF THIS: br-r37-c1-afiq8 is my bead and it PROPOSED the thread-local String scratch, explicitly, as the safe way to avoid the from_utf8 revalidation under #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. I did not flag that the helper is entered re-entrantly by two-endpoint probes. The mechanism I described was right and the concurrency/re-entrancy constraint on it was missing. That omission is mine.

FIX OPTIONS, preferring the one already proven in-tree:
  1. BEST — have has_edge use the two-buffer canonical_node_key_in form, which takes a CALLER-OWNED buffer per endpoint and is therefore reentrant by construction. That form already ships in _fnx_edge_attr_dict_get (lib.rs) and in EdgeView::__contains__ (views.rs, 189c82850), where I used two separate [u8; CANONICAL_KEY_STACK_BUF] buffers for exactly this reason.
  2. Make the scratch a depth-aware pool: RefCell<Vec<String>> with a borrow depth index, so nesting takes slot n+1.
  3. Revert with_node_key_str to the stack buffer and take afiq8 a different way.

Option 1 keeps afiq8's win (no from_utf8 revalidation on the caller-owned path) and removes the re-entrancy entirely.

REGRESSION TEST THIS NEEDS, because nothing in the suite caught it: the Python suite passed 55104/1 on the build BEFORE this change, and the panic is in a path the suite evidently does not exercise with two exact-string endpoints past the fast paths. Add a direct case — build a string-keyed Graph and call has_edge(u, v) plus add_edge(u, v) on nodes that miss the identity-int and cached_exact_string_node_index fast paths.

CLOSING PROBE: the repro above completes without panic.
close_reason: Fixed nested canonical scratch re-entry in has_edge with independent ArrayString buffers; 2000-string regression passes

title: perf(generators): karate_club_graph re-parses a 34x34 constant matrix and pays 156 per-edge add_edge crossings per call — published 0.38x
description:
PROJECT ORDERS 2026-08-08 name karate_club_graph 0.38x as one of the four worst measured losses. Unlike has_node/add_edge, this surface has NO prior-art REJECT in the negative ledger (perf_ledger_preflight --prior-art karate_club_graph returns only an unmeasured-surface audit mention).

MECHANISM (read, not inferred): python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:28502 karate_club_graph() mirrors nx's reference implementation literally — it splits the _KARATE_CLUB_MATRIX string, int()-parses all 1156 cells, and calls G.add_edge(row, col, weight=entry) once per nonzero cell (156 calls, each a PyO3 crossing), then writes G.nodes[v]['club'] per node (34 keydict writes). nx pays the same loop but with pure-dict add_edge, so fnx loses on crossing count.

LEVER: the matrix is a compile-time constant. Precompute the edge stream once, then one batched add_edges_from + one add_nodes_from carrying the club attrs.

CGSE NON-REGRESSION IS ABSOLUTE: node order (0..33 via add_nodes_from) and edge insertion order must be byte-identical to the per-cell loop. Requires a real parity test asserting list(G.nodes), list(G.edges), per-edge weight, per-node club, and G.graph vs the pre-change stream AND vs live networkx.

EVIDENCE REQUIRED: ledger preflight + same-invocation live-nx incumbent arm + A/A null before any ratio is published.
close_reason:
SHIPPED. Mechanism: karate_club_graph() re-parsed all 1156 cells of the constant _KARATE_CLUB_MATRIX per call and paid 155 per-cell PyO3 add_edge crossings + 34 per-node club writes. Now memoises the row-major (row,col,weight) stream once and replays it through one add_edges_from, with club folded into the single add_nodes_from.

NON-OBVIOUS CONSTRAINT FOUND AND LOCKED: Zachary's matrix is NOT symmetric. Seven pairs disagree across the diagonal — (0,12),(2,32),(8,32),(8,33),(22,33),(23,29),(29,32) — so the duplicate lower-triangle entry is what decides each final weight under last-write-wins; and M[22][33]=0 while M[33][22]=3, so that edge exists ONLY because row 33 emits it and lands last in node 22's adjacency row. The obvious upper-triangle rewrite (78 tuples vs 155) would drop one edge and mis-weight seven. tests/python/test_karate_club_graph_parity.py fails loudly on any such attempt.

MEASURED (same-invocation live nx 3.6.1, 41 rounds, 27 iters/slot, taskset -c 40-47, balanced [A',B',B'',A'',A'',B'',B',A'] square so nulls and candidate are position-balanced; identical ELF bench_elf_sha256=80488d1e0014e4ca2907f8166df60fdf15a9de6eab6bd11685d260917fc7041d both arms, only the Python source sha moved 46a3b0f2 -> 930c0caa):
  before 0.3762x CI95 [0.3707, 0.3836]  (so the ORDERS-named 0.38x loss was real on HEAD, not a stale premise)
  after  1.3665x CI95 [1.3572, 1.3812]  <- crosses from loss to WIN vs nx
  A/A null nx  1.0020x CI95 [0.9985, 1.0066]
  A/A null fnx 1.0016x CI95 [0.9991, 1.0034]
Widest null CI half-width 0.0040; effect sits 91x that floor with the candidate CI wholly above 1.0. DECIDABLE in both directions.

SCOPE LIMIT STATED: same-invocation dual-A/A median-CI gate, NOT a perf_harness host-wide quiescence admission (load 6.4 and 7.6 of 64).

PARITY: 16 new tests vs TWO oracles (the pre-batch per-cell builder spelled out in-test, and live networkx) covering node order, edge order, every weight, every club, G.graph, every adjacency row order, attr-dict non-aliasing across calls, and the asymmetry premise itself. Full karate-dependent sweep: 1528 passed, 1 skipped across 33 files. UBS clean (0 critical / 0 warning). perf_ledger_preflight --check-staged: OK.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SURFACE SATISFIED — BUT THE DEGENERATE BOUNDARIES, WHERE THIS BUG CLASS ACTUALLY LIVES, WERE NOT
COVERED (CopperCliff, 2026-08-08).

tests/python/test_kernel_fastpath_edgecase_parity.py already existed and matched this bead's named
surface: to_prufer_sequence on tree / non-tree / single, flow_hierarchy on dag / cycle / mutual /
self-loop, hyper_wiener on connected / disconnected, at 13 cases. It also already carries the note
excluding current_flow/katz n<3 to bp6wk. I checked before writing.

THE GAP, and it is the specific one this bead names. The class being guarded is "a wrapper hands back
a kernel result without networkx's edge-case handling". The inputs where that handling EXISTS are the
null graph, the edgeless graph and the single node — and every fixture in the file had at least two
nodes and at least one edge, except `empty_graph(1)`. So the module covered the ordinary cases of
three functions and not the degenerate ones where the guarded defect would appear.

MEASURED, all agreeing with networkx, none previously asserted:

    to_prufer_sequence  empty_graph(0)      NetworkXPointlessConcept
                        empty_graph(2)      NotATree
                        path_graph(1)       NetworkXPointlessConcept
                        path_graph(3)       ok [1]
                        two components      NotATree
    flow_hierarchy      empty digraph       NetworkXError      <- the division-by-zero shape
                        single node         NetworkXError
                        self-loop only      ok 0.0
                        two self-loops      ok 0.0
    hyper_wiener        empty_graph(0)      NetworkXPointlessConcept
                        empty_graph(1)      ok 0.0
                        empty_graph(3)      ok inf             <- a VALUE, not an exception

NON-VACUOUS: those boundaries produce FIVE DISTINCT outcomes across the five representative cases
(PointlessConcept / NotATree / inf / 0.0 / NetworkXError), so they exercise different contract
branches rather than restating one. The expected outcome is written next to each case so a future
divergence shows which contract moved rather than just that something did.

ALSO ADDED — THE PRUFER ROUND-TRIP. The sequence was only ever compared to networkx's, which catches
a divergence but not a codec that is self-consistently wrong in both directions. `from_prufer_sequence`
must rebuild the original tree; verified on four trees, and the decoded graph also matches networkx's
decode in edge ORDER.

Cases 13 -> 29. File: 29 passed. Full Python suite: 51742 passed, 1085 skipped, 0 FAILED.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: the `_outcome` helper compares exceptions by `type(exc).__name__`. That is
the same name-vs-identity weakness I fixed in br-r37-c1-uaw1x, and it is harmless here for the same
reason — fnx re-exports networkx's exception classes, which uaw1x now pins directly. Duplicating that
lock in this module would add cases without adding coverage.

MEASURED MOVEMENT on that path, same balanced-square substrate, 41 rounds, taskset -c 40-47, live nx 3.6.1 in-invocation, before ELF 80488d1e / after 675707ac with identical Python sources, all rows decidable, every A/A null 0.9977x-1.0015x:

  G.degree(n)         str x512   0.4222x -> 0.4247x   (UNCHANGED — degree does not route through this path)

SWEEP RESULT: exactly TWO published rows sit on this path, and both are now annotated STALE with a pointer to the 7faiu ledger row — README `G.has_node(n)` (line ~1141) and `n in G` (line ~1142). No other README perf row cites a string-keyed lookup mechanism.

CHECKED AND FOUND NOT AFFECTED: the 2026-07-26 CloudyTurtle KEEP for has_edge primitives (br-r37-c1-6q4wl, 1.8044-1.9501x) is a SELF-SPEEDUP row — it measures public-wrapper against captured-raw descriptor, not a vs-nx ratio — so cb519bd06 does not invalidate it. Its arithmetic is a before/after inside fnx and both arms moved together. My 0.4340x -> 0.6502x figure for has_edge is a vs-nx measurement of a different question and is recorded here rather than annotated onto that row.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: no ratio was replaced and nothing was converted. Every number above comes from the balanced-square substrate, not an admitted perf_harness invocation with the host-wide quiescence proof this contract requires. The annotations withdraw confidence in figures that no longer describe HEAD; they do not assert new ones. Understating our own library is the safe direction.

STANDING HAZARD WORTH A PROCESS NOTE, not just a fix. This staleness was only caught because the same agent shipped the lever and then read the claims. On a multi-agent perf campaign that coincidence is not reliable: agent A lands a change on a shared path, agent B's published rows silently age, and nothing links them. Any lever that touches a shared hot path — canonicalization, the adjacency substrate, the batch collectors, the per-mutation entry — should carry the same sweep in its own landing commit. cb519bd06 did not, and this comment is the retrofit.

For the next sweep, the cheap version is: grep the README perf table and the three active ledgers for rows whose stated MECHANISM names the path you just changed, then re-measure only those.

comments.text:
LEDGER AUDIT AFTER THIS SESSION — void rate DOWN, and a much larger gap the rejection metric does not show (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08).

The preflight's own docstring says to run --audit periodically because "a rising void rate IS the decay". I added roughly 19 ledger rows today, so I ran it on my own contribution rather than assuming it was fine.

REJECTION ROWS — improved, and the improvement is arithmetic rather than my opinion:

  now       133 VOID / 185 audited = 71.9%
  baseline  133 VOID / 176 audited = 75.6%   (the figure in the preflight docstring)

The VOID count is UNCHANGED at 133 while the denominator grew by 9. So the rejection rows added since that baseline — several of them mine — are all non-void, and the rate fell 3.7 points. The enforcement gate works: every row I staged today had to pass --check-staged, which is why they carry A/A nulls and ELF hashes rather than being VOID-NONULL.

KEEP ROWS — this is the number that should worry someone, and it is much larger than the rejection problem:

  603 KEEP rows audited
   51 carry a loaded ELF sha-256      552 do not
   18 labelled incumbent
    8 labelled self-speedup
  577 unlabelled
   18 / 603 = 3.0% measured against the incumbent

So 92% of KEEP rows carry no comparison class and 91% carry no in-process ELF hash. The contract that requires both is enforced only on rows added or modified since the merge base — which is correct as a gate, and means the entire historical backlog stays unattested indefinitely. Anyone reading this ledger for evidence is, by row count, mostly reading rows that never had to state what they were measured against.

That is consistent with docs/CLAIM_COVERAGE_AUDIT.md's finding of 2.0% attested, measured a different way, and it is the same problem: the gate stops decay from here forward, it does not repair what predates it.

I am NOT proposing a bulk relabelling. Retro-fitting a comparison class onto a row whose measurement conditions nobody recorded would be inventing provenance, which is worse than the row being honestly unlabelled — and it is the exact failure the class taxonomy exists to prevent. The useful framing is that "603 KEEP rows" is not 603 pieces of evidence: it is 18 attested campaign results, 8 attested self-speedups, and 577 rows whose status is unknown and should be treated as such when anyone cites a count.

MY SESSION'S CONTRIBUTION, for calibration: of the 8 self-speedup-labelled KEEP rows in the entire ledger, most are from today (the canonical-key fix, the preferential_attachment scorer, and the four batch collector fixes), and each carries its ELF hash and its A/A nulls because the gate refused them otherwise. That is a small absolute number against 603, which is the point — the labelled fraction is small because labelling is recent, not because the work is.

(3.6.1 from site-packages, asserted in-process). PYTHONHASHSEED=0, taskset -c 40-43, 21 rounds per

  input  189843 bytes sha256 5d7c003cd5c7507408804b01e266bb81d7cfb2fe6546c58dfebff60f621ea89b
  output  16707 bytes sha256 e6fd694bc8cd85ad2b23c9bc1ed6a76292330fde172c0f2f6beb6f48ebdf2469
Complete-output byte parity between arms holds (800 nodes, 0 edges as preregistered).

RESULT (ratio = t_nx / t_fnx):
  run1 4.3665x CI[4.3173,4.4245] worst_null_bias 0.0100 clauses 111 DECIDABLE
  run2 4.2831x CI[4.2236,4.4038] worst_null_bias 0.0228 clauses 110 vetoed  (nx null 0.9772)
  run3 4.4494x CI[4.3911,4.4921] worst_null_bias 0.0101 clauses 111 DECIDABLE
  run4 4.3528x CI[4.2545,4.4886] worst_null_bias 0.0129 clauses 111 DECIDABLE
  run5 4.4136x CI[4.2950,4.4970] worst_null_bias 0.0134 clauses 111 DECIDABLE
  run6 4.4102x CI[4.2182,4.4949] worst_null_bias 0.0157 clauses 111 DECIDABLE
  run7 4.4408x CI[4.2712,4.5851] worst_null_bias 0.0426 clauses 110 vetoed  (fnx null 0.9574)
  run8 4.4307x CI[4.3735,4.4996] worst_null_bias 0.0118 clauses 111 DECIDABLE
  effect median 4.4119x, min 4.2831x, max 4.4494x, spread 3.9%
  verdict: 6/8 DECIDABLE, 2/8 vetoed

FINDINGS:
1. The effect is stable and large. Clause 1 (CI excludes 1) and clause 2 (effect > 2x null
   half-width) passed in 8/8 runs. Only clause 3 (worst null median bias <= 0.02) ever failed.
2. 'A/A drift' is a misnomer. The two vetoes came from DIFFERENT arms — run2 from the nx null,
   run7 from the fnx null — so it is not something fnx.minimum_branching does. I checked the
   obvious subject-side explanations and ruled them out: 20 consecutive calls on one graph show no
   trend (7.6-8.6 ms, no growth), a fresh graph is not faster, gc.collect() changes nothing, and
   calibrate() returns inner=1 deterministically for both arms. It is a single 21-round null draw
   wandering past a 2% ceiling on a loaded host, at roughly a 25% rate.
3. The bead's stated predicate — proving one identical managed physical Cargo target path across
   two rch exec --base --clean-overlay invocations — has no causal connection to any of this. The
   row is not blocked on rch. It is blocked on (a) host-wide exclusivity, which it never got, and
   (b) a third clause that vetoes a reproducible 4.4x effect a quarter of the time.

NOT CONVERTING the README claim: these runs could not carry the host-wide quiescence proof the
contract requires, so publishing 4.4119x would be proof-class inflation. The README row now
records this evidence and still says 'no current admissible ratio'.

Filed the clause-3 fragility separately with this run as its demonstration evidence.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TARGET HAS MOVED — READ BEFORE RETRYING (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08). This bead's recorded ratios no longer describe HEAD, because a source change landed today on exactly this path.

WHAT LANDED: cb519bd06 (br-r37-c1-7faiu) replaced the core::fmt formatting inside write_canonical_str_key, the canonical node-key builder that every string-keyed has_node / n-in-G / has_edge probe goes through. Profiling attributed 54.5% of has_node(str) to that key build; removing it took 27.6 ns of a 49.4 ns str-vs-int delta.

MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, same balanced-square substrate, 41 rounds, taskset -c 40-47, live nx 3.6.1 in-invocation, before ELF 80488d1e and after ELF 675707ac with identical Python sources, all rows decidable and every A/A null between 0.9977x and 1.0015x:

  G.has_node(present) str x512   0.5178x -> 0.6937x
  G.has_node(missing) str x512   0.6071x -> 0.8696x
  n in G (present)    str x512   0.7840x -> 1.1129x   <- crosses to a WIN

Against this bead's recorded figures (present 0.5199x, missing 0.6417x, and the sibling n-in-G row at 0.7903x), every one of them now understates HEAD, and the n-in-G row understates it enough to flip the sign of the comparison.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not convert anything. These numbers come from the balanced-square substrate, not from an admitted perf_harness invocation with the host-wide quiescence proof this contract requires, so publishing 1.1129x as a claim would be exactly the proof-class inflation the p80x1 family exists to prevent. The README rows are annotated as STALE with a pointer to the 7faiu ledger row and an explicit instruction not to cite the old figures as current — that withdraws confidence in a figure that no longer describes HEAD without asserting a new one in its place.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RETRY. Whoever satisfies this bead's predicate should expect to measure roughly 0.69x present / 0.87x missing rather than 0.52x / 0.64x, and should expect n in G to come back at or above parity. If a retry reproduces the OLD figures on HEAD, something is wrong with the build under test — check the loaded ELF against cb519bd06 before trusting the row.

ON THE PREDICATE ITSELF. It requires two rch exec --base --clean-overlay invocations to prove one identical managed physical target path; LavenderSalmon recorded it failing closed twice on 2026-08-04 with RCH rewriting CARGO_TARGET_DIR to distinct pool paths. CoralIsland reached the same conclusion about the identical predicate on the sibling br-r37-c1-p80x1.14 and stated it plainly there: the rch target-path condition has no causal connection to what actually blocks these rows, which is host-wide exclusivity plus the clause-3 fragility filed as br-r37-c1-d4xot. This bead inherits that objection. Re-pointing the predicate at the real blockers would be a separate decision and I am not making it here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RATIOS RE-MEASURED AND ADMITTED — plus a decomposition and one refuted lever (CopperCliff, 2026-08-08).

This bead is a claim-gate RETRY, which my brief reserves for a quiet exclusive host, so I did not run the contract harness. What I did run is the balanced-square substrate, and both rows came out admissible, which is worth recording because the published figures were stale by a wide margin:

  G.has_node present   0.7595x CI [0.7422,0.7637]   (published 0.5199x)
  G.has_node missing   0.8153x CI [0.8011,0.8209]   (published 0.6417x)
  n in G   present     1.2234x CI [1.2194,1.2280]   (published 0.7903x — now a WIN)
  n in G   missing     1.5063x CI [1.4924,1.5206]   (published 0.9651x — now a WIN)

21 rounds, live nx 3.6.1 same invocation, dual A/A nulls per row all within 0.0016 of 1.0, 30 warm-up iterations per arm, taskset 40-47, load 5.9. README swept in 264bb37a0. The STALE warnings on both rows understated the move: the n in G warning said the SIGN was in question, and it had indeed flipped.

DECOMPOSITION, which this bead did not have. Both spellings are native on fnx — has_node is the PyO3 method and __contains__ the C slot, neither goes through a Python wrapper on a plain graph:

  fnx  G.has_node(k)         70.7 ns
  fnx  Graph.has_node(G,k)   60.2 ns    <- unbound: 10.5 ns is per-call bound-method creation
  fnx  k in G                54.3 ns
  nx   G.has_node(k)         51.4 ns
  nx   Graph.has_node(G,k)   50.6 ns    <- nx pays only 0.8 ns for the same binding step
  nx   k in G                61.0 ns

So the loss splits two ways, and the smaller half is a surprise: fnx pays 10.5 ns to bind a native method per call where nx pays 0.8 ns for a Python one. The larger half is that fnx's native work (60.2 ns) is ALREADY slower than nx's Python dict lookup (50.6 ns) — that is the IndexMap<String,_> canonicalisation substrate this bead's prose names, and it is where the remaining ~9.6 ns sits.

LEVER TRIED AND REFUTED — do not retry it. br-r37-c1-... the standing note that a dunder cannot use the per-instance method-shadow escape implies a REGULAR method can. has_node is a regular method, so I bound it once into the instance dict (vars(g)['has_node'] = g.has_node) to skip the per-call binding. It is SLOWER: 70.5 -> 73.4 ns. The instance-dict lookup costs more than the binding it avoids. The escape exists for non-dunders but is not profitable here, which refines rather than contradicts the standing note.

WHAT REMAINS is the canonicalisation substrate, already mined by br-r37-c1-7faiu (core::fmt removal, 0.5178 -> 0.6937x) and br-r37-c1-oe93x (borrowed key, no per-read String). I found no cheap lever left on this row.

SUBSTRATE: balanced [A B B A A B B A] square, live networkx 3.6.1 in the SAME invocation, dual A/A nulls (one per arm) measured through the identical scheme, warm-up before timing, 21 rounds, 512 probes per timed slot, bootstrap median CI, taskset -c 40-47. Extension built from HEAD by maturin and loaded from the REPO TREE via PYTHONPATH, not site-packages (which is stale on this box): _fnx.abi3.so sha256 016b512e35fe25979fb29aa5c649701eb79a8acbd6cba21520c68b57afe85e87. Host load 79-88 of 64.

MEASURED, two independent invocations, n=2000 / 8000 edges, existing str key:

  run 1  has_node   0.7216x  CI95 [0.7205, 0.7230]   nulls nx 1.0010 / fnx 1.0001   ADMISSIBLE
  run 2  has_node   0.7069x  CI95 [0.7049, 0.7095]   nulls nx 1.0037 / fnx 1.0045   ADMISSIBLE

  run 1  `n in G`   1.1746x  CI95 [1.1716, 1.1772]   nulls nx 0.9958 / fnx 0.9973   ADMISSIBLE
  run 2  `n in G`   1.3652x  CI95 [1.3598, 1.3696]   nulls nx 1.0000 / fnx 0.9951   ADMISSIBLE

THE 0.52x FIGURE IN CIRCULATION IS STALE. HEAD is 0.70-0.72x on this workload. Quote it as a RANGE, not a point: the two runs' CIs do NOT overlap even though both pass their nulls, because the host moved between invocations (nx itself timed 55.9 then 98.7 ns/op). An A/A null certifies stationarity WITHIN a run and says nothing about comparability ACROSS runs — the same correction CopperCliff had to make on br-r37-c1-jc9e4.

`n in G` IS A WIN at 1.17-1.37x. Worth stating because the standing note has it at 0.27x historically and 1.1129x after the corefmt lever; it has kept moving. has_node and `n in G` now sit on OPPOSITE sides of parity — the dunder is FASTER than the named method in fnx, and slower in nx — which is the sharpest datum here for whoever attacks has_node next. Both reach the same native probe, so the gap between them is Python-side dispatch, not the lookup.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. This bead asks for the incumbent gate under the contract harness with stable clean-overlay target reuse. This is a standalone square, not that harness, and it ran at load ~85 rather than in a quiet window. It is admissible on its own terms — both nulls inside [0.98,1.02] in both runs — and it refutes the 0.52x premise, but it does NOT discharge the bead's stated gate. Left OPEN deliberately.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
THE OVERRIDE-PROBE INLINE IS NOT THE has_node GAP — TRIED, MEASURED, REVERTED (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change survives; `git diff` on the package is empty. Bead left OPEN.

THE HYPOTHESIS, and it looked strong. `__contains__`'s factory carries an explicit comment that it writes the private-override probe "as cheaply as Python allows: the key and the sentinel are closure cells rather than module globals, `self.__dict__` replaces the `vars()` builtin call, and the `_private_override` helper is inlined so an ordinary graph pays no extra interpreter frame". `has_node` never got that treatment — it still calls `_private_override(self, _PRIVATE_NODE_OVERRIDE)`, i.e. an extra interpreter frame, a `vars()` builtin call and two module-global lookups per call. A documented optimization applied to one sibling and not the other, on the exact pair that sits on opposite sides of parity, is about as good as a lead gets.

MEASURED, same square, same invocation, live nx 3.6.1:

  has_node BEFORE  0.6819x / 0.6886x / 0.7069x / 0.7216x   (four admitted runs)
  has_node AFTER   0.6835x  CI95 [0.6819, 0.6852]  nulls 1.0057 / 1.0007  ADMISSIBLE

0.6835 sits INSIDE the spread of the unmodified runs. The change is semantically identical and strictly less work, and it bought nothing measurable. Reverted rather than landed: an unmeasurable micro-edit to python/franken_networkx/__init__.py is churn on the most contended file in the repo.

WHAT THAT LEAVES, and it is a better answer than the one I was chasing. `n in G` and `G.has_node(n)` reach the SAME native probe, so the ~2x gap between them is not the lookup and is now not the override probe either. What remains is the call protocol: `n in G` compiles to CONTAINS_OP and goes straight to the type's `sq_contains` slot — no attribute lookup, no bound-method object, no argument tuple — while `has_node` is an attribute lookup plus a bound call plus a Python shim frame, and only then the same native probe. networkx pays the same protocol cost for ITS has_node, but the body it reaches is a bare dict lookup rather than a PyO3 crossing.

So the residual has_node loss is the PyO3 boundary measured against a CPython dict lookup, with the Python method-call protocol on top of both. That is the architectural floor this project already knows by other names, not a missing micro-optimization. Anyone attacking it should be targeting the boundary crossing, and should not re-try the override-probe inline — this entry is why.

STANDING ROWS from the same squares, for whoever needs the current numbers:
  has_node   0.68-0.72x   LOSS, four admitted runs
  `n in G`   1.35-1.37x   WIN, four admitted runs

title: perf(python): move the node private-override probe into native __contains__ so ordinary graphs pay nothing
description:
Step 2 of br-r37-c1-mi31t (step 1 landed 9eea9f3c6: 236.8 -> 198.9 ns, still 0.35x vs nx's 63 ns).

'n in G' is the only node-membership spelling that cannot escape the Python private-override
wrapper. has_node is bound straight to the raw native slot because a graph that gains NetworkX
private storage can be given a per-INSTANCE method shadow; a dunder is looked up on the TYPE, so
Graph.__contains__ must stay a single type-level function and every graph pays the probe.

LEVER: give PyGraph/PyDiGraph/PyMultiGraph/PyMultiDiGraph a Rust bool recording whether a private
node override is installed, and have the native __contains__ branch on it. There is exactly ONE
install funnel — _set_private_override(self, _PRIVATE_NODE_OVERRIDE, value), reached only by the
four _node property setters at python/franken_networkx/__init__.py:45108, 45136, 45148 and 45176 —
so the flag cannot drift as long as that funnel also calls the native setter. With the flag clear
the native __contains__ is exactly today's has_node (98.5 ns measured, ~0.64x vs nx); with it set,
return to the Python mapping path so private-storage semantics are byte-identical.

TESTS the fix must carry: (1) 'n in G' agrees with G.has_node(n) on present / absent / unhashable
keys for all four classes; (2) after assigning G._node = <mapping>, 'n in G' consults the ASSIGNED
mapping and not the native store — the negative case a flag that is never set would fail; (3) the
flag survives copy/subgraph/deepcopy of a private-storage graph.

RETRY PREDICATE: same-invocation A/B rebinding the arms as in
scratchpad probe_contains_ab.py, live nx 3.6.1, 41 interleaved rounds, A/A null, matched host load.
Target: 'n in G' at or near has_node's 98.5 ns.

DOWNSTREAM: this is 91% of the published preferential_attachment loss (ebunch validation was
153.5 us vs nx 37.5 us on 300 pairs, out of a 127.5 us total deficit), so re-measure
preferential_attachment and G.has_node together when it lands.

title: [perf] fnx-algorithms::betweenness_centrality_generic inner loop (lib.rs:3158-3161) — string→index adjacency ~76% of 1025ms/call, baseline N=1500/M=6000
description:
## Scenario
fnx_algorithms::betweenness_centrality (Brandes) on connected sparse random graph, N=1500 nodes / M=6000 edges (avg deg 8), single-threaded. Profiling run 20260601T232229Z-b3bd5e6c0 (artifacts under tests/artifacts/perf/).

## Baseline
p50 1024 ms, p95 1097 ms, p99 1187 ms per call (30 samples, CV 4.7%); peak RSS 11.4 MB.

## Profiler evidence (instrumentation; perf/samply unusable on saturated host)
- PERF_SPANS phase split: BFS/SSSP phase 946 ms (93%), accumulation 29 ms (3%), per-source alloc 19 ms (2%).
- edges_scanned = 18,000,000 per call (n=1500 source-BFS x 12,000 directed adjacency entries).
- Non-distorting microbench ALGO=lookup_sweep isolates the inner-loop ops neighbors_iter(name)+get_node_index(name) over the full edge set = ~0.43-0.52 ms/sweep; x1500 sweeps = ~640-780 ms = ~62-76% of total runtime.

## Hotspot
betweenness_centrality_generic (crates/fnx-algorithms/src/lib.rs:3158-3161): the inner loop does graph.neighbors_iter(nodes[v]) (string-keyed adjacency lookup) then graph.get_node_index(w_name).unwrap() (node-name STRING -> integer index via HashMap) for every one of the 18M edge traversals. ~76% of wall-clock is string hashing + HashMap probing, not graph work — the String-keyed-adjacency tax.

## Hypothesized fix (optimizer to apply + verify; do not change observable output)
Precompute an integer-indexed adjacency once per call (CSR or Vec<Vec<usize>>) BEFORE the source loop, then iterate usize neighbor indices directly in the inner loop — removing the per-edge string hash and HashMap lookup. Expected ~3-4x. Same lever helps closeness_centrality and harmonic_centrality (see sibling bead). Verify parity via existing conformance suite (scores/order unchanged) and re-baseline with crates/fnx-algorithms/src/bin/perf_harness.rs (ALGO=betweenness N=1500 DEG=8).

title: perf(subgraph_view): stop copying the parent graph into the filtered-view Rust base (O(N+E)->O(1))
description: subgraph_view/_generic_filtered_graph_view instantiates type('Graph',(_FilteredGraphView,Graph)). The PyO3 Graph base __new__ eagerly COPIES the entire parent graph (all nodes+edges) into the view's Rust storage on every construction — O(|V|+|E|). The filtered view never reads that base (every query method is overridden to use self._graph + the filters), so it is pure waste. Construction scales linearly with PARENT size: 500n=6ms, 3000n=44ms, 8000n=140ms. This is the dominant cost of k_core/k_shell/k_crust/k_corona (k_crust 9.4x slower than nx) and every G.subgraph()/restricted_view/edge_subgraph. LEVER: add _FilteredGraphView.__new__ returning super().__new__(cls) (empty base, O(1)) so the parent isn't copied; __init__ still wires the live filtered view. Isomorphism: view answers (nodes/edges/adjacency/degree/copy/etc) byte-identical to nx; full view + core-family suites pass.
close_reason: Added _FilteredGraphView.__new__ returning super().__new__(cls) (empty Rust base) so subgraph_view no longer copies the parent's nodes+edges into the view's storage (O(N+E)->O(1)); the filtered view already answers every query via self._graph + filters. Construction 3000n 44ms->0.44ms (~100x). title: perf(MultiDiGraph): has_edge lost 7.6% build-over-build between 98066b4b1 and HEAD — unattributed
description:
Isolated from br-r37-c1-oe93x's six-arm measurement (ledger entry 2026-08-06, ba3a7f493) because it is NOT explained by that bead's lever.

MEASURED, paired in-window, both arms with live nx 3.6.1 in the same invocation, 21 interleaved rounds, dual A/A nulls, corrected three-clause median gate, disjoint CIs:
    MultiDiGraph.has_edge x512   BEFORE 0.5030x   AFTER 0.4649x   ratio 0.924x
BEFORE ELF ee7363ceb00ddbc8710d66a2ae135c414bd6b26597a52b59248db362cb7d8301 (clean rebuild of 98066b4b1)
AFTER  ELF a9b194d1a21467ae1411a66c218e083e055f2f4e7297ec935b47e09a3bcd9fd7 (HEAD at 2026-08-05)

It is the largest adverse move in the eight-row edge family and the only one beyond ~3.6%. The sibling rows were 0.987x (Graph), 0.989x (MultiGraph) and 1.023x (DiGraph), so this is not a uniform drift.

WHY IT IS UNATTRIBUTED, stated plainly: the AFTER arm is HEAD, not any single commit, so it carries every change merged since 98066b4b1. The oe93x lever cannot be the cause - that lever is not on the has_edge path at all (Graph::has_edge uses the owned node_key_to_string exclusively; see br-r37-c1-vz4v9). So something else in that commit range is responsible, or it is a fixture-sensitive artifact.

FIRST STEP, before any optimisation work: bisect the commit range with ELFs built from single commits and re-run ONLY 'perf_harness.py edge-primitives', comparing the MultiDiGraph.has_edge row. Do not attempt a fix until the responsible change is identified - a 7.6% move on one of four sibling rows is as likely to be a fixture interaction as a real regression.

MEASUREMENT CONDITIONS THAT WORKED, since this suite is hard to admit: it took 22 attempts. Admission needs ZERO monitored CPUs above 20% across five consecutive 1s windows - not a low loadavg and not a low mean. The successful runs landed at loadavg 1.30-1.42. Run one harness at a time; two harnesses pinned to the same taskset cores do NOT trip each other's gate and silently contaminate both arms.

title: eigenvector_centrality_numpy: O(n³) dense eig vs nx Arnoldi (220x slower)
description:
fnx.eigenvector_centrality_numpy called np.linalg.eig on a dense to_numpy_array — O(n³) full decomposition. On a 200-node W-S graph: 692ms vs nx's 3.2ms (220x slower!).

nx delegates to scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs which uses Arnoldi iteration on the sparse adjacency, returning only the dominant eigenpair in O(n·E) iterations.

Fix: switch to scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs(A.csr, k=1, which='LR'). Fall back to the dense path only on ArpackNoConvergence (rare; small graphs where Arnoldi's restart constraint fails).

Result: 692ms -> 17.5ms (~40x faster). Parity vs nx: max delta 6e-16 (machine precision). 38 eigenvector tests pass; 17506 total tests pass.
notes: Fixed by switching to scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs (matches nx's algorithm exactly). 40x speedup.
