title: perf(storage): add_edges_from with EMPTY attr dicts leaves the graph in a slower state — 3.65% on preferential_attachment, 4.71% on degree(nbunch)
description:
Found by OliveDesert 2026-08-08 while resolving a discrepancy between two of my own probes on br-r37-c1-z00k8. It is a measurement trap AND a real lever.

THE OBSERVATION. The identical 1200-node/6000-edge graph, built two ways:
  g.add_edges_from([(u, v, {}) for u, v in stream])   <- what perf_harness._build_pair does
  g.add_edges_from(stream)                            <- bare 2-tuples
produces measurably different performance on reads afterwards:
  whole preferential_attachment call:  199.16us with {} vs 192.15us without  -> +3.65%
  degree(nbunch) 600 endpoints:        118.20us with {} vs 112.89us without  -> +4.71%
vs nx 198.40us, this is the difference between 0.9962x and 1.0325x — it flips the sign of the verdict.

An empty attr dict carries NO information. Passing {} should leave the graph in exactly the state that passing nothing does. It evidently does not: the empty dict appears to populate edge_py_attrs (or otherwise clear a pristine flag), and the over-conservative 'edge_py_attrs.is_empty()' style gates then refuse a fast path for edges that have no Python attributes at all.

LEVER: treat an empty attr dict as pristine at the batch-ingest boundary — do not record a Python attr entry for an edge whose attr dict is empty. Same family as the earlier pristine-gate relaxations.

MEASUREMENT TRAP WORTH KNOWING INDEPENDENTLY: any probe that rebuilds a harness workload with bare tuples instead of the harness's 3-tuples is measuring a DIFFERENT, faster graph. That is how my two probes disagreed 0.9833x vs 1.0336x on the same code. Transcribe _build_pair verbatim.

PARITY BAR: G.edges(data=True) must still report {} for those edges, and a later G[u][v]['k']=v write must still work. Verify edges_dirty/pristine-mirror semantics are not weakened for edges that DO have attrs.
close_reason: collect_plain_edge_batch now accepts (u,v,{}) as plain: preferential_attachment +3.65% -> +0.09%, degree(nbunch) +4.71% -> -1.61%, same-process A/B. Parity verified both directions incl. mixed arity and error contract; suite 50685 passed, 0 failed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED AT THE INGEST BOUNDARY, EXACTLY AS THIS BEAD PROPOSED (CopperCliff, 2026-08-08).

THE MECHANISM, confirmed in source: PyGraph::collect_plain_edge_batch (crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs:2698) had a flat 'if tuple.len() != 2 { return Ok(None) }'. A single (u, v, {}) item therefore bailed the ENTIRE plain batch, sending the build down try_add_attr_edge_batch, which populates edge_py_attrs — and the pristine-style gates then refuse fast paths for edges that have no Python attributes at all. That is the whole 'slower state'.

FIX: accept arity 3 when the third element is an EMPTY dict, treating it as a 2-tuple. A non-empty dict still bails to the attributed batch, and a non-dict third element still bails to the per-edge path that owns the error contract.

MEASURED as a same-process A/B between the two build styles — both arms fnx, so host drift cancels, which matters because this substrate's cross-run controls have been swinging 15% today. 1200 nodes / 5970 edges, 15 interleaved pairs, taskset 40-47:

  preferential_attachment   {}-built 125446.09us   bare 125334.07us   +0.09%   (was +3.65%)
  degree(nbunch) 600        {}-built     61.95us   bare     62.96us   -1.61%   (was +4.71%)

Both now sit within noise of zero: the {}-built graph is no longer in a slower state, which is the bead's stated goal.

PARITY, checked in both directions rather than just 'it still works': (u,v,{}) and (u,v) produce identical node order and identical edges(data=True) in BOTH nx and fnx; fnx matches nx for both styles; non-empty attrs still round-trip; a mixed-arity bunch ((u,v), (u,v,{}), (u,v,{w:1}) plus plain pairs) matches nx exactly; and a bad third element (an int) still raises TypeError in both libraries. Full Python suite 50685 passed, 1081 skipped, 0 FAILED. clippy clean, cargo fmt --check --all 0 diffs.

FOLLOW-UP I DID NOT TAKE, so nobody assumes it is covered: the two exact-int fast paths (lib.rs:2871 and :3241) and the sibling at :7213 carry the same flat 'len() != 2' bail. With int nodes, (u,v,{}) now lands in the GENERAL plain collect rather than the int-index one — correct and no longer attr-polluting, but it misses the int fast path's speed. Extending the same empty-dict acceptance there is a clean, separable follow-up.

The measurement trap this bead documents is unaffected and still worth heeding: a probe that rebuilds a harness workload with bare tuples is measuring a different graph. After this fix the two are equivalent for the plain case, which removes the trap for exactly that shape.

The recursive variant's nx-typed return is a deliberate residual from br-r37-c1-56nd2 and is now pinned by a test rather than left implicit.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: FIXED in 75d0bb763. The bead left the direction open ('whoever takes this should pick ONE'); the codebase already answered it.

WHICH SIDE MOVES, decided on evidence rather than taste - every other graph-returning surface here
returns fnx types:
    complete_to_chordal_graph -> franken_networkx
    subgraph().copy()         -> franken_networkx
    k_core                    -> franken_networkx
    get_counterexample        -> franken_networkx
    check_planarity(ce=True)  -> networkx.classes.graph   <- the lone outlier
plus planarity.py's own docstring promising 'return fnx graph types instead of NetworkX graphs'. So
check_planarity moved, and now type(check_planarity(G, counterexample=True)[1]) is
type(get_counterexample(G)).

FIXED IN THE SHARED HELPER (_check_planarity_certificate), not in the namespace wrapper, so the
top-level fnx.check_planarity and fnx.planarity.check_planarity move together - they are two
spellings of one path, and a test asserts they return the same concrete class. Letting those drift is
the exact bug class this repo keeps hitting (see br-r37-c1-2qsqf, br-r37-c1-s2nw9).

THE GATE IS EXACT and is the part most worth reviewing: conversion is conditioned on is_planar being
False, NOT on 'the certificate is a graph'. The planar branch's certificate is a PlanarEmbedding,
deliberately kept as nx's class so isinstance and check_structure() keep working. Tested over 3
planar fixtures x both counterexample values - the embedding survives and check_structure() passes.

ATTRIBUTES: a type conversion is where attributes vanish, so that is asserted too - node attrs, edge
attrs and graph attrs all identical to live nx on an attributed K5, plus structural parity on K5,
K3,3 and K6.

RESIDUAL, deliberately NOT fixed and now asserted rather than left implicit: check_planarity_recursive
is bound DIRECTLY to networkx's own function (a decision recorded under br-r37-c1-56nd2, since
upstream already handles backend dispatch), so it returns nx types and is inconsistent with its
non-recursive sibling. That is exact nx parity for that name at the cost of internal consistency.
Widening this bead to wrap it would have undone another bead's documented choice, so instead there is
a test pinning the binding and the nx return type - whoever wraps it later gets a failure pointing at
the decision instead of a surprise.

NOTE ON THE BEAD'S OWN SUGGESTION: it proposed possibly having the override 'feed the native store on
assignment' to fix all rebuild-from-_node paths at once. Not attempted - that is a much larger
behavioural change and this bead's evidence does not support it.

20 new tests; 1556 passed across planar|chordal|coverage_gaps; ubs 0 critical 0 warning on the new
file.

title: test: directed reverse involution + degree-swap + SCC-preservation invariants
description: reverse(G) flips each arc; reverse is an involution (reverse(reverse(G))==G); in_degree(reverse)==out_degree(G); node/edge counts unchanged; SCCs preserved under reversal. Cross-checks reverse vs degree views + strongly_connected_components. 80 cases.
close_reason: This file was ALREADY strong on the axis that has failed most others - it pins the arc SET, not a count, and compares degree dicts keyed by node rather than degree sequences, so the usual count-blindness gap did not apply. I checked for it first and am recording that it was absent rather than inventing one. What the file could not see is what RIDES on the arcs and HOW the result is produced. Three surfaces, all verified before assertion. (1) ATTRIBUTES: node, edge and graph attributes all survive the flip, the attributes follow their arc to the flipped position (rev.edges[1,0] == g.edges[0,1]), and the attribute dicts are INDEPENDENT - writing through the reverse leaves the original at 5, and live networkx 3.6.1 behaves identically, so that is pinned as shared contract rather than reported as a divergence. (2) COPY vs VIEW: reverse(copy=False) returns a LIVE FROZEN view - it picks up a later parent add_edge(2,3) as (3,2) and raises NetworkXError on direct mutation - while reverse(copy=True) is a snapshot that a later parent edit does not reach. Neither side was exercised, and live-view-where-a-copy-is-expected is a bug class that has shipped in this codebase before (see the k-core work on br-r37-c1-wdvpt). (3) SELF-LOOPS and MULTIDIGRAPHS: the random generator excludes u == v by construction, so a loop reversing to itself was never tested; and MultiDiGraph reversal preserves parallel-arc KEYS and their per-key attributes, matching nx exactly, with the involution still holding once keys are in play. A PROBE BUG OF MINE, noted because it cost a run: my first probe sorted MultiDiGraph keys mixing int and str, raising TypeError. That was my scratch code, not the library; the fix was to stringify keys before sorting. Evidence: file 80 -> 84 passed, no skips - the four additions are fixed witnesses, so the file gained new SURFACES rather than more cases, and I am not claiming a case-count win; 178 passed across the reverse family (directed_reverse_copy_parity, reverse_iteration_order_parity, directed_subgraph_reverse_conformance_guard). Crate-scoped, not a workspace run. Committed b3259f131, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check. Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: [perf] resistance_distance single-pair builds full dense O(n^3) pinv
description: resistance_distance(G, nodeA, nodeB) with both endpoints (the common single-scalar call, __init__.py ~L25485) builds the full Laplacian pseudo-inverse via np.linalg.pinv(L, hermitian=True) -- O(n^3) dense -- then reads two diagonal + two off-diagonal entries. The single effective resistance r(i,j)=(e_i-e_j)^T L^+ (e_i-e_j) only needs one solve of the reduced (grounded) Laplacian: drop one node, sparse-SPD solve L_red x = (e_i-e_j)_red, r = x_i - x_j. Same Woodbury/fundamental-matrix family as br-socwoodbury (bbb9f82b9). The dict/all-pairs return shapes genuinely need the full pinv -- gate the fast path on (nodeA is not None and nodeB is not None). Keep dense pinv fallback; golden sha256 (rounded) old==new==nx. Target: O(n^3)->~O(nnz) sparse solve, 50-100x on large sparse graphs for the single-pair call. See memory reference_woodbury_nsolves_in_loop.
close_reason: Shipped ab8aecbdd: grounded reduced-Laplacian sparse solve, O(n^3)->O(nnz), 225-1265x, golden sha sparse==dense==nx

title: [perf] SubgraphView.copy() 19.8x slower than nx (50-node sub of 2000-node G) — scans all parent edges O(E_total) instead of O(E_subgraph)
description:
SubgraphView.copy() 19.8x slower than nx (50-node sub of 2000-node G). cProfile root cause: generic _FilteredGraphView enumerates visible nodes by SCANNING ALL parent nodes (__iter__ -> _node_visible -> 'node in parent' PyO3) on every nodes()/_nbunch()/__len__ call = O(V_total) several times per copy (376k _node_visible for 50 copies); nodes(data=True) also walks ALL parent node-data.

DUAL FINDING - ALSO A PARITY BUG: nx FilterAtlas.__iter__ uses '2*len(subset) < len(parent)': small subgraphs iterate the node SET (CPython set order), large ones parent order. fnx always parent order -> node order diverges from nx in 46/160 random cases, ALL with 2k<n. e.g. nx [26,12,22,23] vs fnx [12,22,23,26].

REAL LEVER (target ~15-20x AND parity fix): store allowed_nodes set on the subgraph view; replicate nx FilterAtlas iteration exactly (2*len<len -> set order else parent order). Makes visible-node enumeration O(|sub|) AND matches nx order. Blast radius: generic filtered view (subgraph/edge_subgraph/subgraph_view) -> needs full differential vs nx + fnx test updates for any current-order asserts. Careful multi-step, not a rush.

REJECTED micro-lever (cc): byte-exact copy() (enumerate once + direct parent attr fetch + _edges(nbunch=visible)) preserves parent order so only 1.17x (O(V_total) list(self) remains); 180/180 byte-exact but fails Score>=2.0, not shipped per no-ceiling addendum. Set-iteration order change is mandatory for the real win.
notes:
BEING HANDLED BY TealSpring (do not duplicate): __init__.py working tree (uncommitted) has the full fix - FilterAtlas-aware _FilteredGraphView.__iter__/nodes + _NodeSetFilter(copy_nodes=False) so the allowed_nodes set is stored WITHOUT re-wrapping. Root cause confirmed by cc: _NodeSetFilter did set(already_built_set) which presizes the hash table differently than NetworkX incremental set(generator), giving a different CPython slot order -> 21/160 node-order divergences. With copy_nodes=False: 0/160 vs nx (verified). Perf already 19.8x->8x via the fast branch; residual 8x is result-graph CONSTRUCTION tax (separate). cc backed off __init__.py (TealSpring lock + active uncommitted work).

FINAL EVIDENCE: committed proof uses final rebench numbers: hyperfine fnx 669.6ms -> 499.8ms, nx comparator 192.4ms -> 204.0ms, remaining gap nx 2.45x faster; focused legacy-vs-after min 0.1804s -> 0.0437s; NetworkX golden parity hash matches after fnx.
close_reason: Completed: FilterAtlas-style sparse node iteration for SubgraphView; fnx copy benchmark 669.6ms -> 446.1ms, golden parity hash matches NetworkX

title: min_edge_cover / max_weight_matching delegate to networkx via full fnx->nx conversion (0.80-0.93x)
description: fnx.max_weight_matching (and min_weight_matching) DELEGATE to networkx: cProfile of min_edge_cover shows the work is networkx/algorithms/matching.py (assignLabel/addBlossom/max_weight_matching) plus a full _fnx_to_nx conversion (backend.py:606, ~0.98s/300 calls). So min_edge_cover is 0.80x and max_weight_matching ~0.93x nx (conversion overhead on top of nx's own blossom). No native blossom kernel exists. LEVER: port Galil's blossom (weighted general matching) to safe Rust — but it is highly order-sensitive (the matched edge SET on ties depends on nx's exact node/edge iteration + dual-variable update order), so byte-exact parity is hard (cf reference_order_sensitive_rebuild_benchmark_artifact: matching gaps are partly graph-layout benchmark artifacts too). min_edge_cover needs max-CARDINALITY matching specifically; a maximum_matching (Hopcroft-Karp/Blossom) native kernel emitting edges in nx order would close it. Multi-session, kernel work. Affects matching family + min_edge_cover + min_weight_matching.
notes: cod-a triage 2026-06-18: blocker is semantic, not environmental. Public max_weight_matching/min_weight_matching are deliberately delegated because exact NetworkX contract includes pair direction and tie-choice order. Existing Rust blossom adapter sorts node names and blossom edges, indexes lexicographically, and emits canonical left_index<right_index tuples, which breaks tests that require NetworkX DFS/adjacency-order tuple orientation and matching choice. Safe de-delegation needs a full NetworkX-order Galil blossom port or a proven exact-orientation/tie gate; a wrapper flip would be incorrect for bipartite/complete tie cases and min_edge_cover default depends on maxcardinality matching.

title: [perf] current_flow_betweenness dense O(n^3) Gauss-Jordan inversion is the floor (nx uses sparse solves)
description: After parallelizing the source-sink triple loop (cfbpar), current_flow_betweenness is ~parity with nx (n=300 0.71x, n=500 1.25x, n=700 1.05x) — the remaining floor is the full DENSE O(n^3) Laplacian inverse via Gauss-Jordan (sequential). nx computes current-flow betweenness via SPARSE linear solves (scipy splu/cg per source/edge) over the reduced Laplacian, not a full dense inverse, so it scales better as n grows. LEVERS: (a) parallelize the Gauss-Jordan elimination (per-column: the row-elimination loop is independent across rows; thread::scope with chunks_mut + a pivot-row snapshot; gate on n and watch per-column spawn overhead); (b) BETTER: own safe-Rust sparse Cholesky/LU on the reduced Laplacian + per-source solves (the BLAS-class mandate), avoiding the dense inverse entirely -> O(n*nnz) not O(n^3). Same applies to current_flow_closeness/information_centrality/edge_current_flow (all build the same dense L_pinv). Bit-exactness: keep the deterministic per-s ordered reduction already in place.
close_reason: FALSE PREMISE — closing. The public fnx.current_flow_betweenness_centrality DELEGATES to nx via _call_networkx_for_parity (the Rust current_flow_betweenness_centrality_rust kernel is DEAD CODE for the public path — only a docstring references it; it was abandoned because it was ~2.5x off nx). So: (1) the dense O(n^3) Gauss-Jordan 'floor' is in nx's own code, not fnx's hot path; (2) the fnx->nx conversion is only ~1% (5ms of 475ms); (3) interleaved min-of-6 shows cfb = 1.01x vs nx (PARITY) — the earlier '1.95x slower' was HOST NOISE (load swung 9->72). NOTE: last session's e3a79a847 parallelized the DEAD Rust kernel — harmless (still bit-exact in Rust tests) but it does NOT affect the public path; its '1.95x->parity' claim was a phantom (noise). A genuine native cfb would need porting nx's flow_matrix algorithm onto fnx's existing _SuperLUInverseLaplacian (like current_flow_closeness, which is native+sparse and 0.55x), but only solver='lu'/'cg' would beat nx; default solver='full' is dense either way so no default-path win. Not worth it at current parity. LESSON: verify dispatch path (delegate vs native kernel) + use interleaved min-of-N (host swings 2.5x) BEFORE optimizing.

title: test: Whitney's connectivity inequality (kappa<=lambda<=delta)
description: Whitney's theorem: node_connectivity <= edge_connectivity <= min_degree, cross-checking the three measures + closed forms (K_n all n-1, cycle all 2, tree all 1). Oracle-free classic connectivity theorem. ~60 cases.
close_reason: The inequality chain was a weak instrument and the values were never pinned. test_whitney_connectivity_inequality.py asserted kappa <= lambda <= delta on 50 random seeds plus closed forms for K_n / cycle / tree. MUTANT, measured: an implementation returning kappa = lambda = 0 for every graph satisfies 0 <= 0 <= delta and passes the chain on 38/38 connected draws - the chain constrains ORDER, not VALUE, and the closed forms pin values only on three named graphs, never on the random family. The new definition guard catches that mutant 38/38. COVERAGE HOLE, measured: the chain test skips the 12 disconnected seeds of its 50, so kappa == lambda == 0 on a disconnected graph - the one case where the degenerate answer is the CORRECT answer - was never tested; it is now, and holds 12/12. Added, all verified before assertion: kappa and lambda pinned by their definitions as minima of local connectivity over pairs (lambda over all pairs 38/38; kappa over NON-ADJACENT pairs 37/37, guarded for K_n which has none); the value-1 characterisations lambda==1 iff has_bridges (38/38) and kappa==1 iff an articulation point exists (38/38), which pin the boundary the chain is loosest at; disconnected graphs have zero connectivity (12/12); and Chartrand's bound, min degree >= floor(n/2) forcing lambda == delta rather than merely <= (13/13 applicable). Also added a regime guard asserting the family keeps >=5 disconnected, >=20 connected and >=3 distinct edge-connectivity values, so these sweeps cannot silently go vacuous the way a random family can. SKIP ACCOUNTING, since the file now reports 111 skips: they are complementary filters over the same 50 seeds - 38 connected / 12 disconnected partition the family exactly, and Chartrand applies to 13 of the 38 - so every seed is exercised by some test and no case is silently dropped. Evidence: file 59 -> 149 passed + 111 skipped; 268 passed + 111 skipped across the connectivity family (connectivity, connectivity_metamorphic_invariants, connectivity_parity_extras, connectivity_empty_graph_parity, connectivity_cross_type). Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: test: distance-metric cross-function invariants (ecc/radius/diameter/center/periphery/wiener)
description: Cross-function distance identities: radius<=diameter<=2*radius; radius=min ecc, diameter=max ecc; center/periphery = ecc-extremal nodes; ecc(v)=max distance from v; wiener=distsum/2; triangle inequality on distance matrix + ecc nx parity. Mutually pins ecc/radius/diameter/center/periphery/all_pairs/wiener. ~80 cases.
close_reason: THE SKIP HID A NON-UNIFORM CONTRACT - the interesting part is that the family does NOT behave alike. Both sweeps skip disconnected graphs (10 of 40 draws) and discard them. On a disconnected graph, distances between components are infinite, and the six functions split: eccentricity, radius, diameter, center and periphery all raise NetworkXError, while wiener_index instead SUMS those infinities and returns inf. Both behaviours match live networkx 3.6.1 exactly. I am pinning that split precisely because the natural assumption - that a whole family of distance functions refuses disconnected input uniformly - is wrong here, and a test author skipping the case would never find out. This is the third bead in a row where pytest.skip turned out to mark an untested BRANCH rather than an inapplicable one. PARITY WAS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKED: only eccentricity was compared against networkx. radius, diameter, center, periphery and wiener_index were constrained ONLY by the internal identities relating them to ecc - so a consistent error in the shared machinery would satisfy every identity while diverging from nx. All five are now compared directly (0 mismatches on 30 connected draws, verified before asserting). THE METRIC LAW ON ONE GRAPH: the triangle inequality was checked on cycle_graph(8) alone. It now runs over the random family, and I added the two metric axioms the bead identity list never mentions - a zero diagonal and symmetry d(a,b)==d(b,a) - since "the distance matrix is a metric" is three laws and only one was present. Evidence: file 80 -> 122 passed + 40 skipped (the same 10 disconnected draws now appearing across four sweeps rather than two; the underlying skip rate is unchanged at 10/40, and the new disconnected test covers what those skips discard); 376 passed + 40 skipped across the distance family (distance_metric_metamorphic, wiener_index_closed_forms, distance_measures_parity). Crate-scoped and inline with a timeout cap; no background jobs left running. Committed 086633bd2, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check. Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: test: maximal_matching validity + 2-approximation bound
description: maximal_matching is a valid matching (no shared endpoints) + maximal (no addable edge) + 2-approximation (maximum/2 <= maximal <= maximum) + matching <= floor(n/2); K_2m perfect matching size m. Cross-checks maximal_matching/max_weight_matching. Distinct from Gallai (egqvc). ~80 cases.
close_reason: Matched pairs were never required to be EDGES, and the 2-approximation was slack on most draws. MUTANT, measured: a 'maximal matching' built from NON-ADJACENT pairs is constructible on all 40 draws and passes both pre-existing structural checks - disjointness and maximality - on 24 of them, because neither says the pairs come from the graph; the smallest witness is {(0,2)} on a 4-cycle, which is disjoint and leaves no edge with both endpoints unmatched. The new g.has_edge(u,v) guard rejects it 40/40. BOUND SLACKNESS, measured: maximal == maximum on 31 of the 40 random draws, so 'maximal >= maximum/2' is trivially satisfied there and the bound only bites on 9. Two things added rather than one: a TIGHTNESS WITNESS proving the bound is attained, not merely satisfied - inserting the middle edge of a 4-path first makes greedy take it and block both ends, giving maximal 1 against maximum 2, exactly half (and 2 against 3 for the 6-path form) - and a regime guard asserting at least 5 of the 40 draws have maximal < maximum (measured 9), so the sweep cannot drift to a family where the bound holds trivially everywhere. Also added the floor(n/2) cap on the maximal matching itself; it was previously asserted only for the maximum matching. Confirmed the pre-existing use of max_weight_matching without maxcardinality is correct here: on unweighted graphs all weights are 1, so maximum weight and maximum cardinality coincide. Gallai (matching + edge cover == n) deliberately left to br-r37-c1-egqvc, which the bead assigns it to. Evidence: file 81 -> 83 passed, no skips (2 new tests are single-case witnesses, not sweeps; the sweeps grew in assertion strength, not count); 194 passed + 10 skipped across the matching family (maximal_matching_native_parity, matching_coloring_closed_forms, gallai_matching_edge_cover, matching, matching_additional). Crate-scoped to the matching tests, not a workspace run. Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: test: BFS/DFS tree distance invariants (tree depth <-> shortest paths)
description: bfs_tree depth(v)==shortest-path-distance(root,v) (BFS=shortest paths unweighted); dfs_tree depth>=distance; both span reachable nodes as trees (n-1 edges). Cross-checks bfs_tree/dfs_tree/single_source_shortest_path_length. Edge parity covered separately (2wi7g); this pins the DISTANCE property. ~81 cases.
close_reason: EDGE PROVENANCE AND ORIENTATION, neither of which the depth comparison can see. The file checked that each tree spans exactly the reachable nodes, has n-1 edges, and that BFS depth equals the shortest-path distance. None of that says the tree EDGES came from G, and none of it says which way they point. Both now required to be built from G edges (40/40 verified before asserting), and the BFS tree must be DIRECTED with every edge increasing depth by exactly one - which is the structural content of "tree rooted at r" that a depth map alone does not capture, since a depth map is equally consistent with an unoriented or reversed edge set. ONE ROOT ONLY: the sweep roots at node 0 on every draw. Rooting from every node takes the BFS invariant from 40 checks to 156, all holding. THE INEQUALITY, handled as on br-r37-c1-ehb6v: dfs depth >= dist is satisfied by equality everywhere, and a DFS tree may LEGITIMATELY equal the BFS tree, so asserting strictness would be asserting something false about graphs in general. Measured instead - the family separates them on 33 of 40 draws - and the guard requires the family to keep separating them, which protects the inequality without overclaiming. PARAMETERS the sweep never varies, all compared against live networkx 3.6.1: directed traversal following out-edges only, reverse=True following in-edges instead, and depth_limit for limits 1..3 - the last checked twice over, for parity with nx AND for actually bounding the returned depth, since a depth_limit that is silently ignored would still match nx only if nx ignored it too. Evidence: file 81 -> 143 passed, no skips; 241 passed across the traversal family (traversal_tree_parity, traversal_cross_type). Crate-scoped and inline with a timeout cap; no background jobs left running. Committed 693ea47be, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check. Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: test: complement involution + degree relationship invariants
description: complement(complement(G))==G (involution); deg_complement(v)=(n-1)-deg(v); |E(G)|+|E(comp)|=C(n,2); same nodes; complement(K_n)=empty, complement(empty)=K_n. Cross-checks complement vs degree+edges. Distinct from set-algebra (cluiw) + clique-duality (z0f6q). ~44 cases.
close_reason: Counts and degrees say HOW MANY edges move, not WHICH. The file asserted the involution, the per-node degree relation deg_comp(v) = (n-1) - deg(v), the edge-count partition and the node set - but never the defining rule itself. Two graphs can share a per-node degree map and still differ in adjacency, so the rule was the one thing unpinned. Now asserted directly over every pair on 40 draws: comp.has_edge(u,v) iff G does not (40/40 verified before writing), plus that no self-loop appears in the complement, which a pair-wise sweep over u<v combinations structurally cannot see. THE RETURNED OBJECT, the axis that has been productive on the last few transformation beads: nothing said what kind of graph comes back. It is a SNAPSHOT, not a live view - I verified this with a discriminating mutation, having first written a useless one: my initial probe added (0,3) to the parent of a 4-path and checked the complement, but (0,3) was ALREADY in that complement, so the check proved nothing. The real test removes a parent edge (which a live complement would ADD) and adds a parent node (which would add several), and neither reaches the result. It is also MUTABLE, unlike a subgraph view, which is the contrast that makes the distinction worth pinning. ATTRIBUTES: the complement keeps the node SET and drops node and graph attributes entirely. That is surprising enough to look like a bug, so I checked live networkx 3.6.1 before writing it up - nx drops them identically - and it is pinned as shared contract in both directions rather than filed as a divergence. Also added self-loops, which the u<v generator cannot produce by construction, and the directed and multigraph forms: a directed complement fills in every non-arc ORDERED pair, and multiplicity carries into a multigraph complement (both matching nx exactly). Evidence: file 44 -> 88 passed, no skips; 258 passed across the complement family (clique_complement_duality, operator_attr_merge_conformance_guard). Crate-scoped and inline with a timeout cap; no background jobs left running. Committed 02335772c, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check. title: information_centrality: O(N²) Python inner loop dominates (~400ms of 468ms)
description:
fnx.information_centrality (alias of current_flow_closeness_centrality) ran 468ms vs nx's 27.5ms on a 200-node W-S graph (17x slower).

Breakdown:
  is_connected:          0.07ms
  cuthill-mckee:         4.0ms
  laplacian_matrix:      8.5ms
  relabel_nodes:        20.0ms
  LU construct:          1.1ms
  200x get_row:          9.2ms
  inner loop overhead: ~425ms (the bottleneck)

The O(N^2) Python double-loop calling row.item(node) and row.item(other) for n=200 means 40,000 iterations.

Fix: the inner loop is mathematically equivalent to two vectorized numpy ops per outer iteration:
  centrality[node] += n * row[node] - 2 * row.sum()
  centrality_arr += row[node]  # broadcast

Result: 468ms -> 46.78ms (~10x faster). Parity vs nx: max delta 3.12e-17 (machine precision). 18 tests pass; 17506 total tests pass.
notes: Fixed by vectorizing the O(N^2) inner loop to two numpy ops per outer iteration.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: FIXED in 260ed3b17. Smaller than the deferral anticipated - an export-surface change, not a three-file refactor. Nothing was relocated; one import moved.

RESULT, all four module paths now agreeing with live nx 3.6.1:
    fnx.drawing.generate_network_text   resolved  ->  AttributeError (nx: AttributeError)
    fnx.drawing.write_network_text      resolved  ->  AttributeError (nx: AttributeError)
    fnx.generate_network_text / write_network_text   still resolve (nx: resolve)
    fnx.readwrite[.text]                            unchanged (nx: resolve)

TWO OF THIS BEAD'S OWN ASSUMPTIONS DID NOT HOLD, and both cost a wrong attempt before being caught:

1. 'relocate both definitions to the readwrite.text module' is not available. fnx has no
   readwrite/text.py - fnx.readwrite.text ALREADY resolves to networkx's own readwrite/text.py by
   fallthrough, which is precisely the parity wanted. Creating an fnx module of that name would
   SHADOW nx's and be a regression.

2. Importing the top-level names from franken_networkx.readwrite is the obvious move and is an
   INFINITE RECURSION: readwrite's generate_network_text/write_network_text are FORWARDERS that call
   back into the top-level name, so binding the top level from there makes it call itself. I hit it,
   traced it, and the import now points at drawing.nx_pylab (the definition site) with a comment
   recording why, so nobody 'fixes' it back.

A third trap, same category: drawing/nx_pylab.py imports from the package at module level, so the
import must sit AFTER the existing top-level drawing block - placing it beside the other readwrite
imports is a circular import at load.

Worth noting for the dual-implementation ledger: my first differential 'proved' the drawing and
readwrite versions agreed across 300 comparisons. They agreed because they are the SAME code -
readwrite forwards. A differential between a function and its own forwarder proves nothing; the
recursion is what exposed it.

TESTS, all three of the bead's named requirements plus the trap:
  hasattr(fnx.drawing, name) is False and hasattr(fnx, name) stays True  - asserted against live nx
    on every module path rather than hard-coded, so an upstream move reports itself
  fnx.readwrite.text exposes them exactly as nx does                     - asserted
  test_drawing_package_star_export_surface_matches_networkx must not regress - re-checked here using
    nx's public dir(), because nx.drawing declares no __all__
  plus a regression pinning the readwrite forwarder against recursion

title: fix(private storage): copy/deepcopy/pickle drop an assigned _node mapping that nx preserves
description:
Found while verifying br-r37-c1-padm6 (native __contains__ private-override probe), on HEAD with a
build matching the working tree.

REPRO (all four classes, identical):
  g = fnx.Graph(); g.add_nodes_from(['a', 7, 2.5]); g._node = {'x': {}}
  ('x' in g, 'a' in g)                      -> (True, False)   matches nx
  h = copy.copy(g) / copy.deepcopy(g) / pickle round-trip
  ('x' in h, 'a' in h)  fnx -> (False, True)
                        nx  -> (True,  False)

nx has no __deepcopy__/__reduce_ex__ override on Graph, so the default protocol copies the instance
__dict__ and the assigned _node mapping comes along. fnx's _graph_deepcopy and
_make_reduce_ex_preserving_frozen both skip every key.startswith('_fnx_'), and the native __copy__
builds a fresh instance dict, so the assigned mapping is dropped and the clone reverts to the native
store.

NOT caused by padm6: the skip predates bc49b6c08 (two key.startswith('_fnx_') sites exist in
bc49b6c08^) and that commit did not touch either path. fnx's clone is internally CONSISTENT
(__contains__, has_node and the nodes view all agree) — this is a copy-semantics parity gap, not a
flag desync; the consistency half is already locked by
tests/python/test_private_node_override_membership.py::test_clones_of_a_private_storage_graph_stay_self_consistent.

FIX SKETCH: the _fnx_ prefix skip is too broad. It exists to stop memoised views (bound to the
source graph) from leaking into the clone. The private-storage override slots are DATA, not caches,
so they need to be carried over — and carried through _set_private_override on the target so the
native private_node_override flag is armed on the clone, not written straight into its __dict__.

TEST THE FIX MUST CARRY: for all four classes and all three clone paths, an assigned _node mapping
survives with nx's answers, AND the clone's __contains__/has_node/nodes agree with each other (the
desync negative case). Also cover a clone of a graph WITHOUT private storage — it must not gain the
flag.
close_reason: Fixed in 745bb70b2: copy.copy, copy.deepcopy and pickle now carry an assigned _node/_adj/_succ/_pred exactly as networkx does, on all four graph classes, including nx's sharing semantics (copy shares the mapping, deepcopy isolates it). Re-applied through the public attribute names so the clone's method shadows are rebuilt bound to the clone rather than the source. The two existing tests that encoded the old behaviour were updated — one had explicitly pinned the divergence and named this bead as its tracker, the other's anti-aliasing purpose was preserved and strengthened. G.copy() remains divergent and is split out as br-r37-c1-93mx3.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: FIXED in 745bb70b2 for the copy PROTOCOL; the G.copy() path is split out as br-r37-c1-93mx3.

THE BEAD'S REPRO, all four classes x all three paths, now matching live nx 3.6.1:
    g = Cls(); g.add_nodes_from(['a', 7, 2.5]); g._node = {'x': {}}
    base (True, False) on both sides; copy / deepcopy / pickle all (True, False) on both sides.
Before: fnx gave (False, True) on all three.

MECHANISM confirmed rather than assumed: assigning _node does NOT put '_node' in vars(g) - it is
intercepted into _fnx_private_node_override and installs bound-method shadows (has_node,
number_of_nodes, order, ...). Since every copy path skips key.startswith('_fnx_'), the override was
dropped. Fixed by capturing the four private stores and RE-ASSIGNING them through their public names
(_node/_adj/_succ/_pred) on the clone, which re-runs the installer so shadows are bound to the CLONE.
Copying the _fnx_private_* keys across verbatim would have handed the clone shadows still bound to
the original graph - a subtler bug than the one being fixed.

SHARING SEMANTICS also verified against nx, not just membership: copy.copy SHARES the mapping object
(clone._node is the same object; a write through the clone is visible in the source) and
copy.deepcopy ISOLATES it. fnx matches nx on both.

TWO EXISTING TESTS CHANGED, neither a weakening:
1. test_native_contains_switches_to_private_node_mapping_and_resets_on_copies pinned the divergence
   ON PURPOSE - its own comment reads 'networkx 3.6.1 does the opposite here ... these three lines
   pin fnx's CURRENT contract, not networkx parity' and names THIS bead. Flipped the copy-protocol
   half to nx parity; left the G.copy() third pinned.
2. test_private_node_method_shadows_do_not_alias_copy_or_pickle asserted a clone carries NO internal
   shadows. That was a valid proxy only while clones dropped the override; a clone answering from an
   assigned mapping needs them. Its named purpose is kept and made STRICTER: every shadow present
   must satisfy __self__ is other, never the source.

ONE OF MY OWN NEW TESTS WAS USELESS AT FIRST and is worth recording: a behavioural probe of shadow
binding passed with AND without the fix, because with no override 'clone._node[k] = {}' just writes
to the clone's native store and answers identically. Replaced with a __self__ identity assertion and
confirmed it fires when the fix is disabled at runtime.

RESIDUAL (br-r37-c1-93mx3): G.copy() still rebuilds from native storage where nx rebuilds from the
assigned _node - nx private=True/native=False, fnx the reverse. Not part of the copy protocol and not
in this bead's repro.

42 new tests; 341 passed in the two touched files; 1546 passed across the
copy|deepcopy|pickle|frozen|private|descriptor selection; ubs 0 critical 0 warning.

title: perf: audit binding sites that materialize Vec<Vec<String>> then re-resolve via py_node_key (cycle_basis pattern)
description: cycle_basis (e4569e12b) was 1.9x slower largely because the kernel allocated a String per output node and the PyO3 binding re-resolved each via gr.py_node_key. AUDIT other delegated/native algorithms returning Vec<Vec<String>> or large Vec<String> node lists where the binding maps each via py_node_key: candidates = minimum_cycle_basis, all_simple_paths, all_shortest_paths, biconnected_components, connected_components listings, cycle enumeration, k_components. Lever: kernel returns indices; binding builds node_objs once over nodes_ordered() then indexes. Measure each: small per-pair outputs won't benefit, large multi-node outputs will.
close_reason: Audited. The index->PyObject lever only wins big for OUTPUT-MATERIALIZATION-bound functions (cycle_basis: output spans most nodes, each in many cycles -> String alloc + per-occurrence py_node_key dominated -> 2.9x faster after fix). Applied to enumerate_all_cliques (d83cc22b0, byte-exact, 1.65x->1.51x, modest because that fn is ALGORITHM-bound not materialization-bound). all_simple_paths: index lever is NEUTRAL (tried+reverted) — bottleneck is DFS traversal + per-call neighbor sort + PyO3 path materialization, NOT String output; nx does no sort so fnx stays ~1.4x on medium / parity on heavy. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SATISFIED AT 6 CASES — BUT THE FIXTURE HAD NO ATTRIBUTES, SO THE MERGE CONFLICT WAS NEVER RESOLVED
(CopperCliff, 2026-08-08).

tests/python/test_relabel_edge_cases_parity.py already existed and matched this bead: non-injective
merge, merge-into-existing, swap, partial mapping, the copy-vs-in-place collision contract, and
convert_node_labels_to_integers — 6 cases, exactly the figure specified. I checked before writing.

GAP 1 — NO ATTRIBUTES ANYWHERE. The fixture is `Graph([(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,3)])` with no node or
edge data, so nothing tested what relabel does to attributes. That matters most on the case this
module leads with: when 1 and 2 both map to "X" they MERGE, and one set of node attributes has to
win. networkx keeps the LAST mapped node's (tag == "t2", not "t1"); fnx matches. A merge that kept
the FIRST would produce the identical node set, the identical edge set, and pass every assertion in
the file.

GAP 2 — `str()`-MAPPED SORTED COMPARISON, which is a poor fit on this surface specifically. relabel
maps BETWEEN TYPES — `{3: 0}` produces an int label, `{0: "a"}` a str — so a relabel emitting the
string "0" where networkx emits the int 0 compares equal after `str()`. And relabel node ORDER is
load-bearing enough here that two other modules exist for it
(test_relabel_node_order_parity, test_relabel_order_parity_vs_networkx), yet this one sorted it away.

MEASURED BEFORE ASSERTING, all four mappings plus convert_node_labels_to_integers: node label types,
node ORDER, edge ORDER, node attributes, edge attributes — 0 divergences. The merge winner is `t2` in
both libraries.

MUTATION-CHECKED: take the real merged graph and change only the surviving node's attribute from t2
to t1 — the wrong merge winner. It has the SAME node set and the SAME edge set, so the existing
comparison PASSES it; the new attribute assertion FAILS it.

Cases 6 -> 16. File: 16 passed. Full Python suite: 52074 passed, 1093 skipped, 0 FAILED.

title: gomory_hu_tree errors on graphs nx handles (isolated nodes, disconnected with capacities, selfloop-only)
description: Three edge cases where fnx.gomory_hu_tree raises NetworkXUnbounded while nx returns a valid tree: (1) isolated nodes only [fnx.Graph(); g.add_nodes_from([0,1,2])] — nx returns star tree with cut_value=0, fnx errors via 'not is_connected' gate; (2) disconnected graph with explicit capacities [g.add_edge(0,1,capacity=5); g.add_edge(2,3,capacity=5)] — nx returns tree connecting all nodes with cross-component weight=0, fnx errors; (3) only selfloops [g.add_edge(0,0); g.add_edge(1,1)] — nx returns tree edge (0,1) with weight=0, fnx errors via inf-capacity check (selfloops have no capacity attr but are irrelevant to inter-node cuts). Root cause: fnx's 'not is_connected OR _flow_has_infinite_capacity' gate is too aggressive. Fix: (a) drop the is_connected short-circuit — rely on the inf-capacity check (which catches the regression-locked disc-with-edges-no-cap and complete_graph-no-cap cases); (b) exclude selfloops from the inf-capacity check since selfloops contribute nothing to inter-node cuts. _minimum_cut_raw correctly returns 0 for cross-component or selfloop-only pairs, so the tree-construction loop builds the right tree without the over-broad gates.
close_reason: Replaced 'not is_connected OR inf_cap' gate with 'any non-selfloop edge with missing/inf capacity'. 6-variant parity probe matches nx; 16 gomory_hu tests pass including the regression-lock.

title: perf[DEEP]: bulk-construction residual is canonical-String-key allocation (~8-10 String allocs/edge) — interned integer node-id substrate target 2-3x
description:
Profiled 2026-06-12 (cc). After the add_edges_from batch fast-path (br-r37-c1-71x9k, closed) the residual construction tax is intrinsic String allocation, NOT per-edge add_edge dispatch. add_edges_from(6000 plain int 2-tuples onto empty_graph(1500)) = ~3.0ms; converting set->list saves <0.1ms (binding-loop overhead is small). The cost is String canonicalization + clones:

PER EDGE in the full path:
- binding _try_add_edges_from_batch (crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs:2708, 5843): node_key_to_string(u)+node_key_to_string(v) = 2 'str:{len}:{s}' allocs; seen_nodes pair_count clones (verified seen_nodes wasted-clone reduction = within-noise, REJECTED+reverted — not the bottleneck).
- inner extend_keyed_edges_with_attrs_unrecorded (crates/fnx-classes/src/lib.rs:2316): EdgeKey::new (lib.rs:23) does left.to_owned()+right.to_owned() = 2 allocs/edge; self.adjacency.entry(left.clone()).entry(right.clone()) = 2 more clones/edge.
=> ~6-8 String allocs/clones per edge for 6000 edges = ~40-48k allocations. nx stores the int node OBJECTS directly in dict-of-dicts (no canonicalization), so it pays ~0 string work.

ROOT CAUSE: fnx node identity = canonical 'str:{byte_len}:{s}' String key (node_key_to_string). Every structural map (nodes IndexMap<String,_>, adjacency String-keyed, edges EdgeKey{left:String,right:String}) re-stores/re-clones it. This is the foundational vs-nx construction gap (create_empty_copy 2.8x, random_regular P2 br-r37-c1-04z53.75, add_nodes/edges_from 3-6x all bound by it).

DEEP LEVER (alien-graveyard: succinct/interned representation): intern node identities to a u32/u64 index ONCE at insertion (HashMap<canonical_key,u32> side table + Vec<PyObject> display), key adjacency/edges by integer index (EdgeKey becomes (u32,u32), adjacency Vec<Vec<(u32,key)>> or IndexMap<u32,_>). Eliminates ALL per-edge String allocation in the hot path; canonical String computed once per NEW node, not per edge-occurrence. Target 2-3x on bulk construction, broad (touches whole API). RISK: foundational change to fnx-classes Graph representation used by every algorithm + every PyO3 accessor; must preserve canonical-key identity semantics, node/edge iteration order, attr-dict identity. EdgeKeyRef<'a> + indexmap::Equivalent already exist for alloc-free LOOKUP — extend that discipline to the integer-id rewrite. Multi-session effort; gate behind exhaustive golden-sha + isomorphism corpus.
close_reason: Already completed in 1b69096ba: exact-int existing-index edge batch kept; direct loop 0.0056515566s -> 0.0017460271s (3.24x), hyperfine 0.3962154328s -> 0.2996849166s (1.32x), golden payload/file SHA unchanged. Reconciling stale tracker state.

close_reason: THE BEAD SAYS "BOTH DIRECTIONS" AND ONE MEASURE ONLY HAD ONE. local_node_connectivity is checked forward AND reverse; local_edge_connectivity is checked forward only. Edge connectivity is asymmetric on a digraph just as node connectivity is - measured, the sampled pairs differ in that direction on 103 of 150 - so the reverse call is a genuinely distinct value that was never compared with networkx. Now compared, 150/150 agreement verified before writing. THE PREMISE ITSELF NEEDED A GUARD: this whole file rests on directed asymmetry being real. If conn(s,t) always equalled conn(t,s) on the random family, the forward and reverse assertions would be checking one number twice and "both directions" would be decoration. Measured 99 of 150 sampled pairs asymmetric for node connectivity, and added a guard asserting at least 40 stay asymmetric. The pre-existing test_directed_connectivity_is_genuinely_asymmetric covers this with ONE fixed witness (a 3-path); the guard extends the same reasoning to the sweep family. A NON-UNIFORM CONTRACT, the third such split I have found (after br-r37-c1-rjwr4 and br-r37-c1-0ytg7): s == t is NOT handled alike by the two local measures. local_node_connectivity returns 1 - a node is connected to itself - while local_edge_connectivity RAISES NetworkXError. Both match live networkx 3.6.1. Nothing tested either, and the natural assumption is that a matched pair of measures agrees on their degenerate case. MISSING SHAPE: 29 of the 50 draws are not strongly connected, so the global measures are already exercised at 0 - but no draw is built to be DISCONNECTED outright, and that is the cleanest statement of the 0 case; added it for both global measures. title: fix(namespaces): 36 more fnx submodules are replaced wholesale by networkx on the attribute path
description:
Found while closing br-r37-c1-2qsqf on af0496fe5/5f7c4d7fc. Same mechanism, wider blast radius, deliberately NOT fixed in that commit because switching 36 namespaces is a bigger behavioural change than 2qsqf's evidence supports.

MECHANISM: franken_networkx.__getattr__ (python/franken_networkx/__init__.py, the _fnx_submodules set) returns the fnx submodule ONLY for allowlisted names and otherwise falls through to getattr(nx, name). Where networkx has a module of the same name, fnx.<ns> IS networkx's module - so every attribute reached through it is nx's implementation, no matter what the fnx submodule file contains. The fnx submodule is still reachable as 'from franken_networkx.<ns> import X', which is why this hides so well: two spellings of the same import give two different implementations.

MEASUREMENT (fresh interpreter per name, since importing the real submodule for ANY reason binds it onto the parent package and masks the problem): 71 fnx submodule files, 32 resolve to fnx, 39 resolve to networkx. 2qsqf fixed 3 of the 39 (convert, relabel, distance_regular). The remaining 36:

assortativity, asteroidal, boundary, centrality, chains, cluster, communicability_alg, covering, cuts, cycles, d_separation, distance_measures, dominance, dominating, efficiency_measures, exception, graph_hashing, graphical, hierarchy, isolate, link_analysis, link_prediction, lowest_common_ancestors, matching, mis, perfect_graph, polynomials, richclub, similarity, simple_paths, smetric, structuralholes, vitality, voronoi, walks, wiener

WHAT THE FIXER MUST CHECK FIRST, per namespace: does the fnx submodule actually override anything? The 3 fixed in 2qsqf did (convert 7 names, distance_regular 5, relabel 2). A namespace whose fnx file is a pure re-export gains nothing from being allowlisted and should be left alone rather than churned - so this is 36 individual judgements, not one sweep. The audit script pattern is in the 2qsqf comment.

ALREADY GUARDED: tests/python/test_namespace_shadowing_audit.py::test_attribute_path_is_not_networkxs_module covers the 26 namespaces in 2qsqf's scope. Extend its NAMESPACES list as each of these lands - the test is written to take them.

NOTE the test trap that cost two false passes: use a SUBPROCESS with PYTHONPATH pointed at the tree under test. importlib.import_module returns the real submodule (not what fnx.<ns> gives), and a bare subprocess silently probes the INSTALLED package.
close_reason: Fixed in ec202b287: 35 of the 36 remaining submodules are now routed on the attribute path (fnx.<ns> resolves to fnx's module, 32 -> 70 of 71). Triaged individually as the bead required rather than swept — each allowlisted only after confirming its fnx file genuinely overrides a name networkx also exports (1-4 each). 'exception' is deliberately left unrouted because it is a pure re-export, and now carries its own test asserting that reason still holds, so a future override there fails the suite instead of silently re-shadowing. Verified with 12 value-parity checks through the newly-routed paths against live nx 3.6.1 (0 mismatches) and the FULL non-slow suite: 50523 passed, 0 failed. Audit test extended to all 61 routed namespaces; 130 passed.

title: test: closeness/harmonic centrality identities (centrality<->distances)
description: closeness(v)=(n-1)/sum_u d(v,u); harmonic(v)=sum 1/d(v,u); closeness<=1; star-center closeness=1+harmonic=#leaves; K_n closeness=1. Cross-checks closeness_centrality/harmonic_centrality against all_pairs_shortest_path_length. Oracle-free. ~42 cases.
close_reason: The docstring caveat WAS the gap. 'On a connected graph' named the excluded case, and the sweep skipped 10 of its 40 draws as disconnected without testing them at all - disconnectedness is exactly where these two functions stop matching the simple formulas. MUTANT, measured: a closeness_centrality that FORGETS the Wasserman-Faust correction (i.e. returns the wf_improved=False value) is invisible to the pre-existing sweep, which skips all 47 disconnected draws; the new sweep catches it 47/47. wf_improved defaults to True and is a NO-OP on connected graphs, so the parameter had never been exercised by anything in this file. Added, all three verified oracle-free at scale (47/47 each) before being asserted: closeness over the REACHABLE set only, scaled - (R/sum_d)*(R/(n-1)) - and unscaled - R/sum_d; harmonic as the sum of 1/d over reachable nodes, needing no correction since an unreachable node contributes 1/inf = 0; the R==0 isolated-node branch returning 0 from all three (54 isolated nodes occur across the disconnected draws, so the branch is reached, not dead); and the correction never increasing a value. Plus a guard test pinning that wf_improved is the identity exactly when connected AND genuinely differs once the graph splits, so it cannot pass vacuously. SKIP HYGIENE: I first parametrized the disconnected sweep over range(200) and skipped the connected draws, which reported 163 skips and buried the 47 real cases. Replaced with a module-level DISCONNECTED_SEEDS list computed at collection, so the sweep skips NOTHING and the 10 remaining skips are the pre-existing sweep's own. Evidence: file 42 -> 80 passed + 10 skipped; 128 passed + 10 skipped across the centrality family (centrality_metric_invariants, accumulative_centrality_float_tolerance). Crate-scoped, not a workspace run. Test-only, no Rust touched, no CGSE surface.

title: perf: native by-index paired-attr kernel for tensor/strong products (0.49x, set_edge_attributes key-resolution floor)
description:
PROFILE-FIRST FINDING (BlackThrush, 2026-07-16, .so=ecf4897bb). tensor_product / strong_product on edge-attributed simple graphs are 0.49x / 0.45x nx. NOT a floor — the fix is clear:

MEASURED (weighted, G=60n/200e x H=40n/120e, 48000 tensor edges): nx tensor 90ms, fnx tensor 165ms (0.55x). BUT fnx STRUCTURE alone (tensor_product_fast) = 11ms. So the edge-attr DECORATION is 154ms = 93% of fnx's time. That decoration is  — its cost is per-edge TUPLE-NODE KEY RESOLUTION (canonicalize each (g,h) tuple node -> String, O(48000) times). The paired py-dict creation is small; the key resolution is the 154ms.

FIX: native tensor_product_edge_attrs_fast / strong_product_edge_attrs_fast that attach the paired attrs BY INDEX while building the structure — no per-edge tuple-node canonicalization. Model on lexicographic_product_edge_attrs_fast (ecf4897bb) + graph_product_fast's push_tensor. Each tensor edge ((gu,hu),(gv,hv)) inherits _paired_edge_attrs(G[gu][gv], H[hu][hv]) = {key: (g_val, h_val)} — a TUPLE value (non-scalar), so it goes in edge_py_attrs (py mirror) + edges_dirty, NOT the CgseValue store. Expected 0.55x -> ~1.7x.

PARITY CAVEATS (why it needs a focused cycle, not a rush):
1. EDGE ORDER: result edge iteration order = graph_product_fast's push_tensor NODE-MAJOR order (for gu, for hu, for gv in G-nbr(gu), for hv in H-nbr(hu)), NOT the Python _edge_attr_map's G-edge-major order. Must enumerate to match (undirected pushes each edge twice, both orientations, same paired attr; extend_edges + edge_py_attrs canon-dedup).
2. PAIRED-DICT KEY ORDER: _paired_edge_attrs uses {k for k in set(ga)|set(ha)} — Python set-union order, hard to replicate in Rust. GATE: only fire when the union of ALL distinct edge-attr keys across G and H has size <= 1 (e.g. both weighted with just 'weight' — the common case -> paired dict has 1 key, trivial order). Bail otherwise -> current set_edge_attributes path.
3. Gate on pristine mirror (edge_py_attrs empty = store-complete = single-key/scalar sources), simple undirected, matching directedness; multi-key sources eager-mirror -> bail.

strong_product = cartesian (single-source, store-cloneable like lexicographic) UNION tensor (paired). Its kernel does the cartesian-layer via store-clone + the tensor-layer via paired edge_py_attrs. Register near algorithms.rs 26897; wire in tensor_product (23961) / strong_product (24062) like cartesian. Node attrs decorated in Python after.
close_reason: Both tensor (7d2a81584) and strong (cd5671b6e) product edge-attr kernels shipped; single-key undirected product edge-attr family complete. Directed/multi-key remain lower-value follow-ups.

title: perf(structural): weighted shortest-path family pays per-call edge-attr re-sync tax (voronoi_cells weighted 0.27-0.43x)
description: voronoi_cells on a WEIGHTED graph is 0.27-0.43x vs nx (n=250..1000). cProfile: the native multi_source_dijkstra kernel itself (~0.6ms@250) is at-or-faster than nx (0.5ms), but each call pays _fnx_sync_attrs_to_inner (~0.34ms) via _graph_has_nonunit_weight. That sync rebuilds ALL edge AttrMaps from edge_py_attrs every call because edges_dirty is set pessimistically on any edge-dict hand-out and is NEVER cleared (a held G[u][v] ref can be mutated invisibly). Tried edge_only sync (skip ungated node-attr rebuild): correct + byte-identical (golden 53cfd541...) but only 1.0-1.09x even with heavy node attrs — node rebuild is not the bottleneck; the EDGE rebuild is. Same dual-storage substrate floor as br-r37-c1-wsy5c. Real lever needs either (a) a dijkstra kernel that reads edge_py_attrs weights directly (no inner AttrMap sync), or (b) safe edges_dirty clearing after sync with re-set on dict mutation. Both Rust-coupled. Affects entire dijkstra/bellman-ford/floyd/voronoi family.
notes: PARTIAL FIX shipped (commit, ~1.4x): removed the redundant double-sync — voronoi_cells/multi_source_dijkstra_path/single_source_bellman_ford/all_pairs_bellman_ford gated on _graph_has_nonunit_weight (full O(E+N) sync side-effect) AND then called a self-syncing binding = 2 full syncs. Added _binding_self_syncs_gate (no-op, no sync) at those 7 sites. voronoi 0.43x->0.63x, msd_path->0.60x, apbf now 1.7-1.8x faster than nx. cut_size/normalized_cut_size KEEP the sync (their _raw_cut_size kernel does NOT self-sync — removing it returns unweighted count for custom weight names). RESIDUAL (still 0.6x voronoi/msd): the remaining single binding-level sync rebuilds ALL edge AttrMaps (py_dict_to_attr_map over every key) when dijkstra only needs the 'weight' scalar. Deep lever = native kernel variant taking weights as a Vec<f64> built by a fast edge_py_attrs scan reading only 'weight' (like check_dijkstra_edge_weights_fast), never rebuilding inner AttrMaps — keeps inner's completeness invariant. Requires new Rust kernel signatures + rebuild.

comments.text:
FIXED in 816ddb575, but the bead's PREMISE was inverted — recorded so it is not re-derived.

The bead asks fnx to 'handle MultiDiGraph keyed flow dictionaries'. fnx ALREADY handled them; upstream nx is the one that cannot (nx computes sum(flowDict[u][v] * d.get(weight,0) for u,v,d in G.edges(data=True)), so a keyed inner dict raises TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'dict' and 'int'). Executed probe, live networkx 3.6.1:

  MultiDiGraph [(0,1,w=3)], flowDict {0:{1:{0:2}}}   nx=TypeError   fnx=6

What WAS broken, verified on the pre-fix tree:

  MultiDiGraph [(0,1,w=3),(0,1,w=5)], flowDict {0:{1:2}}   nx=16   fnx=0   <- SILENT WRONG VALUE
  DiGraph [(0,1,w=3)], flowDict {}                         nx=KeyError(0)  fnx=0

fnx walked flowDict instead of the graph's edges, so get_edge_data(u,v) returned a {key: attrs} mapping on a multigraph, .get('weight',0) found nothing, and parallel edges contributed ZERO. A partial flow dict was likewise accepted and under-counted instead of raising.

Now iterates G.edges(data=True) (and edges(keys=True, data=True) for multigraphs), matching nx on both. The keyed extension is KEPT — test_multidigraph_min_cost_flow_cost_family_matches_networkx deliberately locks it and fnx's own network_simplex emits that shape — but it now scores each parallel edge against ITS OWN key: {0:{1:{0:2,1:4}}} gives 2*3+4*5=26 instead of collapsing.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: removing the keyed extension to match nx's TypeError. That is a compatibility-doctrine decision that would delete a peer's locking test, so it needs the joint decision protocol, not a drive-by. Filed as the open question here.

Two new tests lock both fixed behaviours plus the extension's per-key scoring. 372 flow-family tests pass; full suite 50163 passed / 1077 skipped with only the pre-existing br-r37-c1-vcz0r failures. ubs on the test file: 0 critical, 0 warnings.

comments.text:
SATISFIED AT 191 CASES, BUT NAME-ONLY EXCEPTION COMPARISON AND UNDIRECTED-ONLY COVERAGE — BOTH
CLOSED (CopperCliff, 2026-08-08).

tests/python/test_exception_contract_parity.py already existed and matched this bead: every named
missing-node function (shortest_path / dijkstra_path / bfs_tree / dfs_tree / ego_graph / eccentricity
/ clustering / has_path / single_source_dijkstra_path_length / dijkstra_predecessor_and_distance) and
every named structural-precondition function (topological_sort / dag_longest_path / eulerian_circuit
/ find_cycle / diameter / center / is_arborescence / immediate_dominators, plus
average_shortest_path_length), at 11 + 9x20 = 191 cases — exactly the figure this bead specifies. I
checked before writing anything.

GAP 1 — THE COMPARISON WAS BY NAME. The `_outcome` helper returns `type(exc).__name__`, so the whole
module asserted only that fnx raises something CALLED NetworkXNoPath. The contract that matters to a
drop-in is that `except nx.NetworkXNoPath:` in user code CATCHES what fnx raises. A separate class
with the same name satisfies every assertion in the file and breaks every caller — which is precisely
the divergence class this bead cites (xn2ho).

  MEASURED FIRST: fnx re-exports networkx's own classes today. For all ten of NetworkXError,
  NetworkXNoPath, NodeNotFound, NetworkXUnfeasible, NetworkXNotImplemented,
  NetworkXPointlessConcept, HasACycle, AmbiguousSolution, ExceededMaxIterations and
  PowerIterationFailedConvergence, `fnx.X is nx.X` holds and `except nx.X` catches a raised `fnx.X`.
  So there is no bug — but nothing PINNED it, and the name comparison would have kept passing if
  that ever changed.
  ADDED: test_exception_classes_are_the_networkx_classes asserts identity AND catchability for all
  ten.

GAP 2 — THE MISSING-NODE SWEEP RAN ON AN UNDIRECTED GRAPH ONLY. The directed and multigraph classes
reach different code for the same arguments, so a contract divergence in one of them was invisible.
Verified equal on DiGraph, MultiGraph and MultiDiGraph BEFORE asserting it (0 divergences across all
11 cases on each), then parametrised the sweep over all four classes.

MUTATION-CHECKED, because a lock that cannot fail is worse than the weak one it replaced: a
same-named `class NetworkXNoPath(Exception)` PASSES the old name comparison, FAILS the new identity
assertion, and is NOT caught by `except nx.NetworkXNoPath`. The new assertion catches exactly the
user-visible break the name check misses.

Cases 191 -> 234. File: 234 passed. Full Python suite: 50778 passed, 1081 skipped, 0 FAILED.

comments.text:
SATISFIED AT 90 CASES — BUT THE MATRIX CODECS WERE CHECKED BY EDGE COUNT ALONE (CopperCliff,
2026-08-08).

tests/python/test_conversion_roundtrip_identity.py already existed and matched this bead:
dict_of_dicts (with weights), dict_of_lists, numpy, scipy sparse, pandas edgelist (with weights),
plus dense/sparse parity vs nx, at 3 x 30 = 90 cases — exactly the figure specified. I checked before
writing.

GAP 1 — THE WEAKEST POSSIBLE CODEC ASSERTION. Both matrix round-trips asserted only

    assert fnx.from_numpy_array(A).number_of_edges() == g.number_of_edges()

A codec that decoded to a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT graph of the same size passes that, on a bead whose
stated premise is "oracle-free codec correctness". The matrices themselves were compared to nx, but
the DECODED GRAPH was only counted.

GAP 2 — ORDER AND CROSS-LIBRARY COMPARISON. `_edges` sorts sorted pairs and the dict test compares
`sorted(...nodes())`, so node and edge ORDER were unchecked on every round-trip; and the pandas arm
never compared the DataFrame or the decoded graph against networkx at all — only against the source.

    matches networkx's own round-trip in node and edge ORDER;

    graphs match in node and edge order.

ONE BEHAVIOUR WORTH NAMING rather than "fixing": the pandas round-trip legitimately DROPS isolated
nodes — an edgelist cannot carry them — so on 6 of these 30 seeds the decoded graph has fewer nodes
than the source. My first probe compared the round-trip to the SOURCE and flagged 29/30 "node order"
divergences because of it; that was my error, not a defect. networkx does exactly the same, which is
why the new assertion compares fnx-vs-nx rather than round-trip-vs-source, and the docstring records
the drop and its seed count so the next reader does not repeat my misreading.

title: perf(batch): add_edges_from has a 6.84x cliff at chunk size 8 — k=7 is 2128 ns/edge, k=8 is 14631, dual A/A nulls 0.9921x/0.9970x
description:
Found by OliveDesert 2026-08-08 while profiling br-r37-c1-jc9e4. This is a user-visible performance cliff, not a micro-regression, and it was not what I was looking for.

REPRODUCTION. 2000 nodes / 8000 edges, str keys, fresh Graph per build, chunked as `for i in range(0, M, k): g.add_edges_from(pairs[i:i+k])`. Edge order asserted identical to the whole-batch build at EVERY k, so this is purely timing. Quiet host, one-minute load 4.04, ELF 675707aceef90feadcfb8c17d73046ad68f76f035395bd3ec884792a717cc403. Script: scratchpad/k8_probe.py (session-scoped, copy it).

  k=1     3646.5 ns/edge
  k=2     2408.5
  k=3     2048.8
  k=4     1870.7
  k=5     1785.6
  k=6     1707.6
  k=7     1679.5     <-- smooth amortization up to here
  k=8    15156.3     <-- 9.0x CLIFF
  k=9    13469.9
  k=10   12147.5
  k=12   10175.1
  k=16    7686.1
  k=24    5339.5
  k=32    4144.3
  k=64    2362.9
  k=8000   352.7     <-- large batches are excellent, 1.86x faster than nx's own add_edges_from

A batch of 8 is NINE TIMES worse per edge than a batch of 7, and does not get back to the k=7 figure until roughly k>=128.

NOT NOISE. Reproduced three times in separate invocations at one-minute loads of 13.3, 4.0 and 4.0, giving 15491, 15650 and 15156 ns/edge. The k=1..7 region is smooth and monotone in the same runs, so the discontinuity is in the code, not the host.

WHY IT MATTERS. Chunked add_edges_from is a normal way to write graph-building code — streaming edges, batching by page, accumulating a small buffer — and the sizes people naturally choose (8, 10, 16, 32, 100) all land in the bad region. At k=8 a single call costs about 121 microseconds on a graph holding ~4000 edges, which has the shape of an O(existing edges) pass per call rather than a constant per-call overhead. Confirm that shape by re-running the sweep at two graph sizes: if the k=8 figure scales with the number of edges ALREADY in the graph, it is a per-call whole-graph pass and that is the bug.

WHAT I DID NOT FIND. I did not locate the threshold in source. A grep for the obvious size guards (len() < 8, <= 7, SMALL_BATCH) in crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs and for a size test in _add_edges_from_materialized found nothing, so the 8 may be indirect — a SmallVec inline capacity, a hashmap/vec growth boundary, or a heuristic that switches collection strategy. Start by finding which path a 7-edge batch takes that an 8-edge batch does not.

PARITY BAR: edge and node insertion order must stay byte-identical at every chunk size (already asserted in the probe and currently correct), along with duplicate-pair merge semantics and partial-failure state.

DECIDE on the balanced-square substrate with a fresh graph per timed unit and both A/A nulls recorded.

SHIPPED AND FIXED. The acceptance test written onto this bead — the N=8000 figure must stop tracking N — passes: x19.30 becomes x1.10.

MECHANISM: collect_plain_edge_batch (lib.rs:2655) built a HashMap<String,usize> from EVERY existing node name, cloning each String, on every call — O(N) allocations and hashes to insert as few as 8 edges. That is the cliff at PLAIN_EDGE_BATCH_MIN=8: below 8 the batch is skipped, at 8 it engages and pays a whole-graph map. Replaced with the graph's own O(1) get_node_index plus a batch-local map of only the nodes this batch introduces (bounded by 2x batch length); a node created by the batch takes node_count() + position among new nodes, because the commit inserts new_nodes in first-appearance order. Collect performs no mutation so an index read during it stays valid.

  after    502.6   497.1   546.4    546.6    555.1  ns/edge   -> x1.10

THE HYPOTHESIS THAT FIT AND FAILED: that collector opened by cloning every existing node key into a HashSet<String> — O(N) String allocations per call regardless of batch size. On 2000 nodes that predicts ~100 us/call against a measured ~117 us, and the k>=8 tail is a clean 1/k curve, exactly the shape of a fixed per-call cost amortized over k.

I replaced it with an O(1) self.inner.has_node lookup per endpoint plus a local set of only the nodes the batch introduces, preserving the pre-insert node_bumps sampling and the self-loop case. check/clippy/fmt clean, rebuilt to ELF 62f685a3. NOTHING MOVED:

REACHABILITY TRAP I HIT INSIDE THIS ATTEMPT — read before editing lib.rs. My first edit went to _try_add_edges_from_batch at lib.rs:7132, which is in impl PyMultiGraph (declared :6137), NOT impl PyGraph (declared :11851). SHAPE PINNED (OliveDesert, 2026-08-08): the per-call cost is O(NODES) and FLAT IN EDGES. This is the probe the previous comment prescribed; it is done, do not re-run it.

METHOD: pre-build a graph of (N nodes, E edges), then time 100 successive 8-edge add_edges_from calls on it (800 edges added, small against E, so size is effectively fixed during the sample). Load 4.25, ELF 675707ac. Script: scratchpad/k8_scaling.py.

A) vary NODES, edges fixed 8000:
   N=500    3889.6 ns/edge   x1.00
   N=1000   7442.0           x1.91
   N=2000  15208.3           x3.91
   N=4000  33816.6           x8.69
   N=8000  75088.1           x19.30

B) vary EDGES, nodes fixed 2000:
   E=1000  14900.6 ns/edge   x1.00
   E=2000  15065.1           x1.01
   E=4000  15694.8           x1.05
   E=8000  15520.9           x1.04
   E=16000 15502.3           x1.04

16x more nodes costs 19.30x; 16x more edges costs 1.04x. It is a whole-node-set pass per call, slightly superlinear the way an allocating hash build is.

AND IT IS NOT THE COLLECTOR. seen_nodes at try_add_plain_edge_batch (lib.rs:3373) is already refuted (replaced with an O(1) per-endpoint lookup, rebuilt, moved nothing). Scanning the entire collector body lib.rs:3307-3520 for node-set-wide operations finds nodes_ordered() exactly ONCE, at :3375, which is that same refuted clone. So the surviving O(N) pass is DOWNSTREAM of the collect: the commit step, the caller PyGraph::_try_add_edges_from_batch (:12578), or a mirror/cache rebuild that runs once per successful batch.

This also explains why it is a cliff and not a curve: below PLAIN_EDGE_BATCH_MIN=8 the batch never engages so no whole-node-set pass is paid; at 8 it engages and pays one per call; the 1/k tail above 8 is that fixed O(N) cost amortized over the batch.

ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR ANY FIX: the N=8000 figure in sweep A must stop tracking N. Improving the k=8 number alone is NOT sufficient — amortization changes could do that without removing the pass. Confirm the enclosing impl before editing lib.rs; names repeat across per-class impls and an unreached edit reads exactly like a refuted hypothesis.

title: resistance_distance uses wrong weight when weight=None
description:
When `weight=None` is passed to `fnx.resistance_distance`, the implementation uses `weight or "weight"` which evaluates to `"weight"`, causing it to use edge weights when None was intended.

**Test case:**
```python
G = fnx.karate_club_graph()  # has weight=4 on edges
fnx.resistance_distance(G, 0, 1, weight=None)  # Returns 0.0635
nx.resistance_distance(G, 0, 1, weight=None)   # Returns 0.1931
```

**Root cause:** Line 23840:
`L = laplacian_matrix(G, nodelist=nodelist, weight=weight or "weight")`

The `weight or "weight"` expression evaluates to "weight" when weight=None, but should be None.

**Fix:** Change to pass `weight` directly instead of `weight or "weight"`.

close_reason: THE BEAD NAMES REALIZABILITY AND ONLY ONE DIRECTION OF IT WAS TESTED. The file checks that a real graph degree sequence is graphical - which is true by construction and cannot fail. The converse, that a sequence CALLED graphical can actually be realized by some simple graph, is what makes the predicate mean anything, and nothing in the file ever constructed a graph. havel_hakimi_graph now builds each graphical sequence and the result must (a) reproduce the sequence exactly, (b) be SIMPLE - no self-loops, no parallel edges, since graphicality is a statement about simple graphs and a multigraph realization would be a different and much weaker claim - and (c) match what networkx realizes. title: test: coloring + approximation validity invariants + parity
description: greedy_color 7 deterministic strategies (parity + proper-coloring validity: no monochromatic edge) + approximation min_weighted_vertex_cover/maximum_independent_set/min_weighted_dominating_set validity invariants (cover touches all edges, IS has no edge, DS dominates all nodes). 180 cases.
close_reason: A REAL BUG FELL OUT, filed as br-r37-c1-bdswh (P1). THE TEST GAP: maximum_independent_set is validated ONLY by the absence of an internal edge, and the EMPTY SET satisfies that - a function returning nothing passed the file. It must now be non-empty, which is always achievable since any single node is an independent set. None of the three approximation outputs was required to consist of the graph OWN nodes either; all three now are. Added the cover/independent-set duality (the complement of a vertex cover is an independent set by definition), which ties the cover to the same property the independent set is judged by without using either function as the other oracle. THE BUG: min_weighted_vertex_cover IGNORES weight= entirely. Measured, not inferred - its weighted result equals its UNWEIGHTED result on 30/30 random draws, and on a 4-node witness with weights {0:1, 1:100, 2:1, 3:100} it returns a cover of total weight 102 where brute force gives an optimum of 2. This is a 2-approximation, so the guarantee is weight <= 4; 102 exceeds it by 25x, which makes it the wrong objective rather than an approximation-choice difference. I isolated the fault before filing: the Python shim at __init__.py:19540 correctly forwards weight to the native kernel AND correctly delegates DIRECTED graphs to networkx - and on the same witness the directed/delegated path returns {0,2} matching nx while the undirected/native path returns {0,1,2}. So the shim and plumbing are fine and the native kernel drops the weight. The shim br-vcnative comment claiming the kernel "replicates nx exactly (incl. weight=None => unit weights)" is half true and should be corrected with the fix. Why nothing caught it: no test in the suite passes weight= to this function, and the validity assertion here is satisfied by ANY valid cover regardless of weight. A TEST OF MINE I DELETED BEFORE COMMITTING, because it was exactly the defect I keep finding in others: I wrote a maximality check that skipped when an addable node existed and then asserted no addable node existed - tautological, passing either way. Worse, the property is not one this approximation guarantees (maximal on 34 of 40 draws), so no version of that assertion was honest. I removed it rather than ship a test that reads as coverage and proves nothing. Evidence: file 180 -> 260 passed, no skips; 786 passed across the coloring/approximation family (approximation_guarantee_invariants, coloring_chromatic_bounds, approximation). Crate-scoped and inline with a timeout cap; no background jobs left running. Committed 4ed661ec3, pushed to main then master separately after a fast-forward check. title: fix(test_coverage_gaps): generated coverage matrix subprocess cannot import networkx
description:
PRE-EXISTING environment defect, unrelated to any code change.

  pytest tests/python/test_coverage_gaps.py::test_generated_coverage_matrix_document_is_current
  RuntimeError: NetworkX FeatureUniverse extraction failed: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'networkx'
  scripts/generate_coverage_matrix.py:408

The parent pytest process imports networkx 3.6.1 fine; the subprocess that generate_coverage_matrix.py spawns to extract the NetworkX FeatureUniverse does not inherit an interpreter/env that can see it. So the test fails for every agent on every run and is currently a permanent red in the suite, which masks real regressions in the same file.

Fix the spawn to use sys.executable with the parent's sys.path (or PYTHONPATH), not a bare 'python'. RETRY PREDICATE: the test passes from a clean checkout with no environment tweaks, and a deliberately stale generated document still makes it FAIL (so it keeps its freshness-locking power).

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: FIXED in 0cf500b07, landed under br-r37-c1-9hnq3 (same defect, filed twice). Closing as a duplicate with the evidence rather than re-fixing.

THE BEAD'S OWN NAMED TEST:
  pytest tests/python/test_coverage_gaps.py::test_generated_coverage_matrix_document_is_current
  -> 1 passed in 1.70s
Whole file: 135 passed, 1 skipped (was 7 failed, 128 passed).

ROOT CAUSE, slightly different from this bead's guess: the spawn ALREADY used sys.executable. The
problem was the -I flag. Isolated mode is deliberate - it is what stops FrankenNetworkX from patching
the very surface the extractor measures - but -I also ignores PYTHONPATH *and* drops the USER
site-packages, which is where networkx is installed. So 'use the parent's sys.path/PYTHONPATH' as
suggested here would NOT have worked on its own, and dropping -I would have defeated the isolation.
The fix passes the pinned networkx tree's directory to the child as argv[1] and the child prepends
just that one entry - isolation preserved everywhere else, and the in-test pinned sha256/version/
module counts mean a contaminated tree fails loudly instead of passing quietly.

RETRY PREDICATE ('passes from a clean checkout with no environment tweaks'): satisfied - no env vars,
no PYTHONPATH, plain 'python3 -m pytest' from the repo root.

Worth knowing: this red test was masking real drift in the same file, exactly as the bead warned.
Once it went green it exposed 4 present->partial coverage regressions (k_core family) alongside 2
unreflected improvements, which netted to zero and kept the totals assertion green. Both handled in
the same commit; details on br-r37-c1-9hnq3.
