title: [bug] DiGraph/MultiDiGraph subgraph().in_degree()/out_degree() silently return EMPTY ({} / 0)
description: SEVERE silent-wrong-result bug. On a directed subgraph view, in_degree()/out_degree() return {} (empty), and single-node in_degree(node) returns 0. Repro: E=[(0,1),(1,2),(2,0),(3,1),(0,3)]; gf=fnx.DiGraph(E); sub=[0,1,2,3]; gf.subgraph(sub).in_degree() -> {} but nx -> {0:1,1:2,2:1,3:1}; gf.subgraph(sub).in_degree(1) -> 0 but nx -> 2. Same on MultiDiGraph. The TOTAL degree() IS correct (matches nx) — only in_degree/out_degree broken. CAUSE: _FilteredGraphView (synthetic DiGraph subclass) does NOT override in_degree/out_degree, so they fall through to the DiGraph native descriptor (_digraph_in_degree/_digraph_out_degree at __init__.py:5328/5337) which computes over the view's EMPTY Rust base (filtered views use super().__new__ empty base per br-r37-c1-pgfd2). FIX: _FilteredGraphView must expose filtered in_degree/out_degree views (mirror how its degree/_WeightAwareDegreeView path filters), matching nx InDegreeView/OutDegreeView contract: iterate (node,deg) over filtered nodes + single-node lookup + nbunch + weight, honoring node/edge visibility. Pre-existing (confirmed on HEAD). NOTE: filtered neighbor rows already have fast native accessors post-subadjrow (use G[node] succ / _native_predecessor_row pred to avoid the O(N+E) .succ[node]/.pred[node] re-materialization).

The public wrapper at __init__.py:transitivity has its own directed-aware triangle-iter path; end users are unaffected. The audit's 'error-divergence' classification was misclassifying this as a bug — refined the classifier in scripts/raw_vs_public_audit.py to distinguish raw_looser_than_public (real bugs) from raw_stricter_than_public (intentional defensive guards). title: perf(lookup): extend the borrowed canonical key to has_edge and get_edge_data — measured headroom on a named loss
description:
Direct product of br-r37-c1-oe93x's six-arm measurement (ledger entry 2026-08-06, commit ba3a7f493).

THE OPPORTUNITY IS MEASURED, not inferred. The borrowed-canonical lever is worth 8-19% build-over-build where it IS applied:
    G.has_node(present)  0.4612x -> 0.5199x  (1.127x)
    G.has_node(missing)  0.5578x -> 0.6417x  (1.150x)
    n in G (present)     0.7312x -> 0.7903x  (1.081x)
    n in G (missing)     0.8093x -> 0.9651x  (1.192x)
all CI pairs disjoint, paired in-window against live nx 3.6.1.

IT IS NOT APPLIED ON THE EDGE PATHS, despite an oe93x status comment claiming it was extended to Graph::has_edge / DiGraph::has_edge. Counting canonicalizer calls in crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs:
    Graph::has_edge   (9042)   node_key_to_string x2   with_node_key_str x0
    has_edge          (13025)  node_key_to_string x3   with_node_key_str x2
    get_edge_data     (6495)   node_key_to_string x2   with_node_key_str x0
    get_edge_data     (14646)  node_key_to_string x4   with_node_key_str x0
So the string-key path still allocates an owned canonical String per lookup - the exact cost the membership lever removed.

CURRENT INCUMBENT LOSSES on those surfaces (admitted, decidable, 21 rounds, dual A/A nulls):
    Graph.has_edge 0.4358x, DiGraph.has_edge 0.4429x, MultiGraph.has_edge 0.5302x, MultiDiGraph.has_edge 0.4649x
    Graph.get_edge_data 0.3352x, DiGraph 0.3507x, MultiGraph 0.2409x, MultiDiGraph 0.2339x

EXPECTED EFFECT, stated in advance so it can be falsified: if the mechanism transfers, has_edge should move ~1.08-1.15x build-over-build like the membership rows did. It will NOT turn these into wins - has_edge would land around 0.47-0.50x, still an incumbent loss. Do not report it as a campaign output; the ledger gate correctly rejects that framing (it rejected mine).

THE TRAP oe93x already documented and this must not repeat: with_node_key_str builds the canonical form in a stack buffer and looks up by &str. A borrowed-key Equivalent<String> impl is the tempting alternative and is WRONG - the map is hashed with FxHasher and str hashing feeds the whole byte slice in one Hasher::write plus a 0xff terminator, so hashing the canonical form in pieces does not reproduce the hash and the lookup silently MISSES. The stack buffer hashes the identical single slice.

TESTS THE FIX MUST CARRY (same shape oe93x required): a key longer than the stack buffer; keys at exactly buffer-1/buffer/buffer+1 bytes; non-ASCII multi-byte keys where byte length differs from char count (the 'str:{len}:' prefix uses s.len() in BYTES); and a mixed str/int/float/bool/None round trip vs nx.

MEASUREMENT NOTE: build the AFTER ELF from 98066b4b1 plus ONLY this change if you want the delta attributable. The oe93x AFTER arm was HEAD and therefore conflated - which is why MultiDiGraph.has_edge's 0.924x in that entry could not be pinned on anything.
close_reason: RESOLVED by a same-invocation self-time A/B (commit 95d01f148), not by another perf_harness pair. 5/5 runs admitted under an admission rule fixed in writing beforehand (A/A null within [0.99,1.01]); 4/5 resolved, all four the same direction. Median effect 1.0520x, 5.2 ns saved per two-endpoint lookup, 3.05% of the Rust-side get_edge_data (~1.9% of the Python-visible call). KEPT as SELF-SPEEDUP, campaign_output=false; the bead's written 8-19% prediction stays FALSIFIED and get_edge_data remains a 0.23-0.36x incumbent LOSS. The revert is cancelled because the direction is now measured, which is the condition the reopen set. The queued 25-attempt perf_harness requeue was stopped at attempt 10: that design divides one run's ratio by another's, and with nx drifting 0.0-3.9% against a 0.7-3.5% effect it could never have resolved this. Ledger entry in the same commit.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: CORRECTING THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE before anyone implements against it. I filed it; half of it is wrong.

I counted canonicalizer calls per FUNCTION BODY and inferred the measured path from that. That was
the mistake - the bodies have fast paths ahead of the canonical fallback, and the benchmark shape
never reaches the calls I counted.

has_edge - THE LEVER DOES NOT APPLY, and this is why the row did not move.
PyGraph::has_edge already carries a keyless exact-string fast path (br-r37-c1-paof2, lib.rs ~9075):

    if key.is_none() && u.is_exact_instance_of::<PyString>() && v.is_exact_instance_of::<PyString>()
        -> cached_exact_string_node_index for each endpoint, then has_edge_by_indices

perf_harness's edge-primitives suite probes exactly that shape - probes = [(str(i), str(i+1)) for i
in range(512)], called as gfx.has_edge(u, v) with no key - so the measured path resolves through an
INTERNED INDEX CACHE and never allocates a canonical String at all. The two node_key_to_string calls
I cited are the fallback for keyed / non-exact-string shapes, which the benchmark does not exercise.
There is already something strictly better than the borrowed key on that path. Applying the lever
there would move nothing, which is precisely what the oe93x measurement showed.

get_edge_data - THE LEVER DOES APPLY. PyMultiGraph::get_edge_data (lib.rs 6495) has NO fast path: it
calls node_key_to_string on u and on v unconditionally, on every call, before doing anything else.
Same for the 14646 body. So the 0.2339x-0.3507x get_edge_data rows ARE paying two owned String
allocations per lookup, and the headroom claim stands for those four rows only.

REVISED SCOPE: this bead is get_edge_data only. Expected effect, stated in advance so it can be
falsified: if the mechanism transfers as it did for has_node (1.08-1.19x build-over-build),
get_edge_data should move similarly and land around 0.25-0.39x - still a decisive incumbent LOSS,
still not a campaign output.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE for whoever takes it: get_edge_data is &mut self and uses u_c/v_c many times
across the body (ensure_edge_py_attrs, edge_keys, py_edge_key), so the nested-closure form used at
lib.rs 13055 does not fit. Use stack buffers whose lifetime spans the body:
    let mut ubuf = [0u8; CANONICAL_KEY_STACK_BUF];
    let u_owned;                        // fallback storage, assigned once
    let u_c: &str = ...write_canonical_str_key(&mut ubuf, s)... else { u_owned = node_key_to_string(py,u)?; &u_owned };
The Equivalent<String> hashing trap recorded in the bead description still applies and is the reason
the stack buffer is the approach.

WORTH CHECKING FIRST, and possibly more valuable than this bead: whether get_edge_data should get
the same paof2 interned-index fast path has_edge already has, rather than the borrowed key. That is
what actually made has_edge's measured path allocation-free.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: MEASURED. Both arms admitted; the prediction this bead made in writing is FALSIFIED. Ledger entry df43527de.

    row                          BEFORE    AFTER    ratio   delta vs A/A noise
    Graph.get_edge_data          0.3355x   0.3466x  1.033x  ~4x half-width  (real)
    DiGraph.get_edge_data        0.3483x   0.3583x  1.029x  ~5x             (real)
    MultiGraph.get_edge_data     0.2443x   0.2459x  1.006x  CIs OVERLAP     (not resolvable)
    MultiDiGraph.get_edge_data   0.2363x   0.2342x  0.991x  ~1x             (not resolvable)

THE PREDICTION, quoted from this bead before any code was written: 'if the mechanism transfers as it
did for has_node (1.08-1.19x build-over-build), get_edge_data should move similarly'. Measured ~1.03x
on the simple classes and nothing resolvable on the multigraph ones - about a THIRD of predicted.
Recorded as falsified rather than reframed as a success.

HYPOTHESIS for the gap, offered as a hypothesis and not a finding: has_node is almost nothing BUT the
canonicalisation, so removing the allocation removes most of the call; get_edge_data also resolves
the edge, calls ensure_edge_py_attrs, marks the store dirty and materialises a Python dict, so the
same saved allocation is a far smaller share of the work. If that holds, this lever's value scales
inversely with how much the surrounding call does - worth testing before applying it elsewhere on the
assumption that it will transfer.

THE MultiDiGraph ROW IS NOT A REGRESSION CLAIM. Its point estimate is below 1.0 with disjoint CIs,
which looks like one, but the between-arm delta is 0.0021 against an A/A null half-width of 0.0019 -
about one noise unit. Not claimed in either direction. Same for MultiGraph, whose CIs overlap.

QUALITY OF THE ARMS: unlike the oe93x AFTER arm (HEAD, conflated across everything since 98066b4b1),
this is a clean single-commit delta - BEFORE a9b194d1 is the previous HEAD ELF, AFTER 145297b5 is
that plus ONLY this lever, both against the same HEAD python tree. So the ~3% is attributable.

KEPT, with the reason stated: decidable +3% on the two most-used classes, no demonstrated regression,
and the code carries boundary tests. It does NOT move get_edge_data out of a 0.23-0.36x incumbent
loss and must not be cited as doing so - classified SELF-SPEEDUP, campaign_output=false.

ATTRIBUTION DEFECT I introduced and am naming rather than hiding: the lever's code landed inside
commit 218e7f9c1, whose subject reads 'style(fnx-python): format the vz4v9 hunks; record the
piped-exit-status audit'. That is a functional Rust change under a formatting subject. History is
pushed and shared, so it is recorded in the ledger instead of rewritten.

comments.author: ProudBasin
comments.text:
ProudBasin: REOPENED, and the revert is ON HOLD. My previous close said 'kept for the decidable +3%'; that +3% is retracted (ledger 112d15cba) because it was nx-arm drift, not an fnx speedup. My next instinct was to revert the lever on that basis — which would have been the SAME inference error mirrored: a contaminated measurement establishes absence of effect no more than presence.

CORRECT SEQUENCING, now in progress:
  1. ONE admitted re-measure under the across-run rule, alternating the arms
     (before, after, before, after) so consecutive pairs sit as close in time as
     the gate allows, and collecting TWO pairs so the nx arm's run-to-run
     movement is estimated FROM THE DATA rather than assumed. Queued, 25 attempts
     per arm.
  2. If it admits: decide on the fnx arm's own movement, with the observed nx
     drift as the error floor.
  3. If it does NOT admit within those attempts: revert, and record explicitly
     that the revert is for WANT OF AN ADMISSIBLE MEASUREMENT, not for a measured
     null. Those are different claims and the bead must not conflate them.

STATE OF THE EVIDENCE, so nobody reads the earlier close as standing:
  - The published 1.033x / 1.029x / 1.006x / 0.991x ratios are NOT retracted as
    measurements — they are what the harness recorded. What is retracted is the
    INFERENCE that they show the lever working.
  - fnx's own arm across those runs: Graph +0.7% slower, DiGraph -1.5%,
    MultiGraph -0.7%, MultiDiGraph +2.8% slower. nx drift over the same pair:
    +3.9%, +1.3%, -0.0%, +2.0%.
  - So the effect being claimed (~3%) is smaller than the yardstick's movement
    (up to 3.9%). NO-VERDICT in both directions.

The across-run rule is now in the ledger HEADER (not just this entry) so every
future before/after row inherits it: per-run CIs describe within-run noise and
say nothing about across-run reproducibility.

comments.author: SnowyValley
comments.text:
SnowyValley: RESOLVED — and NOT by the queued perf_harness re-measure, which I stopped at attempt 10/25 because that design cannot answer this question.

WHY THE REQUEUE WAS THE WRONG PLAN (it was my own previous plan, and I am correcting it). perf_harness compares two builds by dividing one invocation's nx/fnx ratio by another's. Under the across-run rule that is a NO-VERDICT whenever the nx yardstick moves more than the effect. nx moved 0.0-3.9% between the arms; the effect measures at 0.7-3.5% of the call. The effect is INSIDE the drift band, so no number of admitted attempts could ever have resolved it. The host also never quiesced (load 22-62 across 10 attempts). Stopping it freed the one-harness-at-a-time slot for work that can use it.

THE INSTRUMENT THAT ANSWERS: borrowed_canonical_key_self_time_ab, a same-invocation interleaved order-balanced self-time A/B in crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs. One process, so there is no across-run axis and no yardstick to drift. Self-time only; it cannot and does not produce a vs-nx number.

Its A/A null caught two defects in my own design before any result was believed. Fixed arm order gave null 0.8885x — two byte-identical closures differing 12% by POSITION, while the "effect" it reported was 0.8849x, indistinguishable from it. ABBA placement improved the null to 0.9379x but a convex per-slot entry cost survived. Fixed by sweeping the probe set 100x inside each timed slot. Without the null in the design, version 1 would have reported a 12% REGRESSION that does not exist.

ADMISSION RULE, fixed in writing before the repeats were started: admitted iff the A/A null is within [0.99,1.01]; an admitted run resolves iff |effect-1| >= 2*|null-1|.

  run  null      effect    saving  share  long-key  verdict
   4   1.0092x   1.0108x   1.4ns   0.68%  0.9424x   admitted, NO-VERDICT
   5   0.9938x   1.0603x   6.0ns   3.52%  0.9635x   RESOLVED
   6   0.9944x   1.0520x   5.2ns   3.05%  1.0255x   RESOLVED
   7   0.9936x   1.0332x   3.3ns   1.96%  1.0051x   RESOLVED
   8   0.9939x   1.0591x   6.0ns   3.44%  1.0096x   RESOLVED

5/5 admitted, 4/5 resolved, all four in the same direction. Median 1.0520x, 5.2 ns saved per two-endpoint lookup, 3.05% of the Rust-side get_edge_data. Run 4 is the only run that did not resolve and is also the only one whose spread was +/-13% rather than +/-1%. Run 3 is excluded by an amendment written before the repeats produced output (it predates a change inside canonical_node_key_in, and pooling builds is the conflation this instrument exists to avoid).

THE SHARE IS QUOTED IN OUR FAVOUR: the denominator is the Rust-side call (170-207 ns). The Python-visible call is ~277 ns because it also pays interpreter method dispatch, so the share of what a user actually calls is ~1.9% at the median, not 3.05%.

VERDICT: KEPT, SELF-SPEEDUP, campaign_output=false. The bead's written prediction of 8-19% stays FALSIFIED. get_edge_data remains a 0.23-0.36x incumbent LOSS and must not be cited otherwise. The revert is cancelled — not because the lever earned a reprieve, but because the direction is now measured rather than unknown, which is the condition the reopen set.

WITHDRAWN ON ITS OWN DATA: I filed br-r37-c1-ivxvs off two runs whose long-key control read 0.94x, implemented a candidate cause, measured it (0.9439x -> 0.9424x, so not the cause), and then found that control's median over all five admitted runs is 1.0051x. There is no long-key penalty to explain. ivxvs is closed NOT REPRODUCED with a retry predicate; the fallback change is kept as strictly less work for byte-identical output, and its comment states that no performance claim attaches to it.

Tests: the existing boundary sweep canonical_node_key_in_matches_the_owned_canonical guards the branch I changed and gained a multi-byte boundary case (38-44 chars / 114-132 bytes, straddling the buffer where the ASCII sweep cannot). fnx-python --lib 76 passed / 0 failed; workspace clippy -D warnings TRUE_EXIT=0; cargo fmt --check TRUE_EXIT=0; ubs TRUE_EXIT=0, 0 critical, no finding in the added ranges.

title: perf: lazy/arena attr-dict allocation to kill construction PyDict tax (6.9x)
description: Construction tax root cause (profiled this session): per-node and per-edge PyDict::new allocation in PyGraph/PyDiGraph dual-rep. add_nodes_from(100k int)=6.9x slower than nx (370ms; 100k PyDict allocs dominate, node_key_to_string is NOT the bottleneck -- proven, downcast fix shipped 8cff28f7f gave only ~15% on key-conversion paths). Many readers already use .get().map_or_else(empty,...) so they tolerate absence; the risk sites are (a) anything doing .get(node).unwrap() expecting Some-for-existing, (b) the access path needing &mut to allocate-and-store. Scope: ~100+ node_py_attrs/edge_py_attrs read sites across lib.rs/digraph.rs/views.rs/algorithms.rs/readwrite.rs/generators.rs. Target ratio: 6.9x->~1.5x on add_nodes_from, 4x->~2x on Graph(E). title: VF2 is_isomorphic infinite backtrack on isolate-heavy graphs (n>>e)
description:
fnx_algorithms::is_isomorphic walks g1 in node-insertion order during backtracking. On sparse graphs dominated by isolates (e.g. 64 nodes, 6 edges), this maps the first 55 isolates first, exploring 55! permutations before reaching any constrained node. Verified on artifact fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_isomorphism/timeout-34b79920... — fnx hangs >30s, nx returns in 2ms (~15000x slower). Same defect in is_isomorphic_directed.

Fix: precompute g1_order sorted by descending degree (sum of in+out for directed), backtrack via order[depth] instead of just depth. High-degree nodes anchor the search; isolates trivially satisfy their (empty) adjacency contract last.

Verified post-fix: 204µs on the timeout artifact, 120s fuzz_isomorphism burst clean (119972 runs), 819 algorithms unit tests pass.
notes: Fixed in same commit that filed this bead. Walk g1 in descending-degree order so constrained nodes anchor the search before isolates fan out — 55-isolate timeout collapses to 204µs (300000x speedup). Same fix applied to is_isomorphic_directed using in+out degree sum.

title: fix(private storage): subgraph of a graph with assigned _node keeps mapping nodes; nx yields an empty subgraph
description:
Found while verifying br-r37-c1-padm6 (native __contains__ private-override probe), on HEAD with a
build matching the working tree.

REPRO (all four classes, identical):
  g = fnx.Graph(); g.add_nodes_from(['a', 7, 2.5]); g._node = {'private': {}}
  sub = g.subgraph(['private'])
  list(sub.nodes)   fnx -> ['private']    nx -> []
  'private' in sub  fnx -> True           nx -> False

nx induces a subgraph over nodes that survive BOTH the node filter and the adjacency structure: only
_node was assigned, _adj still holds the native nodes, so no node survives and nx yields an empty
subgraph. fnx builds the induced node set from the assigned mapping alone and keeps 'private'.

NOT caused by padm6: sub.has_node('private') is also True, and has_node is bound straight to the raw
native slot with no private-override probe in either the pre- or post-lever build — so the node is
genuinely in the derived graph's native store, independent of how __contains__ is implemented. The
divergence is in subgraph node-set construction.

Same family as br-r37-c1-s8obc (assigned private storage is not honored consistently by derived
graphs) but a distinct code path and a distinct fix.

TEST THE FIX MUST CARRY: for all four classes, subgraph of a graph with an assigned _node mapping
matches nx's node set and membership answers, including the mixed case where _adj is ALSO assigned
(there the nodes should survive) — that mixed case is the negative a fix that simply returns an
empty subgraph would fail.

title: perf(cgse): add_edge autocreation files a redundant add_node ledger record — ~39% of add_edge is the ledger
description:
Split out of br-r37-c1-jc9e4 on measured evidence. NOT started. Needs a CGSE ruling before any code.

MEASURED (ledger_record_cost_ab arm A2, 3 runs, n=20000, 21 rounds): the CGSE ledger is 39.2-39.5% of Graph::add_edge_with_attrs on a growing graph — 318.9/320.9/322.6 ns/edge of 813.7/816.1/817.6. It is TWO records per edge, not one, because add_edge_with_attrs autocreates a missing endpoint via add_node -> add_node_with_attrs, which calls record_decision('add_node', ..) UNCONDITIONALLY at crates/fnx-classes/src/lib.rs:1164.

THE CANDIDATE: do not file the autocreation record. The add_edge outcome record already carries left_autocreated and right_autocreated evidence for exactly this event, so the second record appears to add no audit information a reader does not already have. Removing it would cut roughly half the ledger cost — about 20% of add_edge_with_attrs — for a change far smaller than br-r37-c1-g2nev's ~200-edit Cow migration, and the two compose.

WHY THIS IS NOT A FREE WIN AND MUST NOT BE TREATED AS ONE. CGSE non-regression is absolute. A caller-visible G.add_node() MUST keep producing its record; only the internal autocreation inside add_edge/add_edge_with_attrs is a candidate. So this needs (a) a ruling on whether the decision ledger's contract is 'one record per mutation CALL' or 'one record per user-visible OPERATION', (b) an unrecorded internal autocreation path rather than a flag that changes add_node's public behaviour, and (c) proof that no test, artifact or reproducibility ledger asserts the current record count for add_edge. There are existing *_unrecorded helpers (extend_nodes_unrecorded and friends) that establish the pattern for internal callers skipping the ledger.

MIRROR: DiGraph::add_edge_with_attrs (crates/fnx-classes/src/lib.rs:4308) has the same shape and the same record_decision at 4933 — check it before assuming this is one call site.

DO NOT re-derive: the share (39.3%), the mechanism (line 1164), and the fact that the A1 one-record arm understates it are all measured and recorded on br-r37-c1-jc9e4.
close_reason: Ruled (ledger unit is the OPERATION, per the *_records_once tests and the eo88t precedent), implemented across all 4 graph types via an extracted add_node_with_attrs_unrecorded, gated by a new both-halves test; add_edge_with_attrs 816 -> 507-540 ns/edge. Self-speedup, not campaign output.

title: perf-lever: rust-synced edge-weight store to close the weighted-attr-access floor (~0.6-0.72x on all weight= ops)
description: BOLD PERF LEVER (filed by cc, 2026-06-23, after 52 per-shape-audit wins). The remaining systematic fnx<nx residual is the WEIGHTED-ATTR-ACCESS FLOOR: every weight= reduction caps at ~0.6-0.72x because edge weights are PY-AUTHORITATIVE (edge_py_attrs) and read via a PyO3 get_item+extract per edge. Confirmed on: size(weight) 0.72-0.80x, degree(nbunch,weight) all-types (now native-subset'd but still floored at 0.53-0.69x), pagerank(weight) 0.80x. The native weighted-degree kernels already do the best possible given py-authoritative attrs (per-node PyList + builtins.sum for float parity). LEVER: maintain a rust-side numeric edge-weight mirror (f64 keyed by edge index, for the default/common weight key) updated on every edge write (like adj_indices), so weighted reductions sum in pure Rust with NO per-edge PyO3 — turning the whole weight= family from ~0.7x floor to dominant. Scope: edge-weight store in fnx-classes (Graph/Multi/Di/MultiDi) + maintenance across writers + a fast-path in the weighted-degree/size kernels gated on (weight==the-mirrored-key AND no dirty py override). Parity caveat: must preserve nx's float summation order (1-ULP) — mirror builtins.sum order or accept documented 1e-15 rel-err. Related closed family: the per-shape wrapper audit (edge-view + degree nbunch/weight natives, 52 wins) is DONE; this floor is what's left under it. See memory reference_degree_nbunch_weight_gap + project_perf_convergence_floor_taxonomy.

comments.text: CORRECTION (cc 2026-06-23): my earlier 'byte-exact rust fold' claim is WRONG. CPython builtins.sum is NEUMAIER-COMPENSATED (lib.rs:10833-10837 comment on _native_weighted_degree explicitly warns: build the value list in adjacency order + call the SAME builtin sum, do NOT fold with + in Rust). A naive rust f64 left-to-right sum DIVERGES from nx on FLOAT weights. So the lever is NOT a simple rust fold. Two safe routes: (A) INT-ONLY fast-path: rust i64 sum is exact (no compensation) — gate on all-edge-weights-are-Int (+ edge_py_attrs empty), bail to the py builtins.sum path on ANY Float weight. Helps int-weight graphs only (capacities/counts); float-weight graphs (e.g. random()) keep the floor. (B) Replicate CPython's compensated sum in rust (Neumaier) — version-sensitive, intricate, must match CPython 3.x exactly. Recommend (A) first (safe, bounded) then (B) if float-weight perf matters. The edge_py_attrs.is_empty() gate + inner.edge_attrs(u,v) CgseValue read (no new store) still hold. Did NOT implement — caught the Neumaier trap during feasibility, deferring to avoid a float-parity bug.

THE WEIGHTED-ATTR FLOOR DOES NOT REPRODUCE ON ANY ROW THIS BEAD NAMES — HOLD THE EDGE-WEIGHT STORE (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change. Bead stays OPEN; see the scope limits, which are real and mean this is not a close.

WHY I CHECKED BEFORE BUILDING. This bead proposes a rust-side numeric edge-weight mirror maintained across every writer in all four graph classes, plus fast paths in the weighted kernels, with a stated parity hazard (must preserve nx's float summation order to 1 ULP or accept documented 1e-15 rel-err). That is a large subsystem with a known correctness risk, and its entire justification is "~0.6-0.72x on all weight= ops" recorded 2026-06-23. MEASURED, live networkx 3.6.1 in the same invocation, balanced square, dual A/A nulls, 21 rounds, simple Graph, n=2000/8000 edges, INTEGER weights, extension built from HEAD (_fnx.abi3.so sha256 016b512e35fe25979fb29aa5c649701eb79a8acbd6cba21520c68b57afe85e87), taskset -c 40-47, load ~62 of 64. Two independent runs:

  row                          bead says      run 1      run 2      verdict
  G.degree(weight=) whole       (implied)    4.5553x    4.4037x    ADMISSIBLE both
  G.degree(nbunch, weight=)    0.53-0.69x    1.4869x    1.3893x    ADMISSIBLE both
  G.size(weight=)              0.72-0.80x   44.8368x   49.8986x    UNDECIDABLE both
  pagerank(weight=)                 0.80x       n/a     2.8659x    UNDECIDABLE

PARITY GATED BEFORE TIMING on every row: degree(weight), degree(nbunch, weight) and size(weight) compare equal to nx as dicts/values, and pagerank(weight) matches nx to 0.00e+00 — exactly, not approximately. A ratio against a different answer would be meaningless.

TWO ROWS ARE ADMISSIBLE TWICE and both are WINS. The other two refused their nulls and I am not quoting them as claims — but no reading of a 45-50x or 2.87x point estimate turns into the 0.72-0.80x and 0.80x losses this bead records. The floor it exists to close is not present on the rows it names.

SCOPE LIMITS, and they are why this is not a close:
  * simple Graph only. The bead says "all types"; MultiGraph/DiGraph/MultiDiGraph weighted degree is UNMEASURED here.

RECOMMENDATION: do not begin the edge-weight store on this bead's current evidence. title: Edge view iteration doesn't raise RuntimeError on graph mutation
description:
Follow-up to br-r37-c1-m25z2 (which fixed node iteration). The fix wires NodeIteratorGuard onto NODE __iter__ entrypoints (Graph, DiGraph, MultiGraph, MultiDiGraph + their NodeViews) but EDGE iteration (g.edges) still iterates a Rust-side snapshot silently.

Repro:
    g = fnx.path_graph(3)
    it = iter(g.edges)
    next(it)              # (0,1)
    g.add_edge(99, 100)   # mutates graph
    next(it)              # nx: RuntimeError 'dictionary changed size during iteration'
                          # fnx: silently returns (1, 2)

Same nx contract — dict-backed iteration raises RuntimeError on any structural change. fnx node-iter fix needs to extend to edge-iter via an analogous EdgeIteratorGuard on EdgeView.__iter__ for all 4 graph types (and likely in/out edge views on DiGraph).

P3 because edge-iteration-during-mutation is a less common pattern than node-iteration-during-mutation, and the architectural scaffolding from m25z2 makes the extension straightforward (mirror the NodeIteratorGuard pattern).

comments.text:
SATISFIED AT 11 CASES — BUT BLIND TO ATTRIBUTE KEY ORDER, AND IT NEVER TOUCHED THE BATCH PATH
(CopperCliff, 2026-08-08).

tests/python/test_attribute_preservation_parity.py already existed and matched this bead: all nine
named transforms (copy / subgraph / edge_subgraph / to_directed / relabel / subgraph_copy / ego_graph
/ induced_subgraph / restricted_view), union / disjoint_union / compose, and the compose
conflicting-graph-attr last-writer-wins case, at 9 + 1 + 1 = 11 cases — exactly the figure specified.
I checked before writing.

GAP 1 — `dict(d) == dict(d)` IS BLIND TO KEY ORDER. `_assert_same_attrs` compares node and edge
attribute dicts by value, so it cannot see the ORDER of the attribute keys. On a bead whose whole
subject is "attributes preserved", key order is exactly what flips silently. `_node_attrs` also
str-keys into a dict (blind to node iteration order) and `_edge_attrs` sorts each endpoint pair
(blind to edge direction and edge order).

GAP 2 — THE FIXTURE ONLY USED PER-ITEM ADDS. Attributes were built with `add_node(...)` and
`add_edge(...)` in a loop. `add_nodes_from` / `add_edges_from` commit through a DIFFERENT collector,
and multi-attr key order on that route is a named defect class in this codebase (an AttrMap backed by
a BTreeMap alphabetises: `label` would sort before `weight`). The test could not reach it.

MEASURED BEFORE ASSERTING — no divergence anywhere, on either construction route:
  * attribute key order (node, edge, graph-level): identical to nx for all nine transforms and all
    three operators;
  * node iteration order and RAW edge tuples (endpoints unsorted): identical, 0 divergences;
  * batch-built fixture: node and edge attr key order identical to nx, and still identical after a
    copy().
So the BTreeMap alphabetisation class does not bite these paths today. Nothing locked it, which is
the point of the change.

ADDED: `_attributed_batch` (the same fixture via add_nodes_from/add_edges_from),
`_attr_key_order`, and three tests — transform key-order + node/edge order parity, operator
key-order parity, and the existing value-level assertion re-run against both construction routes.
Every one parametrised over BOTH builders.

MUTATION-CHECKED: an attribute dict with the same items in alphabetised order — exactly what the
named defect class would produce — PASSES the existing `dict(d) == dict(d)` comparison and FAILS the

title: perf(storage): PyGraph mirror maps use SipHash while the core IndexMap uses FxHash — 6.48% of G.nodes[n]
description:
MEASURED, load-independent (CrimsonBeaver, 2026-08-14). callgrind --collect-atstart=no --toggle-collect on NodeView::__pymethod___getitem____, so the module import is excluded. ELF d15815d45ff22096, IR_REPS=20000, PYTHONHASHSEED=0. G.nodes[n] costs 603.3 Ir/call, and three SipHash entries appear in its profile:

   3.24%  core::hash::sip::Hasher<Sip13Rounds>::write
   1.62%  std::hash::random::RandomState::hash_one::<&alloc::string::String>
   1.62%  std::hash::random::RandomState::hash_one::<&str>
  ------
   6.48%  ~39 Ir/call

THE ASYMMETRY. fnx_classes stores adjacency in IndexMap<String, _, rustc_hash::FxBuildHasher> — the profile shows IndexMap::get_index_of::<str> with FxHash on the same call path. But the PyGraph-side Python mirror maps are plain std HashMap, i.e. RandomState/SipHash-1-3. From new_empty_with_policy in crates/fnx-python/src/lib.rs:

    node_key_map:   HashMap::new(),
    node_py_attrs:  HashMap::new(),
    edge_py_attrs:  HashMap::new(),
    adj_py_keys:    HashMap::new(),
    adj_row_py:     HashMap::new(),

So one canonical String key gets hashed with FxHash for the storage lookup and SipHash for the mirror lookup, in the same call. Node keys are short strings, which is exactly where SipHash-1-3's fixed setup cost is worst relative to FxHash.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE SWAP, and this is the part that needs care rather than a sed: std HashMap iteration order depends on the hasher, and these maps ARE iterated. _fnx_sync_attrs_to_inner walks edge_py_attrs and node_py_attrs to push mirrors back into the store; that particular loop is order-insensitive because it replaces per-key. But this project's whole premise is observable iteration order, and rustc_hash is NOT DoS-resistant, so the change needs (a) an audit of every iteration site of these five maps for order leakage into any public output, and (b) a note that node keys are attacker-controllable in the readwrite parsers, which is the security doctrine's stated threat surface — FxHash there is a deliberate tradeoff, not a free win. If any site leaks order, use FxIndexMap (deterministic insertion order) rather than FxHashMap.

ACCEPTANCE TEST, decidable at any host load: re-run the toggle-collect profile and require the three sip/RandomState entries to vanish from the G.nodes[n] breakdown, with per-call Ir dropping by roughly 39. Parity gate is the full Python suite (55097 passed / 0 failed on b3020c27f) plus the CGSE iteration-order tests.

SIZE, stated honestly: this is a 6.48% item on one probe, materially smaller than br-r37-c1-afiq8 (from_utf8, 16.05-17.53% on two probes) and the PyObject_Hash item (21.90%). Take those first. Filed so the observation is not lost, not because it should jump the queue.

    nx   list(g.edges('private'))  -> KeyError: 'private'
    fnx  list(g.edges('private'))  -> []

CAUSE: _AssignedPrivateEdgeView._nbunch tests 'nbunch in self._graph' - node-view membership. Under an assigned _node the node view is the override, so:
  - 'a' (a real adjacency row, absent from the override) fails the scalar test, falls through to the iterable branch, gets iterated AS A STRING, and yields nothing.
  - 'private' (in the override, no adjacency row) passes the scalar test and then contributes no edges, where nx raises.

networkx filters nbunch against _adj (nbunch_iter), which is why it finds 'a' and rejects 'private'.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH ka7fd: that bead's repro and scope are G.edges() with no nbunch, now matching nx on all four classes. Extending _nbunch to filter on the adjacency also requires reproducing nx's RAISE for a node absent from _adj, which is a separate contract (nx surfaces it lazily from nbunch_iter). Doing both under one bead would have mixed a fix with an unrelated error-contract change.

TESTS THE FIX MUST CARRY: edges('a') returns the edge; edges('private') raises the same exception CLASS as nx; a list nbunch mixing both behaves as nx does; all four graph classes; and tests/python/test_edge_view_under_private_node_store.py must stay green.

NOTE: a test asserting this parity was written and removed while closing ka7fd - it failed because the behaviour is genuinely wrong, not because the test was. Do not re-add it as a pin of current behaviour.
close_reason: Fixed in e44bd9eee: _nbunch now filters an explicit nbunch against the ADJACENCY rather than the node view, reproducing networkx's asymmetry exactly — a scalar is matched against the node view and returned unfiltered so a node with no adjacency row RAISES (edges('private') -> KeyError), while an iterable is filtered against the adjacency so the same node is silently skipped (edges(['a','private']) -> [('a','b')]). The row-lookup guard added under ka7fd was removed as part of this: with nbunch=None yielding adjacency keys and iterables pre-filtered, it could only fire on the scalar case, the one place nx deliberately raises. Verified across 4 graph classes x 6 nbunch shapes = 24 combinations against live nx 3.6.1, comparing edge lists or exception type, zero mismatches. 9922 passed in the broad selection; ubs clean.

title: all_pairs_dijkstra: redundant BFS tie-break + PyO3 round-trips
description:
fnx.all_pairs_dijkstra ran 329ms vs nx 117ms (3x slower) on a 200-node 1k-edge weighted Watts-Strogatz. Post-processing dominated: 200 sources × ~1ms reorder = 192ms outside the Rust kernel.

Root causes: _reorder_by_distance unconditionally built a BFS visit-order index for tie-breaking, even when distances were already unique (most weighted graphs have no ties). Worse, _bfs_visit_order pulled G.adj[u] per visit — each a PyO3 round-trip.

Fix: (1) Skip BFS entirely when len(set(dist_values)) == len(dists). Stable sort by distance suffices. (2) Pre-snapshot G.adj into a plain dict in all_pairs_dijkstra and pass it through to the new _bfs_visit_order_from_adj for the rare tie-break case.

Result: 329ms -> 161ms (~2x faster). Now within 1.4x of nx (was 3x). 220 dijkstra tests pass; 17506 total tests pass.
notes: Fixed in same commit. Fast path skips BFS for unique-distance dijkstra outputs; tie-break path uses snapshotted adj dict instead of per-step PyO3 round-trip.

LEVER (replace the data structure): either (a) a generational slot-map / stable-id node store with a separate insertion-order list (O(1) order-preserving removal, no renumber), or (b) lazy cache rebuild behind a dirty flag (skip the per-remove repair; rebuild adj_indices/edge_index_endpoints once on next read) — currently blocked by the &self  API (can't rebuild on immutable read without RefCell, which changes the return type used by locked fnx-algorithms callers) + no-unsafe. Option (b) needs a coordinated API change with fnx-algorithms (TealSpring-locked). Target: remove_nodes_from(half) parity with nx (~2ms). fnx-classes substrate is unreserved.

title: Blossom matching i32 overflow on moderate fuzz inputs
description:
fnx_algorithms::max_weight_matching / min_weight_matching feed quantized i32 weights to the mwmatching crate. The original scale capped per-edge weight at i32::MAX, but mwmatching's primal-dual update at lib.rs:691 ('2*wt + dualvar[i] + dualvar[j]') and at lib.rs:709 ('s += 2*dualvar[bi]' walking blossom-parent paths) accumulates O(n) dual values during the algorithm. Each dual variable starts at max_weight and can grow, so the intermediate slack can reach O(n * max_weight) — overflowing i32 when max_weight is anywhere near i32::MAX/4.

cargo fuzz builds release-with-overflow-checks, so the wrap manifested as a panic at mwmatching-0.1.1/src/lib.rs:691:30 'attempt to add with overflow' on fuzz_matching/crash-a653763f (n=30, e=6, weights in [-236, 177]). Production builds without overflow checks would silently corrupt instead — strictly worse.

Fix: scale per-edge weight to i32::MAX / (4 * endpoint_count) so the dual accumulator has headroom proportional to n. Verified: artifact runs in 2ms (was deadly signal), 120s fuzz_matching burst clean (142291 runs), 819 algorithms unit tests pass.
notes: Fixed in same commit that filed this bead. Per-edge weight ceiling lowered from i32::MAX/4 to i32::MAX/(4*endpoint_count), so internal slack accumulator can grow proportional to n without wrapping. Tightening is invisible at the public API — quantization scale just shifts down, weight ratios preserved.

title: Perf: Rust pagerank is 2.5x slower than nx (scipy.sparse-backed) on 100-node DiGraph
description:
On a 100-node 975-edge DiGraph, fnx.pagerank(alpha=0.85) takes ~3.83ms vs nx's 1.51ms — ratio 0.39x (memory_reference_perf_probe_methodology.md noted this gap). Decomposition shows ALL the time is inside _raw_pagerank (Rust kernel): 3.17ms of the 3.18ms total.

Root cause hypothesis: nx's default _pagerank_scipy uses scipy.sparse matrix-vector multiply (highly optimized C). Our Rust kernel uses a Vec<Vec<(usize, f64)>> CSR-like representation + scalar power iteration in pure Rust. For 100x100 matrices, scipy.sparse is faster than naive scalar Rust because of vectorization (BLAS).

Fix options (in order of effort):
1. Call to_scipy_sparse_array from Python pagerank wrapper, then do matvec in numpy — leverages our existing native COO builder (br-r37-c1-lqlx2). Cost: ~50 LOC in __init__.py, no Rust changes.
2. Use ndarray in Rust pagerank kernel — converts Vec<Vec<>> to a CsMat and uses sprs crate. Cost: dependency add + ~100 LOC.
3. Delegate to nx like louvain does. Cost: ~5 LOC but loses Rust correctness contract.

Recommend option 1 first — it builds on the existing native COO builder and keeps all the Rust precondition checks.

comments.author: SunnyTern
comments.text:
THE 0.44-0.82x COPY LOSS DOES NOT REPRODUCE ON HEAD — DO NOT START THE CSR MIGRATION ON THIS BEAD'S CURRENT EVIDENCE (SunnyTern, 2026-08-09). No source change. Bead stays OPEN, but its premise and its recommended lever both need re-deciding first.

WHY I CHECKED. This bead recommends "migrate MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph adjacency to integer-CSR rows like DiGraph did — large data-structure change". That is a multi-session change, and its whole justification is a 0.44-0.82x loss measured 2026-06-20. Since then MultiGraph moved to MgSlabStorage, whose adjacency rows are INTEGER-keyed already (`rows: Vec<IndexMap<usize, CompactKeys>>` over a `node_order` String->slot map), so the bead's stated cause — "store succ+pred+edges as nested String-keyed IndexMaps" — is now true of MultiDiGraph but NOT of MultiGraph. A premise that has half-expired is worth re-measuring before spending a data-structure migration on it.

MEASURED TWO WAYS, 2000 nodes / 8000 edges, attr-less, live networkx 3.6.1, extension built from HEAD (_fnx.abi3.so sha256 016b512e35fe25979fb29aa5c649701eb79a8acbd6cba21520c68b57afe85e87).

1. INSTRUCTION COUNTS (callgrind, deterministic, decides at any load — host was 75-107 of 64). Ir per copy, baseline-subtracted, both libraries measured identically:

                     nx Ir/copy     fnx Ir/copy    ratio nx/fnx
  Graph              41,354,563       5,108,298        8.10x
  MultiGraph        232,015,356      89,125,844        2.60x
  MultiDiGraph      131,372,414      23,656,679        5.55x

2. WALL CLOCK (balanced square, live nx same invocation, dual A/A nulls):

  Graph.copy()          6.2023x  CI95 [5.1638, 7.4165]   nulls 1.5550 / 1.3397  UNDECIDABLE
  MultiGraph.copy()     2.1200x  CI95 [1.7591, 2.7956]   nulls 0.6715 / 0.6748  UNDECIDABLE
  MultiDiGraph.copy()   2.6102x  CI95 [2.4327, 2.7983]   nulls 1.0023 / 0.9486  UNDECIDABLE

ALL THREE WALL-CLOCK ROWS REFUSED and I am not quoting their ratios as claims. Copy allocates and frees whole graphs per slot, so the arms are non-stationary across a run — the same failure mode the standing note records for mutation/build arms, and the same one that made add_edge refuse three times today. A gc between slots was already in place and was not enough.

WHAT IS DECIDED IS THE INSTRUCTION COUNT. It needs no A/A null because it is deterministic — repeat runs on this instrument have drifted by ~700 Ir in 756M today. On that measure all three copies are WINS by 2.6-8.1x. The wall-clock point estimates agree in direction and roughly in magnitude (2.1-6.2x) even though they are inadmissible, so two independent measures point the same way and neither is anywhere near 0.44-0.82x.

CAVEAT, STATED BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE WAY THE OLD FIGURE COULD STILL BE RIGHT: Ir under-represents allocator and page-fault time, and copy is allocation-heavy. A large Ir win with a wall-clock loss is physically possible if fnx's copy has much worse locality. That is exactly why I ran the wall-clock arm too — and it did not support the loss either; it refused. So the loss is unsupported rather than refuted, and the correct next step is a wall-clock re-measure on a substrate that can hold a copy arm, NOT a data-structure migration.

WHAT I RECOMMEND FOR THIS BEAD:
  * do not begin the integer-CSR migration until a wall-clock copy measurement admits;
  * if it does admit as a loss, note the target is now MultiDiGraph specifically — MultiGraph's rows are already integer-keyed via the slab, which is the likeliest reason its Ir gap (2.60x) is the smallest of the three;
  * the substrate problem is the real blocker, and it is shared with add_edge: build/copy arms that allocate whole graphs per slot do not hold still. Whoever fixes that unblocks several rows at once.

ALSO IN THIS BEAD, UNTOUCHED: the "simple_cycles 0.57x is delegation order-blocked" note. I did not measure it and it is independent of everything above.

My last entry reported the instruction-count wins (MG 2.60x, MDG 5.55x, Graph 8.10x) and three UNDECIDABLE wall-clock rows, and concluded the 0.44-0.82x loss was unsupported rather than refuted. A second run of the same square admitted one of them:

  MultiGraph.copy()   2.3134x  CI95 [2.1949, 2.4065]   A/A nulls 1.0011 / 1.0032   ADMISSIBLE

So for MultiGraph the 0.44-0.82x figure is REFUTED on wall clock, not merely unsupported: 2.3134x with both nulls inside the bound, and it agrees with the deterministic instruction count (2.60x) taken independently.

THE OTHER TWO STILL REFUSE, and I am not quoting them:

  Graph.copy()        5.4523x   nulls 0.9528 / 0.9438   UNDECIDABLE
  MultiDiGraph.copy() 2.7741x   nulls 1.1329 / 1.1996   UNDECIDABLE

Both point estimates match their Ir counterparts in direction and rough magnitude (8.10x, 5.55x), so nothing here suggests a loss anywhere — but MultiDiGraph, which is the type whose adjacency is still nested String-keyed and therefore the actual target of this bead's proposed CSR migration, remains without an admissible wall-clock row.

RECOMMENDATION UNCHANGED AND NOW SHARPER: hold the integer-CSR migration. MultiGraph — whose rows are already integer-keyed via MgSlabStorage — now has an admissible 2.31x WIN, so the bead's premise is dead for that half. MultiDiGraph needs one admissible wall-clock row before a multi-session data-structure change can be justified, and the only thing standing in the way is that copy arms allocate whole graphs per slot and will not hold still. title: fuzz_community timeout — Louvain threshold clamp too tight (1e-9 -> excessive iterations)
description:
fuzz_community::Louvain clamps threshold to [1e-9, 1.0]. Threshold=1e-9 forces Louvain through many tiny modularity-delta iterations, hitting the 5s libFuzzer timeout on 14-byte inputs (e.g. b'\xff
\x8a\x08\xff
\xff,\xff-\x82
\x04\x00'). This is a harness performance issue, not a correctness bug — Louvain is just iterating to convergence at a tighter-than-typical threshold. Fix: raise the threshold lower bound to 1e-6 (matches nx's default 1e-7 ceiling for sane fuzzing) so the fuzzer doesn't drive into pathological convergence. Keep the upper bound at 1.0.
notes:
FIXED. Root cause was NOT the threshold clamp — it was catastrophic float cancellation in louvain_one_level's gain formula (-w_curr/m + 1/m → 0 ± 1.25e-17 ULP). The 'strictly > 0' check accepted this float-dust as a real improvement, sending the algorithm into infinite community-tag oscillation. Reproduces deterministically on triangle+isolates with res=1e-3, thr=1e-6, seed=None (artifacts timeout-0f895372 and timeout-ece83bdf both hit it).

Fix (in louvain_one_level): require gain > LOUVAIN_GAIN_EPS (1e-12) instead of > 0.0. Verified on both timeout artifacts (~24µs each, was infinite). 819 algorithms unit tests still pass.

Also surfaced a separate harness issue: f64::clamp(NaN,..) propagates NaN, fed NaN resolution into modularity → 'modularity returned non-finite' assertion. Fixed via finite_clamp() helper that treats non-finite inputs as the lower bound. 90s burst clean (124k runs).

title: perf(link-prediction): preferential_attachment is the only one of four metrics with no native explicit-ebunch scorer — 0.8635x while its sibling jaccard is 3.2523x
description:
Filed by OliveDesert from the br-r37-c1-3s8x7 re-measure (2026-08-08). Full evidence in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

MEASURED, same-invocation live nx 3.6.1, dual A/A nulls, DECIDABLE:
  preferential_attachment n=1200 pairs=300 -> 0.8635x CI95 [0.8578, 0.8682]
  jaccard_coefficient    n=1200 pairs=300 -> 3.2523x CI95 [3.2444, 3.2573]
Identical graph, identical 300 pairs, identical _link_prediction_validate_ebunch.

STAGE ATTRIBUTION (whole-call deficit 22.99us; fnx 221.28us vs nx 198.29us):
  ebunch validation      fnx 50.69us vs nx 42.88us  -> +7.81us (34%)
  endpoint degree batch  fnx 93.85us vs nx 152.65us -> -58.80us (fnx WINS 1.6191x)
  residual scoring path                              -> +73.98us
So it is NOT ebunch validation (padm6 already cut that overhead ~93%, from 116us to 7.81us) and NOT the degree batch.

MECHANISM, read from source: jaccard_coefficient (:17606), adamic_adar_index (:17623) and resource_allocation_index (:17649) each carry 'if materialized is not None and type(G) is Graph: return _X_native_scores(G, materialized)'. preferential_attachment (:17627) has NO such sibling and falls through to the generic _link_prediction_compute closure machinery (nbr_order/nbr_set/deg caches + per-pair closure dispatch). It is the one member of a four-metric family that never got the native scorer — and the arithmetically simplest of the four (deg(u)*deg(v)).

LEVER: add the _pa_native_scores sibling. The native degree row already exists and already wins (1.6191x); what is missing is the scorer that consumes it without the generic machinery.

PARITY BAR (absolute): nx returns int scores for preferential_attachment and yields in ebunch order. Any native scorer must produce byte-identical (u, v, int) triples over all 300 pairs, keep the lazy generator semantics (nx's _apply_prediction returns a generator; the NodeNotFound/NetworkXNotImplemented raises stay EAGER per br-r37-c1-scceager), and preserve the default-ebunch non_edges path untouched.

RE-DECIDE on the same substrate: output parity over all 300 predictions asserted before timing, both per-stage nulls inside 0.98-1.02.

SHIPPED AS MAINTENANCE, STILL A LOSS. 0.8635x -> 0.9833x on the harness workload. Closes ~88% of the gap to 1.0; does NOT reach parity. Reported as a loss because it is one.

CHANGE: added _pa_native_scores, the explicit-ebunch scorer that jaccard/adamic_adar/resource_allocation already had and preferential_attachment did not. One degree batch then a direct dict-indexed product per pair, replacing the generic _link_prediction_compute machinery (3 neighbour caches, 4-way metric dispatch, 2 closure frames per pair). The whole-graph-vs-endpoint-subset branch is carried over verbatim so pa-degbatch and pa-endpointbatch keep their behaviour. Subclasses keep the generic path.

MEASURED (same ELF 80488d1e..., same-invocation live nx 3.6.1, 41 rounds, taskset -c 40-47, balanced ABBA square, parity asserted over all 300 predictions before timing):
  before 0.8635x CI95 [0.8578, 0.8682]  nulls 0.9979 / 1.0000
  after  0.9833x CI95 [0.9786, 0.9884]  nulls 1.0011 / 1.0028
  jaccard collateral control 3.2523x -> 3.2485x (unperturbed)
The after-CI sits wholly BELOW 1.0, so the remaining ~1.7% loss is decidable too.

A TRAP I WALKED INTO, FILED SO NOBODY REPEATS IT (br-r37-c1-qqj23): a second probe reported the same code at 1.0336x — a WIN — because it rebuilt the workload with bare (u,v) tuples while perf_harness._build_pair emits (u,v,{}). I published the harness build's 0.9833x and did NOT publish the friendlier 1.0336x.

title: fix(top-level namespace): 27 fnx-owned submodules are absent from __all__, so 'from franken_networkx import *' binds fewer names than nx
description:
Same defect class as br-r37-c1-ibcok (drawing), at the TOP LEVEL and much larger.

networkx declares no __all__, so 'from networkx import *' binds every public
module-level name — 944 of them. franken_networkx declares an explicit __all__ of
766, so the same star-import binds a different set.

Measured on HEAD 12428da9c against live networkx 3.6.1:

  nx star-import surface   944 names
  fnx __all__              766 names
  missing from fnx star    189 names (all 189 still resolve as ATTRIBUTES)

The 189 split cleanly in two, and only the first group is in scope here:

GROUP A (27) — names franken_networkx DEFINES IN ITS OWN MODULE DICT while
omitting them from __all__. Unambiguous omissions, zero delegation involved:

  approximation bipartite chordal clique community components convert_matrix
  core dag drawing euler flow hybrid minors moral operators planarity readwrite
  regular smallworld sparsifiers summarization swap tournament traversal tree
  triads

So 'from networkx import *; bipartite.sets(G)' works and the fnx spelling raises
NameError.

GROUP B (162) — NOT in fnx's module dict; they resolve only through the
module-level __getattr__ fallback into networkx (AmbiguousSolution,
ExceededMaxIterations, GraphMLReader, GraphMLWriter, PlanarEmbedding, plus ~157
nx-internal submodule names like astar/atlas/attracting). Exporting those would
make fnx's star surface depend on nx being importable, which is a design
decision, not a bug fix. Filed separately.

FIX: extend __all__ with the Group A names. Note that 'approximation' is a
_ApproximationNamespace instance, not a ModuleType, and its __name__ attribute is
swallowed by its own __getattr__ — so a rule keyed on isinstance(v, ModuleType)
silently misses it (verified: such a rule selects 26 of the 27).

TEST: every public name in vars(franken_networkx) that networkx also star-exports
must appear in __all__ — self-maintaining, so a future submodule that is added
without being exported fails the test. Plus an explicit assertion that the 27
names bind. NEGATIVE CASE: __all__ must not start exporting 'copyreg' (an
accidental stdlib import leak, see the Group B bead) and the count must not
regress below nx's for names fnx owns.

title: test: clique enumeration parity + clique/IS complement duality
description: find_cliques set+count+clique-number parity vs nx + clique/independent-set complement dualities (a clique in G is an independent set in complement(G); alpha(G)=omega(complement(G))). Oracle-free dualities jointly pinning clique machinery + complement op. 120 cases.
close_reason: TWO GAPS, and the second is the more interesting one. (1) MAXIMALITY WAS NEVER ASSERTED. find_cliques promises MAXIMAL cliques and this file checked only that the returned sets behave like cliques. Measured mutant: dropping one node from each clique of size >= 3 still yields valid cliques - a subset of a clique IS a clique - and it fails maximality on 32 of the 32 applicable draws. The clique half was also reached only THROUGH the complement (no edge of comp(G) inside the set), so a find_cliques and a complement that were wrong together satisfied it; membership in G is now checked directly, without the complement in the loop. Also added that every node lies in at least one maximal clique. Honest scope note: the pre-existing nx parity test WOULD catch that mutant, because the returned sets differ. What it would not catch is a shared error, and this file exists for its ORACLE-FREE dualities - so the addition strengthens the half that stands without a reference implementation, not the half that already has one. (2) THE DUALITY TEST DOES NOT TEST THE DUALITY. test_independence_number_equals_complement_clique_number computes omega(complement(G)) with fnx, computes omega(complement(G)) with networkx, and compares them. That is the SAME quantity twice - a parity check - and alpha(G) never appears in it, so the identity alpha(G) == omega(complement(G)) that the test is named for is never exercised. Added alongside it: alpha(G) computed by exhaustive search over node subsets, with no clique machinery involved, verified equal to omega(complement(G)) on all 40 draws (alpha ranged 2 to 5, so the search is doing real work). I left the original test in place rather than replacing it - it is a valid parity check, just misnamed for what it does. Evidence: file 120 -> 200 passed, no skips; 596 passed across the clique family (clique_family_parity, clustering_cliques). description: histogram[k]==#nodes-with-degree-k; sum(hist)==n; sum(k*hist[k])==2|E| (handshaking via histogram); K_n hist[n-1]==n; path/star closed forms. Cross-checks degree_histogram vs degree view. ~50 cases.

title: [parity] power() silently leaks internal canonical key encoding 'str:<len>:<val>' for every string node
description:
Found by the generated NetworkX 3.6.1 behavioral oracle (HEAD 3f5d6fe73, corpus feature_behavioral_corpus_v1.json, identity group for networkx.power / networkx.algorithms.operators.power).

DIVERGENCE: both sides return OK, values differ. Silent - no exception is raised. 2 present-marked paths:
  networkx.power, networkx.algorithms.operators.power

SYMPTOM: every STRING node in the returned graph is renamed to its internal canonical encoding 'str:<len>:<value>'.
  G = fnx.Graph([('a','b'),('b','c'),('c','d')]); fnx.power(G, 2)
    nodes -> ['str:1:a','str:1:b','str:1:c','str:1:d']     (nx: ['a','b','c','d'])
    edges -> [('str:1:a','str:1:b'), ('str:1:a','str:1:c'), ...]  (nx: [('a','b'),('a','c'),...])

The graph STRUCTURE is correct - only the node labels are mangled - which makes this worse, not better: the result looks plausible and every downstream lookup, join, or comparison against the source graph silently misses.

BLAST RADIUS (measured, k=2 and k=3):
  str nodes    -> DIVERGES
  mixed str/int-> DIVERGES on the str nodes only ('a'->'str:1:a', 1 stays 1)
  int nodes    -> OK
  tuple nodes  -> OK
So it is string-keyed nodes specifically, i.e. the default in most real usage.

EXACT REPRODUCER (corpus exact_input, id connected-255201293, undirected simple Graph, k=2):
  nodes n0..n6; edges (n0,n1)(n1,n2)(n2,n3)(n3,n4)(n4,n5)(n5,n6)(n4,n1)(n3,n0)(n6,n3)(n2,n5)(n0,n4)
  fnx.power(G,2).nodes() -> ['str:2:n0', ...]   nx.power(G,2).nodes() -> ['n0', ...]

This is the canonical-str-key divergence class: an internal lazy/encoded key escaping into user-visible output instead of being decoded on the way out. Fix = decode canonical keys when materializing the result graph in the power() path, then re-run the oracle write/check contract.
close_reason: Fixed in d1dcf6a3f: added _canonical_node_key (exact Python mirror of the Rust node_key_to_string encoder) and keyed power()'s reverse map with it. Scope was wider than the oracle found - str, float, bool and mixed all leaked; float/bool also came back as the wrong TYPE. 44 parity checks across all node-key types at k=1..4, 0 mismatches.

title: all_pairs_bellman_ford_path: duplicate Rust BF call to compute distances
description:
fnx.all_pairs_bellman_ford_path called both _raw_all_pairs_bellman_ford_path AND _raw_all_pairs_bellman_ford_path_length — running the full Bellman-Ford kernel TWICE just so we'd have distances for the per-source reorder. On a 200-node 1k-edge weighted graph: 392ms (path) + 345ms (length) = 737ms in Rust, plus ~40ms post-processing = 775ms total vs nx's 277ms.

Fix: derive distances by summing edge weights along each returned path using a pre-cached frozenset-keyed edge-weight dict. Build cost ~3ms; lookup is O(1). Same optimization applied to all_pairs_dijkstra_path. 

Measured: all_pairs_bellman_ford_path 745ms -> 440ms (~40% faster); all_pairs_dijkstra_path 252ms -> 197ms. 313 dijkstra/bellman tests pass; 17506 total tests pass.

Also added _snapshot_edge_weights helper and _path_lengths_from_paths so other APSP wrappers can reuse.
notes: Fixed by deriving distances from paths via cached edge-weight dict instead of running BF/Dijkstra twice. Helpers _snapshot_edge_weights / _path_lengths_from_paths are reusable for other APSP wrappers.

description:

  cargo test --release -p fnx-python --lib -- single_source_shortest_path_deep_paths
  algorithms::tests::single_source_shortest_path_deep_paths_are_independent_and_ordered FAILED
  crates/fnx-python/src/algorithms.rs:28420  assertion left == right failed  left: 0  right: 33

The test seeds the graph through graph.inner.add_edge(node.to_string(), ...), i.e. RAW '0'/'1' strings, but then queries with a PyString source, which node_key_to_string canonicalizes to 'str:1:0'. The canonical never matches the raw inner key, so the result dict is empty and rendered.len() is 0 instead of 33.

Either the fixture must seed canonical keys (node_key_to_string of each endpoint) or it must build through the PyGraph API. Decide which contract the test is meant to pin before editing it -- if the intended contract is that inner and canonical keys agree, the DEFECT is in production, not the test, and this bead must not be closed by rewriting the fixture.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED in 41f80b3c2. Adjudication as the bead required: the defect was in the FIXTURE, not production.

PRODUCTION IS CORRECT (the bead's own retry predicate, executed): fnx.single_source_shortest_path on a 33-node path graph vs live networkx 3.6.1 returns 33 paths, dict equality True, key ORDER identical.

Two-stage diagnosis:
 1. Seeding the inner map with production's own canonical (node_key_to_string) made the length assertion pass but the last-path assertion then failed with keys rendered as raw canonicals: ('str:2:32', ['0','str:1:1',...]). So canonical-key seeding alone is still not the contract.

The assertions were NOT weakened — they were restored from vacuous. With an empty result dict the first/last/independence assertions never ran; they all execute now. cargo test -p fnx-python --lib 73 passed / 0 failed (was 72/1); clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] signature mismatches blocked nx drop-in kwarg calls (8 functions)
description:
A signature sweep comparing every fnx public function against its networkx counterpart surfaced real drop-in breakage. Missing nx-style kwargs caused TypeErrors on documented calls:

- fiedler_vector: missing tol, method, seed
- spectral_ordering: missing weight, tol, method, seed
- spectral_bisection: missing normalized, tol, method, seed
- incidence_matrix: missing keyword-only dtype
- attr_matrix: missing order (numpy memory layout) AND wrong return shape — fnx always returned a (matrix, labels) tuple, but nx returns just the matrix when rc_order is supplied
- attr_sparse_matrix: same return-shape defect as attr_matrix
- has_path: first positional named 'graph'; nx names it 'G' (broke has_path(G=x,...))
- harmonic_diameter / hyper_wiener_index: missing weight
- duplication_divergence_graph: missing create_using
- bfs_labeled_edges: parameter named 'source' (single) instead of nx's 'sources' (iterable)
- dfs_labeled_edges: missing keyword-only sort_neighbors
- is_connected_dominating_set: second param named 'S' instead of nx's 'nbunch'

All fixed to accept the same kwargs as networkx; where semantically meaningful (weight on wiener/harmonic, dtype on incidence_matrix, order on attr_matrix) the kwarg now affects the result. Others (tol/method/seed on the dense spectral solvers) are accepted for signature parity and noted as ignored by the deterministic numpy.linalg.eigh path.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] bethe_hessian_matrix: wrong return type AND wrong values
description: Two defects in fnx.bethe_hessian_matrix: (1) returned a legacy scipy.sparse.csr_matrix while nx returns csr_array — isinstance(r, csr_array) was False. (2) Computed A = adjacency(G, weight=None) and regularizer r from A.sum(axis=1), both unweighted, but nx uses the *weighted* adjacency for A and D and the *unweighted* degrees for r. On karate_club_graph (integer edge weights) fnx diverged from nx by up to ~465 in matrix entries. Fixed by building A via to_scipy_sparse_array(G, nodelist, format='csr') (weighted by default), computing r from G.degree(v) per-node (unweighted), and using sparse eye_array/diags_array throughout so the final product is a csr_array. Verified on karate, cycle5, K4, havel_hakimi; spectrum matches too.
close_reason: Fixed type (csr_array) and values. Verified across weighted and unweighted fixtures; spectrum matches; existing tests pass.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] laplacian / normalized_laplacian returned csr_matrix instead of csr_array
description: fnx.laplacian_matrix and fnx.normalized_laplacian_matrix built their results with scipy.sparse.diags() and scipy.sparse.eye() (both returning legacy csr_matrix). networkx returns csr_array from its laplacian helpers, so isinstance(r, csr_array) was False on fnx. Fixed by switching to diags_array / eye_array and tocsr()-casting the final product. Verified on karate, cycle5, K4, path3 and weighted fixtures.
close_reason: Fixed: sparse-array helpers throughout, .tocsr() on final product; type and values match nx.

title: REVIEW: [CRITICAL] floyd_warshall_numpy silently skipped weight-0 edges → wrong shortest distances
description: fnx.floyd_warshall_numpy initialised its distance matrix by copying weights from to_numpy_array(G) but gated assignment on `if A[i,j] != 0`. to_numpy_array's default nonedge value is 0.0, so weight-0 edges were indistinguishable from absent edges and dropped from the initial distance matrix — leaving dist[i,j] = inf for any edge with weight 0. This silently corrupted shortest paths through zero-cost edges AND, on graphs with negative edges that resolved to a 0 intermediate, produced wrong final distances. Reproducer: DiGraph with edges (0,1,1),(1,2,1),(0,2,5),(1,3,-2),(3,2,0) — nx returns dist[0,2] = -1 (via 0->1->3->2) but fnx returned 2. Fixed by calling to_numpy_array with nonedge=np.inf and then copying the whole array — weight-0 edges stay finite and negative intermediate paths are preserved.
close_reason: Fixed: nonedge=np.inf in to_numpy_array call, direct array copy. Verified on negative-edge DAG, zero-weight-chain DAG, karate (unweighted), and custom nodelist. All match nx exactly.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] 10+ more signature mismatches on public fnx surface (round 2 sweep)
description:
A second pass of the inspect.signature sweep surfaced more drop-in breakages that the Round 38 pass missed:
- is_simple_path: second positional named 'path' (from the Rust binding) instead of nx's 'nodes'
- is_isolate: second positional named 'node' instead of nx's 'n'
- is_edge_cover: second positional named 'edges' instead of nx's 'cover'
- all_neighbors: first positional named 'G' instead of nx's 'graph'
- to_directed / to_undirected: first positional named 'G' instead of nx's 'graph'
- restricted_view: named 'nodes_to_remove'/'edges_to_remove' instead of nx's 'nodes'/'edges'
- visibility_graph: named 'sequence' instead of nx's 'series'
- mycielskian: missing 'iterations' kwarg — nx supports iterated Mycielskians (chromatic number +k)
- kosaraju_strongly_connected_components: missing 'source' kwarg AND yielded lists instead of sets (nx returns sets — isinstance(s, set) was False on fnx)

All fixed with Python wrappers that accept the nx-named kwargs; kosaraju now coerces each Rust-side component to a set. Mycielskian now iterates the base transformation for ``iterations`` steps.
close_reason: Fixed signatures + return types. Each verified with nx-style kwarg calls; mycielskian iterations matches nx size (|V|=3 * 2^k + 2^(k-1) - 1 recurrence); kosaraju yields set instances; parity tests pass.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] 8 more signature / behaviour mismatches (attribute helpers, graph generators, reconstruct_path)
description:
Continuation of the Round 38/39 signature sweep. These surfaced as TypeError on nx-style kwarg calls:

- k_factor: missing matching_weight kwarg (nx uses it when k=1 to control the max-weight-matching tie-break)
- node_attribute_xy: missing nodes kwarg (source-side filter)
- remove_edge_attributes / remove_node_attributes: wrong signature — fnx took (G, name), nx takes (G, *attr_names, ebunch=None) / (G, *attr_names, nbunch=None). Multi-attr and scoped deletion both broken.
- generate_random_paths: missing source= kwarg (fixed walk start)
- reconstruct_path: signature was (sources, targets, pred); nx is (source, target, predecessors) and `predecessors` is normally the *nested* floyd_warshall dict {src: {tgt: predecessor}} rather than a flat dijkstra-style dict. Old fnx signature produced [] on the nested form.
- partial_duplication_graph: fnx had (n, p, seed); nx has (N, n, p, q, seed, *, create_using). Calling with N=10, n=3, p=0.5, q=0.1 raised TypeError. Rewrote to match nx (clique-seed of size n, grow to N, with both p and q probabilities).

All now accept the nx-named kwargs. reconstruct_path was generalised to handle both nested floyd_warshall dicts and flat dijkstra-style predecessor lists for backwards compat with existing fnx callers.
close_reason: Fixed signatures + behaviour. Verified each fixed function; duplication_divergence_graph kept on the original single-p walk so the (n,p) caller surface doesn't regress; partial_duplication_graph now matches nx (N,n,p,q).

title: REVIEW: [LOW] WL subgraph-hashes test had outdated iterations+1 assertion
description: test_wl_subgraph_hashes_have_correct_length asserted each node's hash list had len == 4 for iterations=3 (comment 'init + 3 iterations'). nx.weisfeiler_lehman_subgraph_hashes returns exactly one hash per iteration (no init entry); fnx's implementation correctly matches that contract. The test was on the pre-3.5 assumption. Updated assertion to 3.
close_reason: Test updated. fnx.weisfeiler_lehman_subgraph_hashes already matched nx (3 hashes for iterations=3, verified against nx.path_graph(5)).

title: REVIEW: [MEDIUM] minimum_cut / minimum_cut_value rejected **kwargs, sedgewick_maze_graph rejected DiGraph create_using, + 3 more signature gaps
description:
Another signature pass found:
- minimum_cut / minimum_cut_value: missed **kwargs. nx's contract is to forward extra kwargs to a user-supplied flow_func and raise NetworkXError('You have to explicitly set a flow_func…') when kwargs are passed without one. fnx raised TypeError instead, giving a confusing error message.
- sedgewick_maze_graph: create_using=nx.DiGraph worked on nx but fnx's _classic_named_graph_from_adjlist blocked directed targets with 'Directed Graph not supported in create_using'.
- kl_connected_subgraph: missing same_as_graph kwarg (when True, return tuple (H, is_same)).
- random_unlabeled_tree: missing number_of_trees kwarg (returns list).
- spectral_graph_forge: missing transformation kwarg ('identity'|'modularity'). nx's modularity transformation was unreachable.

All fixed: minimum_cut now accepts **kwargs and raises nx's NetworkXError; sedgewick_maze_graph builds edges directly via empty_graph(0, create_using) allowing any create_using; kl_connected_subgraph returns (H, ok) tuple when same_as_graph=True; random_unlabeled_tree samples number_of_trees independent trees; spectral_graph_forge validates + applies modularity transformation.
close_reason: Fixed. All five now accept the nx kwargs and produce nx-compatible outputs.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] bfs_beam_edges filtered frontier globally instead of locally + is_kl_connected / kl_connected_subgraph used wrong algorithm
description:
Two behavioural defects in the traversal / hybrid module:

1. bfs_beam_edges: fnx sorted the whole frontier by value and kept the top-width, then visited ALL neighbours of those. nx's algorithm is a LOCAL beam — at each visited node it enqueues only the top-width neighbours (by value descending). On karate_club_graph with degree-valued `value` and width=3, fnx emitted 32 edges, nx emitted 7. Fixed by rewriting over generic_bfs_edges with a per-node successor function returning `sorted(G.neighbors(v), key=value, reverse=True)[:width]`, matching nx exactly (7 edges, identical order).

2. is_kl_connected / kl_connected_subgraph: fnx's implementation tested node-cut properties via combinations over node subsets, which has nothing to do with nx's definition — nx defines (k, l)-local connectivity per EDGE: for each (u, v) there must be l edge-disjoint paths. On karate_club_graph: fnx.is_kl_connected(G, 2, 1) returned False, nx returned True. And fnx.kl_connected_subgraph kept dropping nodes instead of pruning edges, collapsing karate to 2 nodes vs nx's 34. Rewrote both to mirror nx's edge-iteration + edge-disjoint-path algorithm (with optional low_memory neighbourhood restriction).
close_reason: Fixed. bfs_beam_edges exact-matches nx; is_kl_connected matches nx on karate/path/K4 across several (k,l); kl_connected_subgraph matches nx on karate for (2,1) and (3,2); same_as_graph bit also matches.

title: REVIEW: [LOW] caveman_graph(l, 1) returned empty graph instead of l singletons
description: fnx.caveman_graph(l, k) built edges via a nested loop without separately materialising the node set. For k=1 the edge loop produces nothing, so the graph was empty — nx.caveman_graph(1, 1) returns a graph with 1 isolated node, (3, 1) returns 3 isolated nodes. Fixed by calling G.add_nodes_from(range(l*k)) before the edge loop.
close_reason: Fixed. Verified caveman(1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (0,5), (5,0), (3,4), (1,2) all match nx exactly in node/edge count.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] all_pairs_node_connectivity over-reported on directed graphs
description: fnx's all_pairs_node_connectivity dispatches to _fnx.all_pairs_node_connectivity_rust, whose directed-graph path over-counts internally-node-disjoint paths. Reproducer: DiGraph on edges [(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0),(0,2)] — nx.local_node_connectivity(G, 3, 0) correctly returns 1 (only one internally-disjoint path), but the bulk Rust helper put {0:2, 1:2, 2:2} for source 3 (and symmetric overcounts for every source-target pair in this graph). Fixed by delegating the directed branch to networkx; the undirected Rust fast path is retained for Graph / MultiGraph.
close_reason: Fixed: directed inputs delegate to nx.all_pairs_node_connectivity; undirected + multigraph paths still use the Rust helper. Verified that DiGraph, undirected karate_club_graph, and a 4-node MultiGraph all match nx exactly.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] voterank used wrong tie-break order → divergent ranking after top few
description: fnx.voterank delegated to _raw_voterank, whose Rust tie-break ordered ties by a different criterion than networkx. nx uses `max(G.nodes, key=score)` which returns the first-iterated max — on karate_club_graph that means the lowest-labelled tied node wins. Concrete diff: nx returns [33, 0, 32, 2, 1, 5, 31, 23, 6, 3, 24, 29, 4, 8]; fnx returned [33, 0, 32, 2, 1, 31, 5, 23, 6, 3, 24, 29, 10, 8] — positions 5/6 and position 12 differ. Rewrote the Python wrapper over nx's literal algorithm (G.nodes iteration order with max()). Verified: karate full & top5, directed example, single node, empty all match nx exactly.
close_reason: Fixed: voterank now implements nx's algorithm directly so ties break by node iteration order. All known test cases match nx output verbatim.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] dispersion used wrong neighbour-check AND wrong normalisation formula
description:
Two bugs in fnx._dispersion_pair, caught by a karate_club_graph probe (u=0, v=4 returned 0.5 in fnx but 0.0 in nx):

1. Shared-neighbour check: fnx computed `shared_in_common = (s_nbrs & t_nbrs) & common` — restricting the shared neighbour of candidate pair (s, t) to the set of u-and-v common neighbours. nx only requires the shared neighbour to be a neighbour of u: `nbrs_s = u_nbrs ∩ G[s] - {u,v}` then `nbrs_s.isdisjoint(G[t])`. The fnx restriction was too tight, so pairs (s, t) that nx would exclude — because they share a neighbour-of-u that isn't a common neighbour of {u, v} — got counted, inflating dispersion scores.

2. Normalisation: fnx used `(disp + b) / (embeddedness + c) ** alpha` (alpha on denominator), nx uses `(disp + b) ** alpha / (embeddedness + c)` (alpha on numerator). Equivalent only when alpha=1.

Rewrote _dispersion_pair to match nx's Backstrom-Kleinberg algorithm verbatim. Verified full-graph, u=0 vector, single pair, alpha=2, b/c params, and unnormalized all match nx.
close_reason: Fixed. _dispersion_pair is now a literal port of nx's algorithm. All probes on karate_club_graph (dict, u=0, single pair, alpha=2, b/c, normalized=False) match nx exactly.

title: REVIEW: [HIGH] min_edge_cover crashed with fnx matching_algorithm
description: fnx.min_edge_cover delegated to nx when matching_algorithm was supplied, but the delegation wrapper (_call_networkx_for_parity) converts G to an nx.Graph before calling, and then nx calls matching_algorithm(converted_G). If the caller passed a fnx matching function (e.g. fnx.max_weight_matching) it received an nx.Graph and raised TypeError: expected Graph, DiGraph, MultiGraph, or MultiDiGraph. Rewrote min_edge_cover in Python as a literal port of nx's algorithm so the supplied matching_algorithm is called with G directly.
close_reason: Fixed. Verified default path, matching_algorithm=fnx.max_weight_matching, bipartite dict-returning path, and raise-on-directed/multigraph all match nx.

title: REVIEW: [MEDIUM] is_eulerian returned False on single-self-loop graph
description: fnx.is_eulerian forwarded to the Rust _raw_is_eulerian, which returned False for Graph([(0,0)]). nx returns True because a self-loop contributes +2 to degree (even) and the graph is connected — the classic Königsberg criterion is satisfied. Added a Python branch for graphs with <=1 node that walks degrees directly (including self-loop contributions) and returns True when all degrees are even; 2+ node case still uses the Rust fast path. Verified: self-loop-only Graph, empty, K3, P4, two-self-loops MultiGraph, and directed self-loop all match nx.
close_reason: Fixed: Python guard for n<=1 catches the self-loop case; larger graphs unchanged.
